处项目

峨眉山古建筑群

Ancient Building Complex at Mount Emei
国家级 明—清 建筑群 宗教建筑
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address乐山市峨眉山市西南
类型 Type建筑群 宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 山佛教文化 传说 景致

中文描述 Description

四川峨眉山，与山西五台山、安徽九华山、浙江普陀山并成为中国四大佛教名山。

峨眉山风景秀丽，气候宜人，即使在炎热的夏天山里依然能保持20度左右的凉爽温度，山顶由于高海拔更是能积起雪来，让峨眉山成了绝佳的避暑胜地。

峨眉山古建筑群，即指一批修建于峨眉山上明清时期的寺庙古建筑，包括报国寺、伏虎寺、清音阁、洪椿坪、万年寺等。

其中，报国寺、伏虎寺与万年寺为峨眉山三大古寺。

峨眉山自古就是旅游胜地，尤其是在炎热的夏天，不少人选择来到这里避暑。

山里寺庙众多，香火鼎盛，一家人休闲玩耍，到寺庙里上炷香求个平安，是不少游客的最佳选择。

山里潮湿多雨，树林茂密，行走其中虽是爬山却不觉疲惫，尤其还有猴区这样好玩的景点，不少游客慕名而来，就是为了到猴山上去给猴子好好地戏耍一会儿。

峨眉山寺庙众多，每个寺庙都能提供不算昂贵的住宿，所以不赶时间可以慢慢沿着山路往上走，走走停停，日落便找一家寺庙住下，第二天继续攀登。

峨眉山山顶便是著名的金顶，缆车坐到最高处，也需要再走一段路才能到，来了金顶一定要看日出看云海，虽没有什么历史古迹，但是峨眉山壮丽秀美的景色还是能让人不虚此行。

报国寺始建于明万历年间(1573—1620年)，就坐落在峨眉山脚下，是入山的门户，故而这里的游人最多，香火尤甚。

一行人中若有人腿脚不灵便，都会至少来报国寺里烧上一炷香——一来向佛祖表达虔诚；

二来借着古寺盛感的香火，腿脚仿佛也能迅速好起来。

山门匾额上的报国寺三字乃康熙御题，旁边的横匾分别书鹤驻云归普照禅林普放光明，关于匾额的内容还有一段颇有意思的描述。

常住在这附近的一位卖香的老人告诉我，相传报国寺沐浴佛光，在每年特定的一段时间里，清晨朝阳升起时遥望山顶，一瞬间金光穿过林海照耀山寺，整座山全部沐浴在灿烂金黄的佛光之中，此时人置身其中倍感渺小，有缘者便能获得佛祖点化。

故得匾普照禅林普放光明。

而古时寺院以静扬名，是清修的圣地，常有仙鹤飞来，立于檐上，整羽默不作声，故得鹤驻云归之名。

除此之外，报国寺各殿上都悬挂各式匾额，看得出这里自古以来便为帝王将相所钟爱。

报国寺既有佛光普照之恢宏大气，又有野鹤归隐之闲适清幽，也是难得的一个特色吧。

伏虎寺最早是晋代所建的一座小庙，唐代云安禅师重建，旁有龙神堂、药师殿。

宋朝时为神龙堂，明朝被毁，清朝顺治八年(1651年)再次重建，更名虎溪精舍，后因附近虎患，寺僧建尊胜幢以镇压，更名伏虎寺，康熙皇帝曾为伏虎寺题写的离垢园。

寺内建筑有山门、弥勒殿、大雄宝殿、观音殿、客堂、斋堂等。

寺院是典型的汉传佛教建筑风格，是峨眉山最大的一座比丘尼寺院，比丘尼指的是满20岁出家，受了具足戒的女子，也就是俗称的尼姑。

寺院距报国寺仅有一公里，一路广植的桢楠杉柏，还有廊桥小亭构成三桥(虎浴、虎溪、虎啸)二坊(伏虎寺、布金林)之势。

其中，三桥流水潺潺，二坊林木葱茏，行走其中大有密林藏卧虎之感。

一路上会遇见许多学生对着虎溪写生，潺潺水声从虎溪桥下响起，树木掩映又几乎遮住了溪流，让人倍感清凉。

伏虎寺环山临水，建筑纵横交错，布置为四合院。

轴线上从低到高，序列殿宇三重布局，隐没于十万株密林森森之中，隐喻清净无为之意。

据说整个寺院淹没在茂密的树林中，却终年无尘无垢，屋顶积不起落叶，檐下落不上灰尘。

寺内有一处离垢园，匾名为康熙亲笔所写，倒是恰当地概括出了这一神奇的景象。

万年寺是峨眉山的开山第一寺，相传为汉代采药老人蒲公礼佛处。

始建于晋，重建于唐，海拔1020米，有索道和缆车从山脚直达。

所以这里是不少游客选择自上面下游山的起点，同时万年寺再往上便没有很老的古寺了，故它也是不少游客登山而上旅行的终点。

万年寺现存雄伟的山门、弥勒殿、观音殿、般若堂、毗卢殿、无梁殿、巍峨宝殿、大雄宝殿、钟鼓楼、行愿殿，其间还有花园、亭榭、水池等，是一座优雅的园林式的寺院，也是峨眉山最大的寺院。

万年寺中最有名的便是它的无梁砖殿，因其全由砖砌成而得名。

无梁砖殿建于明万历二十八年(1600年)，记载是万历皇帝为母亲祝寿所建，不过导游口中却是某一位得宠的妃嫔求子还愿而建。

不管来由为何，它确实是一个少见的庙宇形制。

金色的无梁砖殿造型像是一个蒙古包，上部是半圆形中空的屋顶，下部为方形底座，殿内供奉着普贤铜像。

佛像高3.64米，趺坐于大象背之莲花座上。

六牙白象四足各踏一莲花蹬。

普贤菩萨遍体贴金，头戴双层金冠，雕饰精巧。

这尊圣寿万年寺铜铁佛像与古建筑一起归为峨眉山古建筑群。

游人绕着铜像走一圈，摸摸象腿感受福缘，象腿已被摸得锃光瓦亮，倒也是一处人文景观。

英文翻译 English Translation

Mount Emei in Sichuan, together with Mount Wutai in Shanxi, Mount Jiuhua in Anhui, and Mount Putuo in Zhejiang, is one of China's Four Great Buddhist Mountains.

Mount Emei has beautiful scenery and a pleasant climate; even in hot summer, the mountain maintains a cool temperature of around 20°C, and the summit, due to high altitude, can even accumulate snow — making Mount Emei an excellent summer retreat.

The Ancient Building Complex at Mount Emei refers to a group of Ming-Qing dynasty temple ancient buildings constructed on Mount Emei, including Baoguo Temple, Fuhu Temple, Qingyin Pavilion, Hongchunping, Wannian Temple, etc.

Among them, Baoguo Temple, Fuhu Temple, and Wannian Temple are the three great ancient temples of Mount Emei.

Mount Emei has been a tourist destination since ancient times, especially in hot summer when many people choose to come here for summer retreat.

There are numerous temples on the mountain with flourishing incense; families relaxing and playing, burning incense at temples for peace — this is the best choice for many tourists.

The mountain is humid and rainy with dense forests; walking through it, though climbing, one does not feel tired.

Especially with fun attractions like the monkey area, many tourists come specifically to play with the monkeys on Monkey Mountain.

There are many temples on Mount Emei, each providing not-too-expensive accommodation, so those not in a hurry can slowly walk up the mountain path, stopping and going; at sunset find a temple to stay, and continue climbing the next day.

The summit of Mount Emei is the famous Golden Summit; taking the cable car to the highest point still requires walking a bit further to reach.

When coming to Golden Summit, one must see the sunrise and sea of clouds; though there are no historical relics, the magnificent and beautiful scenery of Mount Emei still makes the trip worthwhile.

Baoguo Temple was founded during the Ming Wanli era (1573-1620), located at the foot of Mount Emei, serving as the gateway to the mountain — hence it has the most visitors and especially flourishing incense.

If anyone in a group has limited mobility, they will at least come to Baoguo Temple to burn a stick of incense — first to express devotion to the Buddha; second, borrowing the flourishing incense of the ancient temple, one's legs and feet seem to quickly recover.

The three characters "Baoguo Temple" on the mountain gate plaque were personally inscribed by the Kangxi Emperor; the adjacent horizontal plaques read "Crane Stays, Cloud Returns," "Universal Illumination Chan Forest," and "Universal Radiance." There is an interesting story about the plaque content.

An old incense seller living nearby told me that according to legend, Baoguo Temple bathes in Buddha light; during a specific period each year, when the morning sun rises and one gazes at the summit, in an instant golden light pierces the forest sea and illuminates the mountain temple, the entire mountain bathed in brilliant golden Buddha light.

At this moment, one feels tiny within it, and those with karmic affinity can receive the Buddha's enlightenment — hence the plaques "Universal Illumination Chan Forest" and "Universal Radiance." In ancient times, the temple was famous for its tranquility, a holy place for pure cultivation; cranes often flew in, perched on the eaves, preening feathers in silence — hence the name "Crane Stays, Cloud Returns." Besides, various plaques hang on each hall of Baoguo Temple, showing that it has been cherished by emperors and generals since ancient times.

Baoguo Temple has both the grandeur of Buddha light universal illumination and the leisure and seclusion of wild cranes returning to seclusion — a rare combination.

Fuhu Temple was originally a small temple built in Jin dynasty, rebuilt by Master Yun'an in Tang dynasty, with Dragon God Hall and Medicine Master Hall nearby.

In Song dynasty it was called Divine Dragon Hall; destroyed in Ming dynasty, rebuilt again in the 8th year of Shunzhi (1651), Qing dynasty, renamed Huxi Jingshe (Tiger Stream Pure Cottage).

Later due to tiger troubles nearby, monks built a Victory Banner to suppress them, renamed Fuhu (Subduing Tiger) Temple.

The Kangxi Emperor personally inscribed "Ligou Yuan" (Free from Defilement Garden) for Fuhu Temple.

Buildings inside include mountain gate, Maitreya Hall, Mahavira Hall, Guanyin Hall, guest hall, dining hall, etc.

The temple is a typical Han Chinese Buddhist architectural style, and is the largest bhikshuni (nun) temple on Mount Emei — bhikshuni refers to women who have left home at age 20 and received full ordination, commonly called nuns.

The temple is only one kilometer from Baoguo Temple; along the way are extensively planted nanmu, fir, and cypress trees, plus covered bridges and small pavilions forming the pattern of "Three Bridges (Tiger Bath, Tiger Stream, Tiger Roar) and Two Arches (Fuhu Temple, Bujin Forest)." Among them, the three bridges have gurgling flowing water, and the two arches are surrounded by lush trees; walking through gives a strong sense of "dense forest hiding a crouching tiger." Along the way one encounters many students sketching by Tiger Stream; the gurgling sound of water rises from beneath Tiger Stream Bridge, and the trees almost obscure the stream, making one feel especially cool.

Fuhu Temple is surrounded by mountains and water, with buildings crisscrossing, arranged as a siheyuan courtyard.

Along the axis from low to high, three layers of halls are arranged, hidden among 100,000 dense forest trees, metaphorically meaning "purity and non-action." It is said that although the entire temple is submerged in dense forest, it is free from dust and dirt year-round; leaves cannot accumulate on the roofs, and dust cannot fall under the eaves.

Inside the temple there is a "Free from Defilement Garden," with the plaque personally written by Kangxi — aptly summarizing this miraculous phenomenon.

Wannian Temple is the first temple established on Mount Emei; according to legend, it was the place where Pu Gong, an old Han dynasty herb gatherer, worshipped the Buddha.

Founded in Jin dynasty, rebuilt in Tang dynasty, at 1020m elevation, with cable cars and gondolas reaching directly from the foot of the mountain.

Therefore it is the starting point for many tourists choosing to tour the mountain from top to bottom; at the same time, above Wannian Temple there are no very old temples, so it is also the endpoint for many tourists climbing up the mountain.

Wannian Temple currently preserves a majestic mountain gate, Maitreya Hall, Guanyin Hall, Prajna Hall, Vairocana Hall, Beamless Brick Hall, Wei'e Hall, Mahavira Hall, bell and drum towers, and Xingyuan Hall, with gardens, pavilions, and pools in between — an elegant garden-style temple and the largest temple on Mount Emei.

The most famous in Wannian Temple is its Beamless Brick Hall, named because it is entirely built of bricks.

The Beamless Brick Hall was built in the 28th year of Wanli (1600), Ming dynasty; records say it was built by the Wanli Emperor for his mother's birthday, though tour guides say it was built by a favored concubine to fulfill a vow after praying for a son.

Whatever the origin, it is indeed a rare temple form.

The golden Beamless Brick Hall resembles a yurt in shape: the upper part is a semicircular hollow roof, the lower part a square base, and inside enshrines a bronze statue of Samantabhadra.

The statue is 3.64m tall, seated in lotus position on a lotus seat atop an elephant.

The six-tusked white elephant's four feet each step on a lotus pedestal.

Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is covered in gold leaf, wearing a double-layered golden crown, exquisitely carved.

This bronze-iron Buddha statue of Shengshou Wannian Temple, together with the ancient buildings, is classified as the Mount Emei Ancient Building Complex.

Tourists walk around the bronze statue once, touching the elephant legs to feel blessings; the elephant legs have been polished shiny, which is also a cultural landscape.

大庙飞来殿

Feilai Hall (Taoist Temple)
国家级 宋—清 宗教建筑
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty宋—清
地址 Address乐山市峨眉山市大庙乡大庙村
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 大木结构 盘龙柱 彩绘 题记 庙会

中文描述 Description

提及大庙飞来殿，给人的第一印象往往是飞来殿明间前部那两根盘龙柱。

龙身曲折盘绕，雕刻精细，彩绘精美，栩栩如生。

飞来殿俗称大庙，坐落于峨眉山市城郊的飞来岗上。

乘公交到佛光西路的西口，再步行半个多小时即到达。

整个寺庙沿轴线依次为山门、九蟒殿、香殿、飞来殿、凌霄殿(新建)，一旁还有毗卢殿、观音殿。

整座寺庙依山势自下而上修建，气势磅礴。

大庙飞来殿的山门为穿斗式梁架，重檐庑殿顶，建于清代，有清道光十四年(1834年)题记为证。

山门后的九蟒殿位于台基之上，抬梁式歇山顶，重建于明崇祯五年(1632年)。

檐下用五铺作斗拱，檐口两侧微微翘起，沉稳质朴。

殿内房檩上可见历代维修的题记，把建筑的身世讲得一清二楚。

拾级而上，香殿前的台阶边有一棵参天大树，十分茂盛。

香殿为抬梁式歇山顶，檐下用五铺作斗拱。

殿内有元至治二年(1322年)题记，另有明洪武二十四年重修字样，推测始建于元代。

飞来殿是寺庙的大殿，抬梁式歇山顶，金黄色的琉璃瓦使得殿宇更加宏伟(原为小青瓦)。

飞来殿面阔五间，进深四间，采用减柱，使得前部成为三间，使得建筑更具层次感。

明间前的檐柱上有蟠龙，高约半柱，遍施彩绘，十分抢眼。

柱子似乎有明显的侧脚，使得建筑看上去更加稳固结实。

檐下用六铺作斗拱，结构清晰有力。

有趣的是斗拱的上昂如同象鼻一般卷曲，活泼有趣；

下昂则雕成了龙头，威严至极。

殿内原有东岳大帝的铜像，但不幸在大跃进时期被毁。

飞来殿古色古香，气势宏伟，真像从千年之前飞来眼前，将浩荡的历史倾泻。

飞来殿有极为悠久的历史。

唐代时就已在此建有家庆楼，宋代理学家魏鹤山曾为之题写匾额。

宋淳化四年(993年)重修，建东岳庙，供东岳大帝(道教泰山之神)；

元泰定四年(1327年)再次重修，依据飞来殿内铁栓上所刻元大德戊戌年(1298年)，来殿开始供奉佛像，形成佛道共处的格局。

几百年来，大庙每年正月初一到初八举办庙会，特别是初八周围有几万民众前来，祭奠已故亲人，堪称盛况。

英文翻译 English Translation

Mentioning Feilai Hall of the Great Temple, the first impression is often the two dragon-coiled columns at the front of the central bay of Feilai Hall.

The dragon bodies twist and coil, with exquisite carving and beautiful, lifelike colored painting.

Feilai Hall, commonly called the Great Temple, is located on Feilai Hill on the outskirts of Emeishan City.

Take a bus to the west end of Foguang West Road, then walk for over half an hour to arrive.

The entire temple along the axis consists successively of mountain gate, Nine Python Hall, Incense Hall, Feilai Hall, and Lingxiao Hall (newly built), with Pilu Hall and Guanyin Hall on one side.

The whole temple is built from bottom to top following the mountain slope, with imposing momentum.

The mountain gate of the Great Temple Feilai Hall has a chuan-dou frame and double-eave hip roof, built in Qing dynasty, evidenced by an inscription from the 14th year of Daoguang (1834).

The Nine Python Hall behind the mountain gate sits on a platform base, with a post-and-lintel xieshan roof, rebuilt in the 5th year of Chongzhen (1632), Ming dynasty.

Beneath the eaves are five-tier bracket sets, with the eave edges slightly upturned on both sides — steady and simple.

Inscriptions from successive repairs can be seen on the roof beams inside the hall, clearly recounting the building's history.

Climbing up the steps, beside the steps in front of the Incense Hall stands a towering tree, very lush.

The Incense Hall has a post-and-lintel xieshan roof with five-tier bracket sets beneath the eaves.

Inside the hall is an inscription from the 2nd year of Zhizhi (1322), Yuan dynasty, plus characters reading "rebuilt in the 24th year of Hongwu, Ming" —推测 it was founded in Yuan dynasty.

Feilai Hall is the main hall of the temple, with a post-and-lintel xieshan roof; golden glazed tiles make the hall even more magnificent (originally small gray tiles).

Feilai Hall is 5 bays wide, 4 bays deep, using column reduction to make the front part 3 bays, giving the building more layering.

On the eave columns in front of the central bay are coiled dragons, about half a column tall, fully painted — very eye-catching.

The columns seem to have明显侧脚 (inward tilt), making the building appear more stable and solid.

Beneath the eaves are six-tier bracket sets, with clear and powerful structure.

Interestingly, the upper ang (lever arms) of the bracket sets curl like elephant trunks — lively and amusing; the lower ang are carved into dragon heads — extremely majestic.

Originally there was a bronze statue of the Great Emperor of Dongyue inside the hall, but unfortunately it was destroyed during the Great Leap Forward.

Feilai Hall is antique and magnificent, truly as if flying before one's eyes from a thousand years ago, pouring out vast history.

Feilai Hall has an extremely long history.

In Tang dynasty, the Jiaqing Tower was already built here; the Song dynasty Neo-Confucian scholar Wei Heshan once inscribed a plaque for it.

In the 4th year of Chunhua (993), Song dynasty, it was rebuilt as Dongyue Temple, enshrining the Great Emperor of Dongyue (Daoist god of Mount Tai); in the 4th year of Taiding (1327), Yuan dynasty, it was again repaired.

Based on the "Yuan Dade Wuxu year (1298)" engraved on the iron bolts inside Feilai Hall, the hall began to enshrine Buddha statues, forming a pattern of Buddhism and Daoism coexisting.

For hundreds of years, the Great Temple holds a temple fair from the 1st to the 8th day of the first lunar month; especially on the 8th, tens of thousands of people from the surrounding area come to pay respects to deceased relatives — a grand spectacle.

杨公阙

Yanggong Que (Stone-carved Pillar)
国家级 汉—宋 石雕
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty汉—宋
地址 Address乐山市夹江县甘江镇双碑村东南1公里
类型 Type石雕
看点 Highlights: 石作 铭文 浮雕

中文描述 Description

杨公阙地处乡下，不过交通倒是还算畅通，到了村上稍稍一问，便能很快找到。

杨公阙又叫杨府君阙，修建于东汉晚期，重修于南宋。

两阙相距13米，是汉阙常用的红砂石材质，根据材料推断是直接利用当地的石材修筑的墓阙。

据《夹江县志》记载，双阙上有铭文，其一镌汉故益州太守杨府君讳宗字德仲墓道；

另一镌汉故中宫令杨府君讳畅字仲普墓道。

这刻在杨宗与杨畅的墓阙上的碑文由于长年累月的风化，左侧还能勉强从断裂又拼合的阙身上找到依稀的字迹，右阙的碑文就已经完全看不出了。

汉阙上面精美的浮雕一直是重头戏，虽然被风化严重，可是依旧能从残存的雕刻中看到汉朝充满想象力、夸张舒畅的笔法。

汉阙几乎都是石质仿木结构建成的建筑，杨公阙从外观上就明显地分为阙基、阙身、阙楼和阙盖几个部分，下半部刻横梁、斗拱、正檐，上半部浮雕食羊、巨龙腾空、龙虎斗、力士等多幅图案。

尤其是楼上精细的斗拱样的雕刻依然清晰可辨。

石头仿木结构，别说是在当时，就是在现在也是极其精妙的和高难度的，这样的做法其实比较吃力不讨好，但另一方面也正因选取了石材这样能长存的材质，才有可能让今人看到这些珍贵的历史记忆。

汉阙为当代学者研究汉代建筑风格提供了相当好的参考。

相比同在四川的高颐墓阙、樊敏阙，杨公阙显然不及前二者那般保存完好，石材也较前二者劣质，但是它依然完整地保留了汉阙应有的气质和风韵，由于风化严重倒也平添了残阳荒漠汉阙遗世独立的沧桑感。

英文翻译 English Translation

Yanggong Que is located in the countryside, though transportation is fairly accessible; upon arriving at the village, a brief inquiry will quickly lead you to it.

Yanggong Que, also called Yang Fujun Que, was built in the late Eastern Han dynasty and rebuilt in Southern Song.

The two que are 13m apart, made of the red sandstone commonly used for Han que; based on the material, it is inferred that the tomb que was built directly using local stone.

According to the "Jiajiang County Annals," the double que bear inscriptions: one is engraved "Tomb passage of Yang Fujun, named Zong, courtesy name Dezhong, former Governor of Yizhou, Han dynasty"; the other is engraved "Tomb passage of Yang Fujun, named Chang, courtesy name Zhongpu, former Prefect of the Central Palace, Han dynasty." The inscriptions on the tomb que of Yang Zong and Yang Chang, due to long-term weathering, can still be faintly made out on the left que from its broken-and-reassembled body, while the inscription on the right que has completely disappeared.

The exquisite reliefs on Han que have always been the highlight; although severely weathered, one can still see the imaginative, exaggerated, and fluid brushwork of the Han dynasty from the surviving carvings.

Han que are almost all stone buildings imitating timber structures; Yanggong Que is clearly divided externally into que base, que shaft, que tower, and que cap.

The lower part is carved with horizontal beams, bracket sets, and main eaves; the upper part has reliefs of multiple scenes including a feeding sheep, a soaring giant dragon, dragon-tiger fight, and strongmen.

Especially the fine bracket-set-like carvings on the tower are still clearly discernible.

Stone imitating timber structure — not to mention in that era, even now it is extremely exquisite and highly difficult.

This approach is actually quite laborious for little reward, but on the other hand, precisely because stone, a long-lasting material, was chosen, it is possible for people today to see these precious historical memories.

Han que provide quite good reference for contemporary scholars studying Han dynasty architectural styles.

Compared with Gao Yi Tomb Que and Fan Min Que, also in Sichuan, Yanggong Que is obviously not as well preserved as the former two, and its stone is of inferior quality; however, it still completely retains the temperament and charm that a Han que should have.

Due to severe weathering, it even adds the vicissitudes of a Han que standing alone in the world under a setting sun in a desolate desert.

犍为文庙

Temple of Confucius in Jianwei
国家级 清 文庙
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address乐山市犍为县南街
类型 Type文庙
看点 Highlights: 大木结构 轴线 牌坊

中文描述 Description

犍为文庙据称是四川第一大文庙，坐落于犍为县城南街，与东南清代的奎阁、节孝总坊一并构成了所谓一庙、一坊、一阁的古建筑群。

每逢中、高考之时，当地众多学生、家长都会前来祭拜，祈求取得一个好成绩，可见中国文化中对求学的重视。

犍为文庙始建于北宋大中祥符年间(1008—1016年)，历经三迁三建，十二次大修，几经浮沉，览尽沧桑。

现存的文庙应为清康熙九年(1670年)所建，一直修补至宣统三年(1911年)方完工。

文庙坐北朝南，中轴对称，气势恢宏。

自南向北沿中轴依次为万仞宫墙、灵星门、泮池、大成门、燎台、大成殿、启圣宫，贤关、圣域、东庑、西庑分居两侧，布局严谨，层级清晰，称之为犍为故宫。

文庙最南侧为一高墙，约五米，上书万仞宫墙四个大字，遒劲有力，给人以威严的气氛。

高墙围成了一个半圆形，两侧分别开贤关、圣域两门。

进入文庙，即为棂星门，为四柱三间石牌坊，建于明万历年间。

坊上遍布浮雕，各种人物、动物、云彩都雕刻的极为细腻逼真。

柱下设抱鼓石，中间两柱上端雕有蟠龙。

坊上匾额刻有道冠古今、德参天地、金声玉振、江汉秋阳等字样。

如此精美的石牌坊给了来者和文庙都开了一个好头。

越过泮池，就是文庙最具特色的大成门。

大成门为穿斗式梁架，屋顶则将歇山式、悬山式、庑殿牌楼式屋顶结合到了一起，极为独特。

正面屋顶在歇山顶的基础之上，在明间上方设置了庑殿牌楼式屋顶两层，题有天开文运四字，辅之以绿色、金黄色的琉璃瓦，整个建筑因此显得华贵别致，一种治学的严肃敬畏之感油然而生。

大成殿为穿斗式歇山顶，面阔七间，进深五间，黄色瓦顶。

檐下用九踩斗拱，出檐深远。

大成殿雕刻极为精美，撑弓、柱础等处皆有十分出彩的雕刻。

殿内有孔子、四配(颜回、子思、曾子、孟子)与十二哲人像，殿外东西庑立有七十二贤人塑像。

在众多先贤之前，在庄园的大成殿前，万籁俱寂，但似乎耳畔又回响起了琅琅书声，求学之路，从不停息。

英文翻译 English Translation

Jianwei Confucian Temple is said to be the largest Confucian temple in Sichuan, located on South Street of Jianwei County town.

Together with the Qing dynasty Kuige (Pavilion of Literary Prosperity) to the southeast and the Jiexiao Zongfang (General Chastity and Filial Piety Archway), it forms the so-called ancient building complex of "one temple, one archway, one pavilion." Every year during the high school and college entrance exams, many local students and parents come to worship, praying for good grades — showing the importance placed on education in Chinese culture.

Jianwei Confucian Temple was founded during the Northern Song Dazhong Xiangfu era (1008-1016),经历 three relocations and three constructions, twelve major repairs, through many ups and downs, witnessing all vicissitudes.

The existing temple should have been built in the 9th year of Kangxi (1670), Qing dynasty, with repairs continuing until the 3rd year of Xuantong (1911) when it was finally completed.

The temple faces south, with central axis symmetry and imposing momentum.

From south to north along the central axis are successively: Wanren Palace Wall, Lingxing Gate, Pan Pool, Dacheng Gate, Liao Platform, Dacheng Hall, and Qisheng Palace; Xianguan, Shengyu, East Wing, and West Wing are on both sides, with rigorous layout and clear hierarchy — called the "Jianwei Forbidden City." At the southernmost end of the temple is a high wall about 5m tall, inscribed with the four large characters "Wan Ren Gong Qiang" (Ten Thousand Ren Palace Wall), powerful and vigorous, giving a majestic atmosphere.

The high wall forms a semicircle, with the Xianguan and Shengyu gates opening on both sides respectively.

Entering the temple, one reaches the Lingxing Gate, a four-column, three-bay stone archway built during the Ming Wanli era.

The archway is covered with reliefs; various figures, animals, and clouds are carved extremely delicately and realistically.

Under the columns are drum-shaped stone bases, and the upper ends of the two central columns are carved with coiled dragons.

The plaques on the archway are inscribed with characters such as "Dao Crowns Past and Present," "Virtue Matches Heaven and Earth," "Golden Sound and Jade Vibration," and "Jianghan Autumn Sun." Such an exquisite stone archway gives both visitors and the temple a good start.

Crossing the Pan Pool, one reaches the most distinctive Dacheng Gate of the temple.

Dacheng Gate has a chuan-dou frame, and its roof combines xieshan-style, overhanging gable-style, and hip-roof archway-style roofs — extremely unique.

On the basis of the xieshan roof, the front roof sets two layers of hip-roof archway-style roof above the central bay, inscribed with the four characters "Tian Kai Wen Yun" (Heaven Opens Literary Fortune), complemented by green and golden glazed tiles — making the entire building appear luxurious and unique, and a sense of solemn awe for scholarship arises spontaneously.

Dacheng Hall has a chuan-dou xieshan roof, 7 bays wide, 5 bays deep, with a yellow tile roof.

Beneath the eaves are nine-tier bracket sets with deep eaves.

Dacheng Hall has extremely exquisite carvings; the supporting brackets and column bases all have outstanding carvings.

Inside the hall are statues of Confucius, the Four Associates (Yan Hui, Zisi, Zengzi, Mencius), and the Twelve Philosophers; outside the hall, the east and west wings stand with statues of the Seventy-Two Worthies.

Before the numerous sages, in front of the grand Dacheng Hall, all is silent, but it seems the sound of loud reading echoes in one's ears — the path of learning never ceases.

郭沫若故居

Former Residence of Guo Moruo
国家级 清 民居
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address乐山市沙湾区文豪街
类型 Type民居
看点 Highlights: 名人故居 院落 花园

中文描述 Description

走在沙湾的街道上，建筑一例都是仿古的样式，把郭沫若故居掩藏得很好。

郭沫若故居临街为一三开间的瓦房，十分朴素。

明间为正门，上方匾额题有贞寿之门。

左侧次间为郭鸣兴达号商铺，右侧次间现在改为了售票处。

进了郭沫若故居，发现所有房屋就是一样的穿斗式单檐悬山顶，屋面为小青瓦，颇有南方民居的特色。

撑弓雕刻精细，显示了郭家当年的气派。

故居共有三进院落及一后花园，供郭沫若及其家人生活居住。

第三进院落东边为绥山山馆，是郭家的私塾所在，幼时郭沫若即在此学习。

向窗外望去，是宽阔的后花园，风景秀丽。

郭沫若故居现已建成了4A级景区，在后花园后修建了纪念馆。

虽然天空下着微雨，但故居仍然游人如织。

站在天井之中，天色熹微，看着雨滴落在植物青色的叶子之上，有一种烟雨迷蒙的凄美之感。

屋檐下的郭沫若先生的铜像严肃深沉，一个接一个的天井幽深绵延，让这座朴素的建筑似乎有了历史的沧桑与沉重。

英文翻译 English Translation

Walking on the streets of Shawan, the buildings are all in antique style, well concealing the Former Residence of Guo Moruo.

The residence faces the street with a three-bay tile-roofed house, very simple.

The central bay is the main gate, with a plaque above inscribed "Zhen Shou Zhi Men" (Gate of Chastity and Longevity).

The left side bay was the "Guo Ming Xing Da Hao" shop; the right side bay has now been converted into a ticket office.

Entering the Former Residence of Guo Moruo, one finds all houses have the same chuan-dou single-eave overhanging gable roof with small gray tiles — quite characteristic of southern residential architecture.

The supporting brackets are finely carved, showing the Guo family's prestige in those days.

The residence has a total of three courtyards and a rear garden, for Guo Moruo and his family to live in.

To the east of the third courtyard is Suishan Mountain Hall, the Guo family's private school, where the young Guo Moruo studied.

Looking out the window, there is a spacious rear garden with beautiful scenery.

The Former Residence of Guo Moruo has now been developed into a 4A-level scenic area, with a memorial hall built behind the rear garden.

Although the sky is drizzling, the residence is still crowded with visitors.

Standing in the courtyard (tianjing), the sky is dim; watching raindrops fall on the green leaves of plants gives a misty, poignant beauty of rain and mist.

The bronze statue of Mr.

Guo Moruo under the eaves is serious and deep; one courtyard after another stretches deep and long, giving this simple building a sense of historical vicissitudes and weight.

离堆及乌尤寺

Lidui (Wuyou Mountain) and Wuyou Temple
国家级 秦—清 水利建筑、宗教建筑
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty秦—清
地址 Address乐山市市中区城东南1.5公里岷江东岸
类型 Type水利建筑、宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 三江汇流 山势 林木

中文描述 Description

离堆是一座自然形成的圆形小山，当大渡河、青衣江、岷江三江汇流之处。

史料记载李冰当年治理水患时凿离堆，避沫水之害，开凿出的崖疏通水道，使得离堆渐渐与原本的凌云山分离，离堆之名也由此而来。

除开水利工程这一点不谈，离堆本身绿树遮掩，郁郁青青，也不失为一处游玩避暑胜地。

离堆之上筑有乌尤寺，山脚下的门票是与乐山大佛合并一起的通票。

一位在山脚卖香的老奶奶说，大多数人都是从乐山大佛景区的凌云山脚登山，礼完佛顺道逛逛乌尤寺，像我们这一行专程前来乌尤寺的倒是少见。

过了山门沿着石板路一路上行，不出二十分钟便能走到乌尤寺。

乌尤寺始建于唐，原名正觉寺，北宋时改名为乌尤。

坐东向西，依山取势，占地面积3152平方米。

天王殿、弥陀殿、大雄殿、观音殿、罗汉堂等殿宇都建在山头上，寺院周围广植林木，亭台错落，绿树成荫，倒是平添几分清幽与禅意。

我们入寺便立刻笼罩在老和尚不紧不慢念经的经文之中，当时也并非节假日，游人也寥寥，老和尚的诵读在整个寺院里回荡，真是让人从头至脚都被净化了。

乌尤寺的香火基本都被乐山大佛给抢去了，不过它依然给我留下了极其深刻美好的印象。

若是到乐山大佛礼佛后，别忘了留下一些香烛，顺道来下乌尤寺，这座静谧的院子非常适合独自安静地聆听佛经。

英文翻译 English Translation

Lidui is a naturally formed circular small mountain at the confluence of the Dadu River, Qingyi River, and Min River.

Historical records state that when Li Bing controlled floods in ancient times, he chiseled Lidui to avoid the harm of the Mo River (Dadu River); the excavated cliff opened the water channel, causing Lidui to gradually separate from the original Lingyun Mountain — hence the name Lidui (Separated Mound).

Apart from its role as a water conservancy project, Lidui itself is covered with green trees, lush and verdant, making it a fine place for sightseeing and summer retreat.

On top of Lidui stands Wuyou Temple; the ticket at the foot of the mountain is a combined ticket with the Leshan Giant Buddha.

An old woman selling incense at the foot of the mountain said that most people climb from Lingyun Mountain at the Leshan Giant Buddha scenic area, and after worshipping the Buddha, stop by Wuyou Temple; people like our group who come specifically to Wuyou Temple are rare.

Passing the mountain gate and walking up the stone slab path, one reaches Wuyou Temple in less than twenty minutes.

Wuyou Temple was founded in Tang dynasty, originally named Zhengjue Temple, renamed Wuyou in Northern Song.

Facing west from east, following the mountain terrain, it covers 3,152 sq m.

Halls such as the Heavenly Kings Hall, Amitabha Hall, Mahavira Hall, Guanyin Hall, and Arhat Hall are all built on the hilltop; trees are extensively planted around the temple, with pavilions scattered and green shade forming — adding a touch of tranquility and Chan (Zen) meaning.

Upon entering the temple, we were immediately enveloped in the unhurried chanting of an old monk.

It was not a holiday, and there were few visitors; the old monk's chanting echoed throughout the entire temple, truly purifying one from head to toe.

Wuyou Temple's incense has basically been taken away by the Leshan Giant Buddha, but it still left me with an extremely deep and beautiful impression.

If you come to worship at the Leshan Giant Buddha, don't forget to leave some incense and candles and stop by Wuyou Temple — this quiet courtyard is perfect for listening to Buddhist scriptures alone in peace.

嘉州古城墙

Ancient City Wall of Jiazhou
省级 明—清 城墙
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address乐山市市中区滨河路
类型 Type城墙
看点 Highlights: 古城墙 十字交叉拱

中文描述 Description

乐山古名嘉州，为青衣江、大渡河、岷江三江汇流之地，依山傍水，自古为战略要地，修建有城墙。

明时，乐山先后建成临岷江、大渡河的东南段城墙和依高标山的西北段城墙，城墙材料皆取自当地的红砂岩，形成了不规则的城墙轮廓。

清时又在东北修了半圈外城墙，用以抵御陆上进攻，城墙主要仍用红砂岩建造，但上部也采用了青砖。

现存城墙大多为明清遗迹，总长约4公里，主要分布在江边、高标山等地。

刚下过大雨的夏天，伏在江边的古城墙上，石缝间的青苔上还残留着水滴。

听着墙下的大渡河水拍击古城墙，如同江上船只旅人的喧嚣，如同千军万马的怒吼，不过一样地消逝在了这茫茫的江水之中。

本来古城墙的南边往日其实是陆地，但由于大渡河改道，江水直抵城墙，不禁让人出生出沧海桑田之感。

这一段城墙还存有丽正门、会江门两座城门。

丽正门又名铁牛门，城门洞四面均可进入，采用了特别的十字交叉拱，四个门洞的拱券交于一点，结构巧妙独特。

在丽正门恰逢僧人组织放生活动，几十个市民接力着将鱼虾放归大渡河，反映了乐山佛教信仰之虔诚浓厚。

另一城门会江门则隐藏在江边建设银行的家属院的角落里，然而到处的钢架、棚顶显示了它的现状并不乐观，拱券、城墙上的条石都有松动的样子，旁边立着告示：城墙危险，请勿靠近。

时间是残酷的，再高大坚固的城墙也会颓圮，人们早已淡忘了这座城门，我们早已不需要束手束脚的城墙了，这也许就是城市的新陈代谢。

英文翻译 English Translation

Leshan was anciently named Jiazhou, located at the confluence of the Qingyi River, Dadu River, and Min River, nestled between mountains and water — a strategic location since ancient times, with city walls built.

In Ming dynasty, Leshan successively built the southeastern section of the wall facing the Min and Dadu rivers, and the northwestern section following Gaobiao Mountain.

The wall materials were all taken from local red sandstone, forming an irregular wall outline.

In Qing dynasty, another half-circle of outer wall was built in the northeast to resist land attacks; the wall was still mainly built of red sandstone, but blue-gray bricks were also used in the upper part.

Most of the existing wall is Ming-Qing remains, with a total length of about 4km, mainly distributed along the river and at Gaobiao Mountain.

In summer just after heavy rain, leaning on the ancient city wall by the river, water droplets still remain on the moss between the stone crevices.

Listening to the Dadu River below the wall pounding the ancient city wall — like the clamor of travelers on river boats, like the roar of thousands of troops and horses — yet all equally vanished into this vast river water.

Originally the south side of the ancient city wall was actually land in the past, but due to the Dadu River changing course, the river water now reaches directly to the wall, making one feel the vicissitudes of life (the sea turning into mulberry fields).

This section of wall still preserves two city gates: Lizheng Gate and Huijiang Gate.

Lizheng Gate, also called Tieniu (Iron Ox) Gate, can be entered from all four sides of the gate tunnel, using a special cross-shaped intersecting arch where the arch vaults of the four gateways meet at one point — ingenious and unique in structure.

At Lizheng Gate, we happened to encounter monks organizing a life-release activity; dozens of citizens relayed to release fish and shrimp back into the Dadu River, reflecting the devout and strong Buddhist faith in Leshan.

The other gate, Huijiang Gate, is hidden in a corner of the family courtyard of the Construction Bank by the river; however, steel frames and canopy roofs everywhere show its current condition is not optimistic.

The arch vaults and the dressed stones on the wall appear loose, with a notice standing beside: "Dangerous city wall, please do not approach." Time is cruel; even the tallest and sturdiest wall will crumble.

People have long forgotten this city gate; we no longer need walls that bind our hands and feet — perhaps this is the metabolism of a city.

罗城古建筑群

Ancient Building Complex in Luocheng
省级 明—清 城镇
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address乐山市犍为县罗城镇
类型 Type城镇
看点 Highlights: 街道 戏楼 长廊

中文描述 Description

罗城古镇位于犍为县罗城镇内，处在一个小山丘的顶上。

古镇内的遗存建筑始建于明崇祯年间，现主要位于凉厅街一带。

凉厅街平面布局独特，呈现出两头窄中间宽的梭形，形似船只，所以街名又称船形街，罗城古镇也有山顶一只船之名。

自船头走进船形街，街道由窄变宽，勾勒出一个梭形广场。

沿街两边的民居都是穿斗式悬山顶，屋面覆青瓦。

房屋前廊宽大，由一根根圆木的檐柱支撑，房屋间屋顶相接，在街的左右形成了200余米的凉厅。

当地百姓在凉厅中摆设桌椅，经营茶馆。

每天下午，人们闲坐在藤椅上细细品茶，再摆一会儿龙门阵(侃天说地)，或者打打牌，悠闲至极，一幅四川传统的生活图景。

古镇的历史，早融在了一壶壶茶水中，散发出的香气滋养了一个个普通而温馨的日子。

船形街中间是戏楼和石牌坊，均为1985年重建。

船尾是灵官庙，始建于清乾隆十九年(1754年)，正面为正殿，背面为观音殿。

船形街不远处原为南华宫遗址，南华宫毁于大火，现只余石狮一对。

石狮通高4米，据说是乐山最大的石狮，雕刻精湛。

雄狮威武挺拔，脚踩绣球；

雌狮温柔和善，伴一小狮。

门前石狮如此，可以想象旧日南华宫的华美。

但不幸的是南华宫已经被毁，罗城镇内其他古建筑的现状也堪忧。

依稀可见船形街后随意修建的水泥楼房，凉厅下惬意的日子也在被现代文明威胁着。

英文翻译 English Translation

Luocheng Ancient Town is located within Luocheng Town, Qianwei County, on top of a small hill.

The surviving buildings in the ancient town were first built during the Ming Chongzhen era, now mainly located around Liangting Street.

Liangting Street has a unique planar layout,呈现 a spindle shape narrow at both ends and wide in the middle, resembling a boat — hence the street is also called Boat-Shaped Street, and Luocheng Ancient Town has the name "A Boat on the Mountaintop." Entering Boat-Shaped Street from the "bow," the street narrows then widens, outlining a spindle-shaped plaza.

The folk houses on both sides of the street all have chuan-dou overhanging gable roofs covered with gray tiles.

The front verandas of the houses are wide, supported by round timber eave columns; the roofs between houses connect, forming over 200m of covered corridors (liangting) on the left and right of the street.

Local people place tables and chairs in the covered corridors, running teahouses.

Every afternoon, people sit leisurely in rattan chairs sipping tea, chatting (telling stories and gossip), or playing cards — extremely relaxed, a traditional Sichuan lifestyle scene.

The history of the ancient town has long melted into pots of tea, whose fragrance nourishes ordinary but warm days.

In the middle of Boat-Shaped Street are a theater tower and a stone archway, both rebuilt in 1985.

At the "stern" is Lingguan Temple, founded in the 19th year of Qianlong (1754), Qing dynasty, with the main hall on the front and Guanyin Hall on the back.

Not far from Boat-Shaped Street was originally the site of Nanhua Palace; Nanhua Palace was destroyed by fire, now only a pair of stone lions remain.

The stone lions are 4m tall overall, said to be the largest stone lions in Leshan, exquisitely carved.

The male lion is majestic and upright, pawing a silk ball; the female lion is gentle and kind, accompanied by a small lion.

With such stone lions at the gate, one can imagine the splendor of the old Nanhua Palace.

Unfortunately, Nanhua Palace has been destroyed, and the condition of other ancient buildings in Luocheng Town is also worrying.

Cement buildings casually built behind Boat-Shaped Street can be faintly seen, and the comfortable days under the covered corridors are also being threatened by modern civilization.

灵岩寺石牌坊

Stone Memorial Arch of Lingyan Temple
省级 明 宗教建筑
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty明
地址 Address乐山市峨眉山市高桥镇高桥村西南800米高桥中学内
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 石作 雕刻

中文描述 Description

灵岩寺在明代是香火相当鼎盛的寺庙，相传当年此地正是水路要塞，又能从此地的山脚看到峨眉山的金顶，观瞻佛光，因此前来礼佛的善男信女众多，灵岩寺整日都笼罩在袅袅的青烟里。

如今我们一路寻访，高桥镇不过是一个平常甚至有些贫穷的小镇，而曾经繁华的灵岩寺，只剩一方缺角的牌坊了。

石牌坊四柱三间三楼，建于明嘉靖十年(1531年)。

石坊坐南向北，高6.2米，檐下施石质斗拱9朵，现有2朵缺失，枋上与板上均有极其精美的雕刻，麒麟、凤凰、祥云、牡丹等图案清晰可辨。

明间正面刻救口祥林4字，背面刻祗园觉路4字。

牌坊的整体造型雍容典雅，做工精良，让人不禁对之前灵岩寺的盛景充满遐想。

至于为何灵岩寺沦落到此，一说是寺院僧侣常年习武，又得罪了康熙帝，于是康熙下令将这古寺付之一炬；

又有说是反清复明运动时，它沦为两军交战的牺牲品。

真相究竟是怎样我们可能真的无从得知了，只知道这一座安静的石牌坊历经风雨，岿然屹立，仿佛全然不知身后的寺庙早已经灰飞烟灭。

英文翻译 English Translation

Lingyan Temple was a temple with extremely flourishing incense in Ming dynasty.

According to legend, this place was a waterway stronghold at the time, and from the foot of the mountain here one could see the Golden Summit of Mount Emei and observe the Buddha light — hence many devout men and women came to worship, and Lingyan Temple was enveloped in curling blue smoke all day long.

Today, searching all the way, Gaoqiao Town is just an ordinary, even somewhat poor small town, while the once-prosperous Lingyan Temple has only one archway with a missing corner left.

The stone archway has four columns, three bays, and three stories, built in the 10th year of Jiajing (1531), Ming dynasty.

The stone arch faces north from south, 6.2m tall, with 9 stone bracket sets beneath the eaves (2 currently missing).

Both the lintels and panels have extremely exquisite carvings; patterns of qilin, phoenix, auspicious clouds, and peonies are clearly discernible.

The front of the central bay is engraved with the four characters "Jiu Kou Xiang Lin," and the back with "Zhi Yuan Jue Lu." The overall form of the archway is graceful and elegant, with fine workmanship, making one cannot help but imagine the former grand scene of Lingyan Temple.

As for why Lingyan Temple declined to this state, one theory is that the temple monks practiced martial arts year-round and offended the Kangxi Emperor, so Kangxi ordered the ancient temple to be burned to the ground; another theory is that during the "Overthrow Qing, Restore Ming" movement, it became a casualty of battle between two armies.

We may truly never know the truth; we only know that this quiet stone archway has weathered storms and stands firm, as if completely unaware that the temple behind it has long since turned to dust and ashes.

乐山文庙及老霄顶

Temple of Confucius in Leshan and Laoxiaoding
省级 清 文庙
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address乐山市市中区月咡塘街
类型 Type文庙
看点 Highlights: 形制 轴线 古树

中文描述 Description

乐山文庙坐落于高标山下，乐山老城的中心地带，一旁就是乐山二中。

文庙依山而建，建筑分处于五个平面上。

自山下望去，重重殿宇层层升高，气势雄伟。

乐山文庙始建于唐，在明代历经三次搬迁到了今址，后在明末清初毁于战火，现存的文庙主要是清康熙年间重建的。

文庙布局中轴对称，沿轴线依次为泮池、棂星门、大成门、大成殿、崇圣祠，左右有名宦祠、乡贤祠、东西庑殿、尊经阁、崇文阁等。

泮池的水是绿色的，有记载称，前人曾在泮池中栽植莲花，清香四溢。

自桥上经过，便到了棂星门下。

棂星门面阔三间，红砂岩质地，两侧匾额书有德配天地道贯古今，勉励治学之人做到德艺双馨。

每根柱子的抱鼓石上都有石狮，只是由于被风雨侵蚀的缘故略显残破。

棂星门后的大成门于1952年被拆除，现建成的建筑似乎是在模仿大成门的模样，但却有些不伦不类，不能不说是文庙的一处伤疤。

跨过大成门，古树参天，万籁俱寂，幽深宁静，古朴典雅，与文庙外的闹市完全是不同的世界。

文庙似乎已经鲜有人来过了，荒凉而萧瑟。

但大成殿依旧保持着它的威严。

大成殿为抬梁式梁架，单檐歇山顶，黄色琉璃屋面，气势恢宏。

柱子皆用金丝楠木，因而几百年来仍然坚固结实。

大成殿左右的东西庑殿为硬山顶，顶上的封火山墙显得丰富有趣。

院内还有武汉大学西迁的纪念碑。

抗战期间，武大迁至此处办学。

国家危难之关头，武大师生未曾放弃学业。

在这小小的文庙中，求学、救国的心不曾被束缚。

登上乐山文庙后的高标山，山顶便是老霄顶，现存有万寿观、万景楼等建筑，皆为重檐歇山顶。

老霄顶现已成为乐山市民平时休闲之处，万寿观内设有茶桌，还辟出场地供老人们打太极，悠闲而惬意。

登高远眺，山下的乐山文庙金碧辉煌，远处的乐山大佛云雾缭绕，将乐山的文化气息阐释得淋漓尽致。

英文翻译 English Translation

Leshan Confucian Temple is located at the foot of Gaobiao Mountain, in the center of old Leshan city, with Leshan No.

2 Middle School beside it.

The temple is built against the mountain, with buildings distributed on five levels.

Looking up from the foot of the mountain, layers of halls rise step by step, with imposing momentum.

Leshan Confucian Temple was founded in Tang dynasty, relocated three times in Ming dynasty to its current site, then destroyed in war at the end of Ming and beginning of Qing; the existing temple was mainly rebuilt during the Qing Kangxi era.

The temple layout is symmetric along a central axis, with successively: Pan Pool, Lingxing Gate, Dacheng Gate, Dacheng Hall, and Chongsheng Shrine along the axis; on the left and right are Official Virtue Shrine, Local Worthy Shrine, East and West Wing Halls, Zunjing Pavilion, Chongwen Pavilion, etc.

The water in the Pan Pool is green; records say predecessors once planted lotuses in the Pan Pool, with fragrance overflowing.

Crossing the bridge, one arrives at the Lingxing Gate.

Lingxing Gate is 3 bays wide, made of red sandstone; the plaques on both sides read "Virtue Matches Heaven and Earth" and "The Way贯 Through Past and Present," encouraging scholars to achieve both virtue and skill.

On the drum-shaped stone base of each column is a stone lion, though slightly damaged due to wind and rain erosion.

The Dacheng Gate behind Lingxing Gate was demolished in 1952; the currently built building seems to imitate the appearance of Dacheng Gate, but is somewhat nondescript — which must be said to be a scar on the temple.

Crossing Dacheng Gate, ancient trees tower to the sky, all sounds are silent, deep and quiet, simple and elegant — a completely different world from the bustling market outside the temple.

It seems few people have visited the temple recently, desolate and bleak.

But Dacheng Hall still maintains its majesty.

Dacheng Hall has a post-and-lintel frame, single-eave xieshan roof, and yellow glazed tile roof, with imposing grandeur.

The columns are all made of golden silk nanmu (Phoebe zhennan), hence still solid and sturdy after hundreds of years.

The East and West Wing Halls on the left and right of Dacheng Hall have flush gable roofs, with the sealing gable walls on top appearing rich and interesting.

In the courtyard there is also a monument to the westward relocation of Wuhan University.

During the War of Resistance against Japan, Wuhan University moved here to run its school.

At the critical moment of national crisis, the teachers and students of Wuhan University never gave up their studies.

In this small Confucian temple, the hearts of seeking knowledge and saving the nation were never bound.

Climbing Gaobiao Mountain behind Leshan Confucian Temple, at the summit is Laoxiaoding, where buildings such as Wanshou Temple and Wanjing Tower now survive, all with double-eave xieshan roofs.

Laoxiaoding has now become a leisure place for Leshan citizens; Wanshou Temple has tea tables inside, and space has been cleared for elderly people to practice tai chi — relaxed and comfortable.

Climbing high and looking far, the Leshan Confucian Temple below is resplendent and magnificent, and the distant Leshan Giant Buddha is shrouded in clouds and mist — interpreting Leshan's cultural atmosphere to the fullest.

文峰塔

Wenteng Pagoda
省级 明 塔
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty明
地址 Address乐山市犍为县龙孔镇文峰塔山
类型 Type塔
看点 Highlights: 石作 远眺 地形 诗词

中文描述 Description

文峰塔位于犍为县龙孔镇文峰塔山，为明代所建的文峰塔。

塔为八角九级楼阁式砖塔，通高约30米。

塔身各层均开有窗洞，塔檐以砖叠涩挑出，造型挺拔秀丽。

文峰塔坐落于山顶，登临可俯瞰周围山川田园风光。

作为风水塔，文峰塔体现了中国古代建筑中以塔镇风水、振兴文运的传统观念。

英文翻译 English Translation

Wenteng Pagoda is located on Wenteng Pagoda Mountain, Longkong Town, Qianwei County, a pagoda built in Ming dynasty.

It is an octagonal nine-story pavilion-style brick pagoda, about 30m tall overall.

Each story of the pagoda body has window openings, and the eaves are projected by brick corbelling, with an upright and elegant form.

Wenteng Pagoda is situated on the mountaintop; climbing it offers a bird's-eye view of the surrounding mountains, rivers, and rural scenery.

As a feng shui pagoda, Wenteng Pagoda embodies the traditional concept in ancient Chinese architecture of using pagodas to stabilize feng shui and revitalize literary fortune.

REGION

资阳市

睏佛寺摩崖造像

Cliffside Statues of Kunfo Temple
省级 唐—宋 摩崖石刻
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty唐—宋
地址 Address资阳市乐至县回澜镇马锣杨家沟
类型 Type摩崖石刻
看点 Highlights: 造像

中文描述 Description

马锣睏佛寺摩崖造像位于资阳市乐至县回澜镇马锣杨家沟，雕刻于唐末宋初，迄今已有1000多年的历史。

登上一段台阶，经过一片竹林，睏佛寺便映入眼帘。

卧佛便藏身于这个破旧的建筑之中，睏佛寺的寺名是否由此而来呢？

在如此荒郊野岭之中存在着体量如此巨大，雕刻如此精美的卧佛实属罕见。

卧佛造像长10.5米，头长即达2.1米，高鼻梁，眼睛微闭，嘴角翘起，体态浑圆，面容安详，生动地表现出佛祖迁化时的超然神情。

佛祖背后刻有弟子雕塑20尊，皆表现出悲哀、忧郁之情，栩栩如生。

漫长的历史岁月中，石刻佛像历经风风雨雨，许多石像已经风化严重，遭到破坏。

睏佛寺周围的佛像也有很多在文革期间被破坏，而这尊卧佛却保存完好，实属不易。

2013年5月，马锣睏佛寺摩崖造像成为国家级重点文物。

希望这尊大佛能够一直保存完整，让更多人见到这来自古代的宝物。

英文翻译 English Translation

Cliffside Statues of Kunfo Temple are located in Yangjiagou, Maluo, Huilan Town, Lezhi County, Ziyang City, carved in late Tang and early Song, with a history of over 1,000 years.

Climbing a flight of steps and passing through a bamboo grove, Kunfo Temple comes into view.

The reclining Buddha is hidden within this dilapidated building; perhaps the temple name "Kunfo" (Sleeping Buddha Temple) derives from this?

It is truly rare to find a reclining Buddha of such massive size and exquisite carving in such a remote wilderness.

The reclining Buddha statue is 10.5m long, with the head alone reaching 2.1m; it has a high nose bridge, eyes slightly closed, corners of the mouth upturned, a rounded body, and a serene face — vividly expressing the transcendent expression of the Buddha at parinirvana.

Behind the Buddha are carved 20 disciple statues, all expressing sorrow and melancholy, lifelike.

Over the long years of history, the stone-carved Buddha statues have weathered storms; many stone statues have been severely weathered and damaged.

Many Buddha statues around Kunfo Temple were also destroyed during the Cultural Revolution, yet this reclining Buddha has been preserved intact — truly not easy.

In May 2013, the Cliffside Statues of Maluo Kunfo Temple became a National Key Cultural Relic.

It is hoped that this great Buddha can always be preserved intact, allowing more people to see this treasure from ancient times.

圣德寺塔

Pagoda of Shengde Temple
国家级 宋 砖石塔
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty宋
地址 Address资阳市简阳市简城南一公里处
类型 Type砖石塔
看点 Highlights: 宋塔 壁画

中文描述 Description

圣德寺塔位于资阳市简阳市简城镇，为方形十三层砖石塔。

唐朝时期，当地建立了圣德寺，在宋朝时，寺中建起石塔。

现如今，寺庙已经不复存在，只剩下圣德寺塔屹立不倒。

圣德寺白塔属于砖石仿木结构，虽然属于宋朝时期的建筑，但是其方形平面和布局特点在宋代已属少见，颇具唐代遗风，是研究唐宋时期佛塔形式演变轨迹的重要资料。

白塔外形独特，塔在造型上是楼阁式塔，但是整体上看塔身又是密檐式的外轮廓。

同时，塔身第三级的八座小抱厦十分独特，国内罕见。

除了外形之外，在圣德寺塔内部还保存有百余幅佛像壁画，绘画的主要内容是千佛图和佛国胜景。

绘画以传统线描为主，并且在人物面部和云气加以渲染。

绘画用笔简练，颇具唐代遗风，同样是前人给我们留下的珍贵遗产。

此外，圣德寺塔在过去被堪舆家称为文笔，这也被认为是简州文运昌盛，出了几许状元的原因。

由于它悠久的历史，独特的建筑、绘画艺术和丰厚底蕴，圣德寺塔于2006年被列为全国重点文物保护单位。

英文翻译 English Translation

Pagoda of Shengde Temple is located in Jiancheng Town, Jianyang City, Ziyang City.

It is a square thirteen-story brick-stone pagoda.

In Tang dynasty, Shengde Temple was established locally; in Song dynasty, a stone pagoda was built within the temple.

Today, the temple no longer exists, leaving only the Pagoda of Shengde Temple standing tall.

The White Pagoda of Shengde Temple is a brick-stone structure imitating timber construction.

Although it is a Song dynasty building, its square plan and layout characteristics are already rare in Song dynasty, quite reminiscent of Tang dynasty style — important material for studying the evolution of pagoda forms from Tang to Song.

The White Pagoda has a unique exterior: in form it is a pavilion-style pagoda, but overall the pagoda body has the outline of a multi-eaved pagoda.

Meanwhile, the eight small attached halls (baosha) on the third level of the pagoda body are very unique, rare in China.

Besides its exterior, over a hundred Buddha murals are preserved inside the Pagoda of Shengde Temple; the main content of the paintings is the Thousand-Buddha image and scenes of the Buddha realm.

The paintings are mainly traditional line drawings, with rendering added to figures' faces and clouds.

The painting brushwork is concise, quite reminiscent of Tang style — also a precious legacy left by our predecessors.

Additionally, the Pagoda of Shengde Temple was called the "Writing Brush" by feng shui masters in the past, which was also considered the reason for Jianzhou's flourishing literary fortune and producing several zhuangyuan (top scholars).

Due to its long history, unique architecture, painting art, and rich heritage, the Pagoda of Shengde Temple was listed as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit in 2006.

木门寺

Mumen Temple
国家级 明 宗教建筑
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty明
地址 Address资阳市安岳县石鼓乡木门村西北1公里
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 明代木构 石亭 雕刻

中文描述 Description

在安岳城北的石鼓乡木门村，有一座建于明代的古寺，木门寺。

经历数百年风吹雨打，建筑只剩下石牌坊、无际禅师亭、祖师殿、大雄宝殿，其余部分均已毁坏。

无际禅师亭是木门寺最为重要的建筑。

亭为石砌建筑，是仿木结构四方亭，攒尖顶。

亭正中立着无际禅师墓塔，此塔为无际禅师主持建造，以备自己身后之事的。

塔为八角形平面，塔高五层，达4.7米，塔身上刻有无际禅师坐像。

除墓塔外，亭内还立有两处石碑，记载着木门寺的兴建以及无际禅师的生平事迹。

英宗之时，明朝处于乱世之中，无际禅师深为英宗倚重。

故在无际禅师圆寂之后，英宗敕建了无际禅师之塔亭。

这是一座精致的石亭，亭子的柱、枋、房瓦、滴水、椽子等结构均为石头制成，但是做工精美，与木制几乎无异。

全亭只有两扇大门为木料制作，这也是木门寺名称的由来。

为了充分显示塔亭的庄重与珍贵，在石亭之外，又建了一座木制大殿将其覆盖。

殿中建亭，亭中建塔，这种形制，实属罕见，是建筑学者和雕刻艺术家研究、鉴赏的不可多得的宝物。

英文翻译 English Translation

In Mumen Village, Shigu Township, north of Anyue County town, there is an ancient temple built in Ming dynasty — Mumen Temple.

After hundreds of years of wind and rain, only the stone archway, Wuji Chan Master Pavilion, Patriarch Hall, and Mahavira Hall remain; the rest has been destroyed.

The Wuji Chan Master Pavilion is the most important building of Mumen Temple.

The pavilion is a stone-masonry structure, a square pavilion imitating timber construction with a pyramidal roof.

In the center of the pavilion stands the tomb pagoda of Wuji Chan Master; this pagoda was built under the supervision of Wuji Chan Master himself, in preparation for his own passing.

The pagoda has an octagonal plan, five stories tall, reaching 4.7m; the pagoda body is carved with a seated statue of Wuji Chan Master.

Besides the tomb pagoda, two stone steles stand inside the pavilion, recording the construction of Mumen Temple and the life story of Wuji Chan Master.

During the reign of Emperor Yingzong, the Ming dynasty was in troubled times, and Wuji Chan Master was deeply relied upon by Emperor Yingzong.

Therefore, after Wuji Chan Master's parinirvana, Emperor Yingzong ordered the construction of the pagoda pavilion of Wuji Chan Master.

This is an exquisite stone pavilion; the columns, lintels, roof tiles, drip tiles, rafters, and other structural elements are all made of stone, but the workmanship is exquisite, almost indistinguishable from wood.

Only the two main doors of the entire pavilion are made of wood — this is also the origin of the name "Mumen Temple" (Wooden Gate Temple).

To fully demonstrate the solemnity and preciousness of the pagoda pavilion, a timber main hall was built outside the stone pavilion to cover it.

A pavilion built within a hall, a pagoda built within a pavilion — this form is truly rare, a rare treasure for architectural scholars and carving artists to study and appreciate.

卧佛院摩崖造像

Cliffside Statues of Wofo Temple
国家级 唐 摩崖造像
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty唐
地址 Address资阳市安岳县八庙乡卧佛沟
类型 Type摩崖造像
看点 Highlights: 雕刻 卧佛

中文描述 Description

卧佛院摩崖造像位于资阳市安岳县，现如今卧佛院虽已被毁，但卧佛沟两侧精美的石刻还在向我们诉说着盛唐时期的辉煌。

在卧佛沟两侧的崖壁上，唐代的能工巧匠们留下了传世佳作，凿有大大小小龛窟共138个，其中佛像造像84龛，总数量达到1593尊。

在这些佛像之中，最壮观的莫过于释迦牟尼的横卧造像了。

这座卧佛像全长23米，头长3米，肩宽3.1米，侧卧于崖壁之上。

佛像双目微闭，嘴角微微翘起，形体修长，面部圆润，神情安详端庄。

这座雕像用笔精练，寥寥数笔，生动形象地表现出释迦牟尼涅槃时的超脱景象。

除了这座卧佛造像之外，卧佛沟的其他佛像也是精彩绝伦。

卧佛像上部的诸弟子像，个个栩栩如生，呈现出肃穆的神情。

值得一提的是，这里的造像充分利用了视觉因素，造像的上半身总是超出正常比例，这是因为虔诚的信徒们都是匍匐在造像前面，以仰视的视角观之，这个时候造像就呈现为正常的人体比例，十分威武。

卧佛沟不仅有摩崖造像，还有大量宝贵的经书石刻。

在卧佛像对面的崖壁上，就是卧佛院的藏经阁。

崖壁之上，共凿有55个藏经龛窟。

至今保存较为完整的经洞共15个，造字面积达131平方米，皆为大小规格在2~4厘米的端正楷书。

藏经洞内所刻经目包括《大唐东京大敬爱寺一切经论目序》《大般涅槃经》《法华经》《妙法莲华经》《大方便佛报恩经》《般若波罗蜜多心经》《佛名经》《檀三藏经》等共16部，所刻经文不仅字迹工整，更为可贵的是记有确切的年代，是研究佛教文化的重要资料。

英文翻译 English Translation

Cliffside Statues of Wofo Temple are located in Anyue County, Ziyang City.

Although Wofo Temple has now been destroyed, the exquisite stone carvings on both sides of Wofo Valley still tell us of the glory of the High Tang period.

On the cliff walls on both sides of Wofo Valley, skilled Tang dynasty craftsmen left masterpieces handed down through generations, chiseling a total of 138 niches and caves large and small, among which 84 niches contain Buddha statues, with a total count reaching 1,593.

Among these Buddha statues, the most spectacular is none other than the reclining statue of Shakyamuni.

This reclining Buddha statue is 23m long overall, with a 3m head and 3.1m shoulder width, lying on its side on the cliff wall.

The Buddha has eyes slightly closed, corners of the mouth slightly upturned, a slender body, a rounded face, and a serene and dignified expression.

This statue uses concise carving strokes, with just a few strokes vividly expressing the transcendent scene of Shakyamuni at nirvana.

Besides this reclining Buddha statue, the other Buddha statues in Wofo Valley are also superb.

The disciple statues above the reclining Buddha are each lifelike, presenting solemn expressions.

It is worth mentioning that the statues here fully utilize visual factors: the upper body of the statues always exceeds normal proportions, because devout believers all prostrate themselves in front of the statues, viewing from a仰视 perspective — at this time the statues present normal human proportions, very majestic.

Wofo Valley has not only cliffside statues but also a large number of precious scripture stone carvings.

On the cliff wall opposite the reclining Buddha statue is the scripture library of Wofo Temple.

On the cliff wall, a total of 55 scripture-storage niches were chiseled.

To date, 15 scripture caves are relatively well preserved, with a total carved character area of 131 sq m, all in neat regular script of 2-4cm size.

The scripture catalogs carved inside the scripture caves include 16 works such as "Preface to the Catalog of All Sutras and Shastras at Daai Temple in Eastern Capital of Great Tang," "Mahaparinirvana Sutra," "Lotus Sutra," "Wonderful Dharma Lotus Sutra," "Great Expediency Buddha Repayment Sutra," "Prajnaparamita Heart Sutra," "Buddha Name Sutra," and "Sandalwood Three Basket Sutra." The carved scriptures are not only neatly written, but more valuably record exact dates — important material for studying Buddhist culture.

道林寺

Daolin Temple
省级 明 宗教寺庙
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty明
地址 Address资阳市安岳县姚市镇道林村
类型 Type宗教寺庙
看点 Highlights: 形制 轴线 明代木构

中文描述 Description

安岳县姚市镇道林村本是一个平凡的小村落，但却拥有一座家家户户知晓并引以为豪的寺庙——道林寺。

道林寺始建于元代，重修于明永乐年间，它能够保存至今，就不得不提起明代高僧无际禅师了。

永乐五年(1407年)，明成祖朱棣召见全国著名高僧进京讲经说法，无际禅师的谈吐深得朱棣赏识，于是明成祖御赐重修道林寺无际禅师道场。

明清年间，道林寺又经历了数次重修扩建，几经兴废，如今仅存大雄宝殿这一古代建筑了。

道林寺最近重新修缮了一次，建筑焕然一新。

走进道林寺的山门，就看见天王殿。

天王殿是近代修建的建筑，从油漆剥落的情况来看，也有些年代了。

走过天王殿之后，便是重修后的大雄殿了。

大雄殿面阔三间，进深三间，单檐歇山顶形制。

古代的建筑师们独具匠心，在殿内采取抬梁式承重、穿斗式梁架的混合结构。

大雄殿占地面积虽然不大，但是斗拱数量众多，使建筑显得庄重威严，雄伟壮观。

我们和村里人提起附近的古建筑的时候，村里人都指着道林寺的方向，非常自豪地向我们介绍这座古建筑。

相信在村民们的爱护之下，道林寺一定会保存得很好，让更多后人们瞻仰古代工艺之精美。

英文翻译 English Translation

Daolin Village, Yaoshi Town, Anyue County was originally an ordinary small village, but it possesses a temple known to every household and a source of pride — Daolin Temple.

Daolin Temple was founded in Yuan dynasty and rebuilt during the Ming Yongle era.

That it can be preserved to this day must be attributed to the famous Ming dynasty monk Wuji Chan Master.

In the 5th year of Yongle (1407), the Yongle Emperor Zhu Di summoned famous eminent monks from across the country to the capital to preach sutras and expound the Dharma; Wuji Chan Master's eloquence deeply impressed Zhu Di, so the Yongle Emperor bestowed an imperial decree to rebuild the Daolin Temple as the道场 (practice site) of Wuji Chan Master.

During the Ming and Qing dynasties, Daolin Temple underwent several reconstructions and expansions, through many rises and falls; today only the Mahavira Hall, an ancient building, remains.

Daolin Temple was recently renovated once more, and the building looks brand new.

Entering the mountain gate of Daolin Temple, one sees the Heavenly Kings Hall.

The Heavenly Kings Hall is a modern-era building; judging from the peeling paint, it also has some age.

Passing through the Heavenly Kings Hall, one reaches the rebuilt Mahavira Hall.

The Mahavira Hall is 3 bays wide and 3 bays deep, with a single-eave xieshan roof form.

Ancient architects showed ingenuity by adopting a mixed structure of post-and-lintel load-bearing and chuan-dou frame inside the hall.

Although the Mahavira Hall does not occupy a large area, it has numerous bracket sets, making the building appear solemn, majestic, and imposing.

When we mentioned nearby ancient buildings to the villagers, they all pointed in the direction of Daolin Temple and introduced this ancient building to us with great pride.

It is believed that under the villagers' care, Daolin Temple will surely be well preserved, allowing more future generations to admire the exquisite craftsmanship of antiquity.
