曾经是青林口最早的中心半边街如今只剩一溜稀稀拉拉的房子，难得见到一个人影，昔日辉煌已不在。

在道路尽头，是横跨潼江的铁索桥，名永济桥。

曾三次毁于洪灾，因而为了镇水护桥，还修建一座三楼一殿的云楼，名曰锁水寺。

民国十六年(1927年)重建后，又更名为桂林桥。

锁水寺山门右边有一道高4米的巨型石碑。

石碑上书桂林桥三字，刚劲有力，小写有三丰神笔，传说为张三丰所书。

青林口古镇共有五省会馆、五座大型宫殿和五座古戏台。

古镇街道还有一幢别具一格的过街凉亭，每逢夜晚，古镇都会点亮七盏巨大的街灯，亮如白昼。

英文翻译 English Translation

In the small mountain valley southwest of Erlangmiao Town, at the confluence of the Mange River (source of the Tong River) and another small river, Qinglinkou stands quietly against the mountain and beside the water.

Historically, Qinglinkou was once a transportation hub, naturally developing into a commercially prosperous ancient town.

Today's Qinglinkou, although its streets are dilapidated and the stone slab roads appear weathered, from the old houses standing in rows on both sides and the tall timber structures carved with exquisite patterns, one can still see the prosperous appearance of the ancient town once gathering merchants, with numerous guild halls and temples spread around.

The crew of the Journey to the West sequel once filmed two episodes of exterior scenes here, and Qinglinkou Ancient Town rose to fame as a result.

Now on both sides of the ancient street there are some small shops, either restaurants or selling local specialties.

Among them, dried tofu and preserved eggs are particularly famous.

At the end of the new street is the famous Red Army Bridge, originally named Heyi Bridge.

It was the place where the Fourth Front Army of the Red Army forcibly crossed the Jialing River and established the Soviet regime.

A female Red Army soldier surnamed Liu was placed in the home of a silversmith surnamed Yang in the town due to injury, but was unfortunately discovered by the Kuomintang Communist-Clearance Squad.

Under the Kuomintang's severe torture, she would rather die than surrender, and heroically died at the head of Heyi Bridge.

To commemorate this Red Army soldier, people hung a Red Army Bridge plaque on the wind-and-rain tower on the bridge.

Today, the stone-carved slogans on the Red Army Bridge such as Support the Red Army, Resolutely Oppose Imperialism and Resist Japan, and The Red Army is the Savior of the Poor are still clearly visible despite vicissitudes, silently recounting that bloody history to later generations.

The Red Army Bridge connects to the other end of the old street; old houses line up along the nameless small river, making the small town呈 a T-shaped structure.

At the southernmost end of the old street is the Fire God Temple, built during the Qing Guangxu era.

It consists of the Fire God Hall, Wenchang Hall, and Jade Emperor Hall, enshrining the Daoist Jade Emperor, Fire God, and Wenchang Lord, as well as the Buddhist Lord Shakyamuni.

Walking north along the bluestone slab road and turning past an ancient bodhi tree, one reaches Banbian Street (Half Street).

Once the earliest center of Qinglinkou, Banbian Street now only has a sparse row of houses, with rarely a person in sight; its former glory is gone.

At the end of the road is an iron chain bridge spanning the Tong River, named Yongji Bridge.

It was destroyed by floods three times; therefore, to subdue the water and protect the bridge, a cloud tower with three stories and one hall was built, named Suoshui Temple (Water-Locking Temple).

After reconstruction in the 16th year of the Republic (1927), it was renamed Guilin Bridge.

To the right of the Suoshui Temple mountain gate is a giant stone stele 4m high.

On the stele are written the three characters Guilin Bridge, vigorous and powerful, with small writing Sanfeng Divine Brush, legend says written by Zhang Sanfeng.

Qinglinkou Ancient Town has a total of five provincial guild halls, five large palaces, and five ancient theater stages.

The ancient town street also has a unique cross-street pavilion; every night, the ancient town lights up seven huge street lamps, bright as daylight.

文胜普照寺

Puzhao Temple in Wensheng
省级 明—清 宗教寺庙
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address绵阳市江油市文胜乡长坪村东500米
类型 Type宗教寺庙
看点 Highlights: 明代遗构 碑文

中文描述 Description

据记载，文胜普照寺修建于明朝洪武年间，后经明清前后14年的维修加建，成为一座远近闻名的寺院。

文胜普照寺坐东朝西，现存一进四合院。

该寺内除大雄殿为明代建筑外，其余房屋均为清乃至现代所建。

大雄殿为单檐悬山顶，屋顶陡峻，用材硕大，有明代后期风格，是市内遗存较早的木建筑。

此外，文胜普照寺的一个与众不同之处就是它内部收藏的一系列石碑碑文记载了它在一代代人的努力下逐渐发展前进的感人历史。

寺内存有古碑五块，分别是道光四年(1824年)万善同归碑记、道光十四年(1834年)广种福田碑记、道光十四年新修雨廊碑记、咸丰十年(1860年)功德碑记和光绪二十一年(1895年)中元会碑记。

另有当代维修普照寺碑记一通。

将石碑上的故事串联起来，就是普照寺的发展史：住持圆慧培补了大雄宝殿、文昌殿和两廊，后来再次化缘培补了寺庙、塑造了神像；

住持法林化缘培补了寺庙，新修了东西两廊，几年后又化缘新塑三尊大佛，为罗汉穿金。

住持超凡兴办了一次中元会。

看过这些你会恍然惊叹，这样一座幽深的小院凝聚了那么多先辈的心血。

英文翻译 English Translation

According to records, Wensheng Puzhao Temple was built during the Ming Hongwu era, and after 14 years of maintenance and expansion before and after the Ming-Qing period, it became a well-known temple near and far.

Wensheng Puzhao Temple faces west from east, with one existing siheyuan courtyard.

Inside the temple, except for the Mahavira Hall which is a Ming dynasty building, the other houses were built in Qing or even modern times.

The Mahavira Hall has a single-eave overhanging gable roof, with a steep roof and large timber materials, having a late Ming style; it is an earlier surviving timber building in the city.

In addition, a distinctive feature of Wensheng Puzhao Temple is that a series of stone stele inscriptions collected inside record its touching history of gradual development and progress through the efforts of generations.

There are five ancient steles preserved in the temple: respectively the Wan Shan Tong Gui (All Goodness United) Stele Record of the 4th year of Daoguang (1824), the Guang Zhong Fu Tian (Broadly Planting Blessing Fields) Stele Record of the 14th year of Daoguang (1834), the Newly Built Rain Corridor Stele Record of the 14th year of Daoguang, the Merit Stele Record of the 10th year of Xianfeng (1860), and the Zhongyuan Festival Stele Record of the 21st year of Guangxu (1895).

There is also one contemporary Maintenance of Puzhao Temple Stele Record.

Connecting the stories on the stone steles is the development history of Puzhao Temple: Abbot Yuanhui repaired and supplemented the Mahavira Hall, Wenchang Hall, and two corridors; later he again begged for alms to repair the temple and sculpt deity statues; Abbot Falin begged for alms to repair the temple and newly built the east and west corridors; a few years later he again begged for alms to newly sculpt three Great Buddhas and gild the Arhats.

Abbot Chaofan organized a Zhongyuan Festival once.

After reading these, you will suddenly marvel that such a deep and quiet small courtyard has condensed the efforts of so many predecessors.

河西普照寺

Puzhao Temple in Hexi
省级 明—清 宗教寺庙
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address绵阳市江油市太平镇普照村南5米
类型 Type宗教寺庙
看点 Highlights: 李白 明代木构 修复

中文描述 Description

河西普照寺位于江油市太平镇平通河西岸，这一带汉代文化遗址众多，包括汉台、河西汉代崖墓群等。

普照寺位于江油市城市与青莲镇之间，与云岩寺及太白故居等多个文物景点连成一线，具有重要文物价值。

江油作为诗仙李白曾经居住的地方，自然少不了他四处云游留下的印记。

天台国清寺，天下为四绝。

今到普照游，到来复何别。

楠木白云飞，高僧顶残雪。

门外一条溪，几回流岁月正是他游览普照寺之后留下的诗篇。

作为回应，普照寺山门楹联写道：寺古曾留唐寺迹，楼高恰映汉云台。

另外这里还有李白夜读，神明为李白挂灯，莹莹朗朗，光照十里，故称天灯。

李白别去，天灯即不复发光的神奇传说。

从李白留诗的故事来看，普照寺可能初建于唐代，也可能更早。

如今至少也有1300多年的历史。

时至今日，寺内留存的古建筑仅存大雄宝殿，它建于明代，并留有一些明以前的遗风。

屋面起坡平缓，原为九脊顶，现在九脊已经不复存在。

室内有栩栩如生的彩雕云龙盘踞，精美华丽。

在汶川地震之后，在对这座建筑的修复中专家们最大限度的使用了原有构件，保持了原汁原味。

殿内遗存了不少有年头的古物塑像等，其中的一部分已是残损不全。

比如高约2米、似整木雕刻的一座漆金造像，从其左袖上刀痕看，曾有人破坏性挑开辨真伪。

这样的急功近利，浮躁浅薄不禁令人心痛。

英文翻译 English Translation

Hexi Puzhao Temple is located on the west bank of the Pingtong River, Taiping Town, Jiangyou City.

This area has numerous Han dynasty cultural sites, including the Han Platform and the Hexi Han dynasty cliff tomb group.

Puzhao Temple is located between Jiangyou City and Qinglian Town, forming a line with multiple cultural relic attractions such as Yunyan Temple and the Former Residence of Li Bai, with important cultural relic value.

As the place where the Poet Immortal Li Bai once lived, Jiangyou naturally cannot lack the imprints he left during his travels everywhere.

Tiantai Guoqing Temple, among the four finest under heaven.

Today I visit Puzhao, what difference is there upon arrival.

Nanmu trees and white clouds fly, eminent monks wear remnant snow on their heads.

Outside the gate a stream flows, several times flowing through the years — this is precisely the poem he left after visiting Puzhao Temple.

In response, the couplet on the Puzhao Temple mountain gate reads: The ancient temple once left traces of Tang temples; the tower height precisely reflects the Han Cloud Terrace.

In addition, there is also a magical legend here: Li Bai studied at night, and the deity hung a lamp for Li Bai, bright and clear, illuminating for ten li, hence called Heavenly Lamp.

After Li Bai left, the Heavenly Lamp no longer emitted light.

Judging from the story of Li Bai leaving a poem, Puzhao Temple may have been first built in Tang dynasty, or even earlier.

Today it has at least over 1,300 years of history.

To this day, among the ancient buildings preserved in the temple, only the Mahavira Hall survives; it was built in Ming dynasty and retains some pre-Ming legacy.

The roof slope is gentle, originally a nine-ridge roof, but now the nine ridges no longer exist.

Inside there are lifelike painted carved coiling dragons, exquisite and gorgeous.

After the Wenchuan earthquake, in the restoration of this building, experts maximized the use of original components, maintaining the authentic flavor.

Many aged ancient object statues remain inside the hall, some of which are already damaged and incomplete.

For example, a gilded statue about 2m high, seemingly carved from a single piece of wood; judging from the knife marks on its left sleeve, someone once destructively pried it open to distinguish authenticity.

Such eagerness for quick success and superficiality cannot help but make one heartbroken.

窦圌山云岩寺

Yunyan Temple in Doutuan Mountain
国家级 宋—清 宗教建筑，木结构
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty宋—清
地址 Address绵阳市江油县武都镇圌山村东1.5公里
类型 Type宗教建筑，木结构
看点 Highlights: 飞天藏 山景 修复

中文描述 Description

云岩寺坐落在江油市北25公里窦圌山半山腰上。

相传窦圌山初名圌山，唐朝一位主薄窦子明在此得道成仙，后人便称其为窦圌山。

唐僖宗李儇于乾符年间敕令在窦圌山修建云岩寺，规划分为东西两院，东禅林西道观。

宋代整体改为道观，南宋建造飞天藏。

在明末云岩寺大部分毁于战火，清雍正三年(1725年)又重修各殿。

整座建筑群占地面积约13000平方米，其中建筑面积约4000平方米。

像云岩寺这样建于山脊，背负三座主峰，坐北朝南而又是中轴线对称布局的古寺院建筑群，在全国是罕见的。

寺前山门外有李白赞圌山石碑一通，碑文樵夫与耕者，出入画屏中，则是国民党元老于右任手书镌刻而成。

开车接近窦圌山时，就可以远远看到那里地形的奇特——一片粗糙的巨石突兀地指向天空，这里极具特色的砾岩丹霞地貌和类岩溶景观使得窦圌山成为展示断层等地质现象的国家级地质公园。

主景区三峰鼎立，峰距13~40米，峰顶各有一座古建筑，其间以铁索相连，以奇、险、幽、秀称绝。

而在那里常年都有的铁索飞渡表演，更是为这里增添了一大亮点。

接近云岩寺，可以首先看到一侧位于崖边，视野开敞的飞仙亭。

这就是传说窦子明成仙之地，故于此处重建飞仙亭，辅以一干雕塑和碑刻。

这里是俯瞰远处秀丽风光的好去处。

回归正途，在密林掩映中就是云岩寺的山门。

一入山门首先是一潭碧水，其上古朴的石桥映衬得院落更加幽美。

从山门起依次为：文武殿、天王殿、大雄殿、藏经楼，左右两侧辅有钟鼓楼、东禅堂、飞天藏殿。

其中天王殿为主要的建筑，重建于清雍正十三年，殿前有碑3通。

至于镇山之宝，我国唯一现存的宋代道教木制转轮经藏——飞天藏自然是当之无愧。

这座飞天藏为宋代精细小木作，高10.5米，径7.2米，由藏座、藏身、天宫楼阁及藏楼4个部分组成，顶部为八角攒尖制式。

虽有一定程度的损毁，飞天藏上仍留有木雕人像125尊，斗拱共计24种592朵。

如此历史悠久，规模庞大，结构复杂，雕饰精美的转轮藏实为罕见。

另外由于这里佛道相融的文化底蕴，建筑上时常会出现一些特殊的装饰。

不能不提的是5.12汶川地震给窦圌山、云岩寺带来的巨大损失。

山顶上原建有东岳殿、鲁班殿、窦真殿三座建筑，地震之后东岳殿、窦真殿整体垮塌；

鲁班殿四面墙体垮塌。

而山腰的云岩寺建筑群的每一个建筑也均有不同程度损毁，飞天藏没有受到毁灭性打击可算是不幸中的万幸。

令人印象极为深刻的是对完全坍塌的真武殿的处理，并不是原样重修，而是搭建一个玻璃的歇山顶外壳，在里面放置坍塌的残垣断壁。

这样的设施对后人一定是一种警醒与启示。

英文翻译 English Translation

Yunyan Temple is located on the mountainside of Doutuan Mountain, 25km north of Jiangyou City.

According to legend, Doutuan Mountain was originally named Tuan Mountain; a Tang dynasty registrar named Dou Ziming attained immortality here, and later generations called it Doutuan Mountain.

Emperor Xizong of Tang, Li Xuan, issued an edict during the Qianfu era to build Yunyan Temple on Doutuan Mountain, planned to be divided into east and west courtyards: east Chan (Buddhist) forest and west Daoist temple.

In Song dynasty the whole was converted to a Daoist temple, and the Feitian Zang (Flying Heaven Revolving Sutra Cabinet) was built in Southern Song.

Most of Yunyan Temple was destroyed by war at the end of Ming, and various halls were rebuilt in the 3rd year of Yongzheng (1725), Qing.

The entire building complex covers about 13,000 sq m, of which the building area is about 4,000 sq m.

Ancient temple building complexes like Yunyan Temple, built on a mountain ridge, backed by three main peaks, facing south with a central-axis symmetric layout, are rare nationwide.

Outside the mountain gate in front of the temple there is a stone stele praising Tuan Mountain by Li Bai; the inscription Woodcutters and plowmen, entering and exiting within painted screens, was handwritten and engraved by Yu Youren, a founding elder of the Kuomintang.

Driving close to Doutuan Mountain, one can see from afar the peculiar terrain — a stretch of rough giant stones abruptly pointing at the sky.

The distinctive conglomerate Danxia landform and karst-like landscape here make Doutuan Mountain a national geological park displaying geological phenomena such as faults.

The main scenic area has three peaks standing together, with peak distances of 13-40m; each peak top has an ancient building, connected by iron chains between them, renowned for its wonder, danger, seclusion, and beauty.

And the iron-chain crossing performances held there year-round add another major highlight.

Approaching Yunyan Temple, one can first see the Feixian (Flying Immortal) Pavilion on one side, located at the cliff edge with an open view.

This is the legendary place where Dou Ziming attained immortality, hence Feixian Pavilion was rebuilt here, supplemented by a group of sculptures and stele carvings.

This is a great place to overlook the beautiful scenery in the distance.

Returning to the proper path, amid dense forest shade is the mountain gate of Yunyan Temple.

Upon entering the mountain gate, first there is a pool of clear water; the ancient stone bridge above it sets off the courtyard to be even more serene and beautiful.

Starting from the mountain gate依次 are: Wenwu Hall, Heavenly Kings Hall, Mahavira Hall, Scripture Library, with bell and drum towers, east Chan hall, and Feitian Zang Hall on the left and right sides.

Among them, the Heavenly Kings Hall is the main building, rebuilt in the 13th year of Yongzheng, Qing, with 3 steles in front of the hall.

As for the town-protecting treasure, the only surviving Song dynasty Daoist timber revolving sutra cabinet in China — Feitian Zang — is naturally well-deserved.

This Feitian Zang is a fine Song dynasty small-timber work, 10.5m high, 7.2m in diameter, consisting of 4 parts: cabinet base, cabinet body, heavenly palace pavilion, and cabinet tower, with an octagonal pyramidal top.

Although damaged to a certain extent, Feitian Zang still retains 125 carved wooden figures, with a total of 24 types and 592 bracket sets.

Such a historically long, large-scale, structurally complex, and exquisitely carved revolving sutra cabinet is truly rare.

In addition, due to the cultural heritage of Buddhism and Daoism merging here, some special decorations often appear on the buildings.

What cannot go unmentioned is the huge loss brought to Doutuan Mountain and Yunyan Temple by the 5.12 Wenchuan earthquake.

Originally there were three buildings on the mountain top: Dongyue Hall, Luban Hall, and Douzhen Hall; after the earthquake, Dongyue Hall and Douzhen Hall completely collapsed; all four walls of Luban Hall collapsed.

And every building of the Yunyan Temple complex on the mountainside also suffered varying degrees of damage; that Feitian Zang did not suffer devastating damage can be considered a blessing in misfortune.

What is extremely impressive is the treatment of the completely collapsed Zhenwu Hall: instead of rebuilding it as original, a glass xieshan-roof shell was erected, with the collapsed ruins placed inside.

Such a facility must be a warning and enlightenment for later generations.

太白故居

Former Residence of Li Bai
省级 清 名人故居
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address绵阳市江油市青莲镇
类型 Type名人故居
看点 Highlights: 李白 诗词

中文描述 Description

来到江油，不容错过的景区一定是太白故里——青莲，我国最伟大的诗人李白生活了24载的地方。

今日，这一区域已经进行了全面的规划与开发，大鹏亭、太白楼、太白碑林等景观更是修建得大气磅礴。

如果想要凭吊诗仙、承沐盛世遗风，走访太白故居正是不二之选。

由于该镇境内有两条盘江支流古号廉泉清溪，所以此地原名清廉，在李白自号青莲居士之后，此地才改名青莲镇，自宋沿用至今，可见当地人民对李白的敬重与对家乡的自豪。

701年，李白出生在青莲镇的陇西院，他5岁开始读书，10岁时已攻读《诗》《书》及诸子百家；

15岁时，李白锋芒已初露，一些诗赋开始得到社会名流的称赞。

他也开始接受道家思想的影响，好剑术，喜任侠。

18~24岁，他在隐居潜心读书的同时游历了江油周边各地。

724年，24岁的李白仗剑去国，辞亲远游踏上征途，自成都下峨眉，然后顺江直下重庆，从此再也没有回到故土青莲。

就是这短短24年内，李白就已经给江油留下了太多故事。

故居内粉竹楼是李白之妹李月圆故居。

相传李月圆和女友张雪娥在楼上吟诗、刺绣，每日梳妆后将脂粉水泼向楼下竹林，竹林被逐渐染成粉色，故称粉竹楼。

读书台位于江油市太平镇让水小匡山山顶，曾有联题于此：书可读于台上；

字应化入库中。

倒笔写天，气贯星斗；

举杯邀月，诗惊鬼神。

在陇西院的门前，还有一尊牧童骑牛的青石雕像，牛身上刻着那首李白少年时的成名作《咏石牛》：此石巍巍活像牛，埋藏是地数千秋。

风吹遍体无毛动，雨打浑身有汗流。

芳草齐眉难入口，牧童扳角不回头。

自来鼻上无绳索，天地为栏夜不收。

以示纪念。

太白故居邻近还有一座太白祠，也是历代人们为凭吊诗仙而建。

除了这些，蜀风堂、名贤祠、李白衣冠墓、磨针溪、洗墨池、李月圆墓等也都有属于它们自己的故事，等待人们前来发掘。

英文翻译 English Translation

Coming to Jiangyou, the scenic spot not to be missed must be Taibai's Hometown — Qinglian, the place where Li Bai, China's greatest poet, lived for 24 years.

Today, this area has undergone comprehensive planning and development; landscapes such as Dapeng Pavilion, Taibai Tower, and Taibai Stele Forest have been built on a grand and majestic scale.

If one wishes to pay homage to the Poet Immortal and bathe in the legacy of a prosperous era, visiting the Former Residence of Li Bai is the perfect choice.

Because within this town there are two tributaries of the Pan River, anciently called Lianquan and Qingxi, this place was originally named Qinglian (Clean and Honest); after Li Bai styled himself Qinglian Jushi (Qinglian Layman), this place was renamed Qinglian Town, used since Song dynasty to this day — showing the local people's respect for Li Bai and pride in their hometown.

In 701, Li Bai was born in Longxi Courtyard of Qinglian Town; he started reading at age 5, and by age 10 had already studied the Book of Songs, Book of History, and various schools of thought; at age 15, Li Bai's talent had begun to show, and some of his poems and rhapsodies began to receive praise from social celebrities.

He also began to accept the influence of Daoist thought, fond of swordsmanship and chivalry.

From ages 18 to 24, while living in seclusion and devoting himself to study, he traveled around various places near Jiangyou.

In 724, at age 24, Li Bai took up his sword and left his country, bidding farewell to relatives to travel far; he went from Chengdu down to Mount Emei, then followed the river straight down to Chongqing, and from then on never returned to his hometown Qinglian.

In just these short 24 years, Li Bai had already left too many stories for Jiangyou.

Inside the residence, Fenzhu Tower (Pink Bamboo Tower) is the former residence of Li Bai's sister Li Yueyuan.

According to legend, Li Yueyuan and her girlfriend Zhang Xue'e recited poems and embroidered upstairs; after daily grooming, they poured their cosmetic powder water toward the bamboo forest downstairs, and the bamboo forest was gradually dyed pink, hence called Fenzhu Tower.

The Reading Platform is located on the summit of Xiaokuang Mountain, Rangshui, Taiping Town, Jiangyou City; there was once a couplet inscribed here: Books can be read on the platform; characters should transform into the warehouse.

Writing upside down at the sky, spirit permeates the stars; raising a cup to invite the moon, poetry startles the spirits.

In front of the gate of Longxi Courtyard, there is also a bluestone statue of a shepherd boy riding an ox; on the ox's body is engraved Li Bai's youthful masterpiece Ode to the Stone Ox: This stone stands majestically exactly like an ox, buried in this land for thousands of autumns.

Wind blows all over its body but no hair moves; rain beats its whole body but sweat flows.

Fragrant grass reaches its eyebrows yet hard to enter its mouth; the shepherd boy pulls its horns but it does not turn back.

Since ancient times there is no rope on its nose; heaven and earth as its pen, it does not return at night.

As a memorial.

Near the Former Residence of Li Bai there is also a Taibai Shrine, also built by people of various dynasties to pay homage to the Poet Immortal.

Besides these, Shufeng Hall, Mingxian Shrine, Li Bai's Clothes-and-Hat Tomb, Mozhen Stream, Ink-Washing Pool, Li Yueyuan's Tomb, etc., all have their own stories, waiting for people to come and discover.

七曲山大庙

Taoist Temple at Qiqu Mountain
国家级 晋—清 宗教庙宇
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty晋—清
地址 Address绵阳市梓潼县文昌镇七曲村
类型 Type宗教庙宇
看点 Highlights: 百尺楼 文昌宫 翠云廊 古柏

中文描述 Description

七曲山大庙的创建是为了纪念晋代的张亚子。

因道家传说中他执掌文昌府事及人间官禄，所以元代封其为文昌帝君，因而此又有文昌宫之称。

其后其中的内容渐杂，儒、佛兼而有之，有启圣祠、天尊殿、关帝殿，也曾做过张献忠的家庙，于是出现概念含混的名称大庙。

庙依山势布局，坐南向北，共有殿堂楼阁23处(元代建筑1处，明代建筑9处，清代建筑13处)。

中轴线上依次为山门、百尺楼、文昌正殿、桂香殿、天尊殿，由低至高逐殿而升。

其他各殿分布在中轴线两侧。

大庙占地面积1.2万平方米，建筑面积6000平方米，保护区面积达21万平方米，内有全国最大的古柏树林，计有古柏2万余株。

中国尚文的历史有北有孔子，南有文昌之说，所以文昌宫、文庙就成为了代代书生科考前必去祭拜的场所。

而梓潼这座七曲山大庙正是这一文化传统的祖庭，所以在很久以前这里就有了宏伟的牌坊。

时至今日，这座古老的庙宇仍旧有令人难以置信的旺盛香火。

一入山门，便看见不同于其他寺庙的高耸阶梯，逆光仰望，只见得顶端香烟袅袅，殿宇依稀，烛火相映，仿佛笼罩在一种超凡脱俗的意境中。

而登临顶端，回首相望，又赫然看到高逾三层，据说可与岳阳楼和黄鹤楼媲美，有西蜀名楼之称的百尺楼(即魁星楼)呈环抱之势环绕在侧，确是气宇不凡。

再向内深入，便是各色殿宇，无不依山而建，引人层层登高；

再向上走一路更是清净许多，只见山坡上古柏森森，遮天蔽日，不少柏树脚下还有祈福领养的标牌，更是让人心生温馨之感。

登到最高处，便是雄踞顶峰、建于明初的天尊殿，这里仍是柏树丛生，却已经没了山下魁星殿等处的人声鼎沸，又是另一番宁谧景象。

大殿亦是处处精雕细琢，气氛神圣。

殿前有一口古井，边上围栏处密密麻麻挂满了祈福的长命锁，有些早已锈迹斑斑，有些则明显是崭新的，小小一处仿佛堆叠了一代代人的祈愿。

行走在这里，会发觉处处充满了人们的祈愿之物，想想如果能与自己在意的人携手许下愿望是这样美好，即使不信宗教的人也会不禁为这份愿景而感动。

或许宗教的本意就是让人心生善意，常怀一颗向往幸福的心。

英文翻译 English Translation

The creation of Qiqu Mountain Great Temple was to commemorate Zhang Yazi of Jin dynasty.

Because in Daoist legend he governed the affairs of Wenchang Prefecture and official ranks in the human world, in Yuan dynasty he was conferred the title of Emperor Wenchang, hence it also has the name Wenchang Palace.

Later its content gradually became mixed, incorporating both Confucianism and Buddhism; there are Qisheng Shrine, Tianzun Hall, Guandi Hall, and it also once served as Zhang Xianzhong's family temple, hence the conceptually ambiguous name Great Temple.

The temple is laid out according to the mountain terrain, facing north, with a total of 23 halls and pavilions (1 Yuan dynasty building, 9 Ming dynasty buildings, 13 Qing dynasty buildings).

On the central axis依次 are the mountain gate, Baichi (Hundred-Foot) Tower, Wenchang Main Hall, Guixiang Hall, and Tianzun Hall, ascending hall by hall from low to high.

The other halls are distributed on both sides of the central axis.

The Great Temple covers 12,000 sq m, with a building area of 6,000 sq m, and a protected area of 210,000 sq m; inside there is the largest ancient cypress forest in China, with over 20,000 ancient cypresses.

In China's history of valuing literature, there is a saying In the north there is Confucius, in the south there is Wenchang; therefore Wenchang Palaces and Confucian temples became the places that generations of scholars must visit to worship before imperial examinations.

And this Qiqu Mountain Great Temple in Zitong is precisely the ancestral court of this cultural tradition, so long ago there were already grand archways here.

To this day, this ancient temple still has an unbelievably flourishing incense.

Upon entering the mountain gate, one sees towering steps different from other temples; looking up against the light, one only sees curling incense smoke at the top, halls faintly visible, candlelight reflecting each other, as if enveloped in a transcendent atmosphere.

And climbing to the top, looking back, one suddenly sees the Baichi Tower (i.e., Kuixing Tower), over three stories high, said to rival Yueyang Tower and Yellow Crane Tower, known as the Famous Tower of Western Shu, surrounding in an embracing gesture on the side — truly extraordinary in bearing.

Going further inward, there are various halls, all built according to the mountain, inviting people to climb layer by layer; going further up the road is even more serene; one only sees ancient cypresses dense on the hillside, blocking the sky and sun; at the foot of many cypresses there are also blessing-adoption signs, making one feel warm.

Climbing to the highest point is the Tianzun Hall, majestically occupying the summit, built in early Ming; here cypresses still grow densely, but the bustle of people at the Kuixing Hall and other places at the foot of the mountain is gone — another scene of tranquility.

The main hall is also exquisitely carved everywhere, with a sacred atmosphere.

In front of the hall there is an ancient well; on the surrounding fence densely hang blessing longevity locks, some already rusted, some obviously brand new — this small place seems to have stacked the wishes of generations.

Walking here, one finds that everywhere is filled with people's wish objects; thinking that if one could make a wish hand in hand with someone one cares about would be so beautiful, even non-religious people cannot help but be moved by this vision.

Perhaps the original intention of religion is to make people kind-hearted, always cherishing a heart yearning for happiness.

李业阙

Li Ye Que
国家级 汉 墓阙、石雕
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty汉
地址 Address绵阳市梓潼县长卿镇南桥村西北500米
类型 Type墓阙、石雕
看点 Highlights: 碑文 形制

中文描述 Description

长卿山下的石马坝有一通红砂石质，用一块整石刻成的石碑，基石长，高0.25米，无装饰；

阙身高2.45米。

正面左上方刻着汉侍御史李公之阙，这八字下方刻着清道光邑令周树棠的《移阙记》。

李业阙在新中国成立后方移至此地，加建亭子和名碑，供桌依旧是简单的木桌。

然而谁能想到这通立于简陋棚屋之中的石阙，竟是现存汉阙中年代最早的，其雕刻艺术价值仅次于平阳府君阙，并且对阙文化的研究具有重要意义。

但是因其结构简单，身、顶无饰，也有李业阙不是阙的争辩，至今尚未定论。

关于李业阙阙主，还有一个令人崇敬的故事。

李业本为汉室官员，王莽取代汉室自立为帝后，不愿同流合污的李业托病辞官还家，闭门谢客，太守刘咸和王莽先后慕名而请其为自己效力，均遭到拒绝；

后来公孙述占据益州自立为王，欲聘李业为博士却再度遭其称病推辞。

恼羞成怒的公孙述以毒酒和官位威逼利诱，但是李业选择了名可成不可毁，身可杀不可辱，饮下毒酒自尽。

潼川滚滚光如练，应共芳名万古流。

正是他为后人留下的一曲关于不屈气节的浩荡长歌。

英文翻译 English Translation

At Shima Dam below Changqing Mountain there is a red sandstone stele, carved from a single整块 stone; the base stone is long, 0.25m high, without decoration; the que (tower) body is 2.45m high.

On the upper left of the front face are engraved the eight characters Que of Lord Li, Palace Censor of Han; below these eight characters is engraved the Record of Moving the Que by Zhou Shutang, county magistrate of Daoguang era, Qing.

Li Ye Que was moved to this place only after the founding of New China, with a pavilion and name stele added; the offering table is still a simple wooden table.

However, who would have thought that this stone que standing in a simple shed is actually the earliest dated among surviving Han dynasty ques; its carving art value is second only to Pingyang Fujun Que, and it has important significance for the study of que culture.

But because its structure is simple, with no decoration on the body and top, there is also a debate that Li Ye Que is not a que, which has not been concluded to this day.

Regarding the owner of Li Ye Que, there is also a revered story.

Li Ye was originally an official of the Han court; after Wang Mang replaced the Han dynasty and declared himself emperor, Li Ye, unwilling to associate with the corrupt, feigned illness and resigned to return home, closing his door to visitors.

Governor Liu Xian and Wang Mang successively, hearing his reputation, invited him to serve them, but both were refused; later Gongsun Shu occupied Yizhou and declared himself king, wanting to hire Li Ye as a scholar but was again refused on grounds of illness.

Enraged, Gongsun Shu used poisoned wine and official position to coerce and entice him, but Li Ye chose that name can be achieved but not destroyed, body can be killed but not humiliated, and drank the poisoned wine to kill himself.

The rolling Tong River shines like silk, should flow with your fragrant name for ten thousand ages.

This is precisely the vast and long song of unyielding integrity he left for later generations.

飞鸣禅院

Feiming Buddhist Temple
省级 清 宗教禅院
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address绵阳市安县桑枣镇红牌村罗浮山
类型 Type宗教禅院
看点 Highlights: 诗词 古柏 香火

中文描述 Description

在安县城西南，有一座风景秀丽的山峦，因其山腰常有云雾缭绕，好似在云雾之中若隐若现浮动不定，故而得名浮山，又名罗浮山，是绵阳一个较为有名的景点。

而飞鸣禅院坐落于罗浮山中部，是绵阳市内规模最大、级别最高的佛教禅宗寺院。

飞鸣禅院初为唐武宗所建，宋时改名祥符观，明永乐年间又更名玉虚观，后经毁建等波折，清代恢复原名寺飞鸣禅院。

今存东岳殿、大佛殿、祖师殿、十王殿及耳房等，均为清代建筑。

所谓禅院与寺院不同，禅院突出的特点是由佛教禅宗派别的禅师们所建，是仅供禅师们参禅悟道修行的场所。

当然，飞鸣禅院后来也成为了信众们前来朝庙敬香的圣地，每逢节日，香客不绝，日集万人。

清代进士李调元在《再游浮山》五言律诗中，曾留下吟咏罗浮山浮山名胜地，一月两停鞭的著名佳句。

我们拜访飞鸣禅院时，一开始误以为飞鸣禅院在罗浮山公园内，于是先进入了罗浮山。

在罗浮山公园内有羌王城、西游记拍摄取景地、比较实惠的小餐厅以及一些游乐设施，整体气氛幽静；

直至爬到山顶我们才意识到飞鸣禅院的入口其实是在山脚下的公园外侧，于是下山去找飞鸣禅院。

飞鸣禅院的山门牌坊一看就是新粉刷的，颜色浓艳；

一进门还有一座惹眼的巨大金色佛像，远远望向远方的空蒙。

再往里走氛围就沉静了许多，既有正殿下经幡飘扬，角亭默然耸立，石兽不怒自威；

也有殿前翠柏森森，雕窗斑驳经年，祈愿的红丝带在树下历数时光流逝……终于觅得些许古刹味道。

英文翻译 English Translation

Southwest of Anxian County town, there is a mountain with beautiful scenery; because its mountainside is often wreathed in clouds and mist, as if floating and uncertain, half-hidden in the clouds and mist, it is named Fushan (Floating Mountain), also known as Luofu Mountain, a relatively famous scenic spot in Mianyang.

And Feiming Buddhist Temple is located in the middle of Luofu Mountain, the largest-scale and highest-level Buddhist Chan temple in Mianyang City.

Feiming Buddhist Temple was originally built by Emperor Wuzong of Tang; in Song it was renamed Xiangfu Temple; in the Ming Yongle era it was renamed Yuxu Temple again; after twists and turns of destruction and reconstruction, in Qing it restored its original name Feiming Buddhist Temple.

Today surviving are Dongyue Hall, Great Buddha Hall, Patriarch Hall, Ten Kings Hall, and side rooms, etc., all Qing dynasty buildings.

The so-called Buddhist temple (chanyuan) differs from a monastery (siyuan); the突出 feature of a chanyuan is that it was built by Chan Buddhist sect masters, a place only for Chan masters to practice meditation and attain enlightenment.

Of course, Feiming Buddhist Temple later also became a sacred place for believers to come to worship and burn incense; every festival, pilgrims are endless, gathering ten thousand people daily.

Qing dynasty jinshi Li Tiaoyuan, in his five-character regulated verse Revisiting Fushan, once left the famous line praising Luofu Mountain: Fushan scenic place, twice in a month I halt my whip.

When we visited Feiming Buddhist Temple, at first we mistakenly thought Feiming Buddhist Temple was inside Luofu Mountain Park, so we first entered Luofu Mountain.

Inside Luofu Mountain Park there are the Qiang King City, Journey to the West filming location, an affordable small restaurant, and some amusement facilities; the overall atmosphere is serene; it was not until climbing to the mountain top that we realized the entrance of Feiming Buddhist Temple is actually outside the park at the foot of the mountain, so we went down the mountain to find Feiming Buddhist Temple.

The mountain gate archway of Feiming Buddhist Temple looks freshly painted at first glance, with rich colors; upon entering there is also an eye-catching huge golden Buddha statue, gazing far into the distant misty sky.

Going further in, the atmosphere becomes much more serene; there are prayer flags fluttering under the main hall, corner pavilions standing silently, stone beasts majestic without anger; also there are verdant cypresses dense in front of the hall, carved windows weathered over the years, red blessing ribbons counting the passage of time under the trees...

finally finding a bit of the flavor of an ancient temple.

平阳府君阙

Pingyang Fujun Que
国家级 东汉 墓阙、石雕
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty东汉
地址 Address绵阳市游仙区一环路东段芙蓉溪畔
类型 Type墓阙、石雕
看点 Highlights: 子母阙 雕刻

中文描述 Description

阙是我国古代的一种建筑，类似于道路两侧的门类示意物，一般立在官庙和墓门之前，用来提示来人已经进入了某个规定的区域。

绵阳有不少汉阙遗存，而屹立在绵阳科技馆新馆前面的这对平阳府君阙建于东汉末年，双阙俱全且均有子母阙，据说是全国汉阙中阙间距最大，保存最完整，阙体最大的。

因其重要历史价值，被列入我国第一批国家级文物保护单位之列。

1939年建筑大师梁思成先生在测绘此阙时依据县志记载将其命名为平阳府君阙，说到这个名字的来历，一种说法是绵阳县志是转抄清代绵州才子李调元书中记载的名称，但是在转抄时将杨误抄作阳，结果这个谬误就沿用至今；

另一个说法是墓阙的主人可能是《三国志·蜀志》里记载的一个叫李福的涪县人，他在延熙三年随大将蒋琬出征汉中时病故，因蜀的国号为汉，李福又是涪县人，归葬涪县称平阳府君完全可能。

平阳府君阙属墓阙，由大小相近的两座子母阙组成，南北相距26.2米。

子母阙均由阙基、阙身、阙盖、阙檐、介石和阙顶六部分组成，左侧母阙高5.14米，子阙高3.34米；

右侧母阙高5.12米，子阙高约3.3米。

阙体由15层略带黄色的青灰色砂石叠砌而成，其间无任何黏结物，严整坚固，显示了高超的石材加工技巧。

平阳府君阙上的浮雕也具有极高的艺术价值，在正面以及各个细部比如斗拱、介石等处密集雕刻了各式富有生机的浮雕。

浮雕内容包括车马出行图、舞乐图、追猪图等精细的大型叙事场面，狮虎、力士、蛟龙、朱雀等生动有力的图腾，两阙原均有铭文，但左阙已残损无法辨认，右阙尚存汉平……君……等字。

梁代时，亦有人毁去原有雕饰，凿刻上佛像题记等内容。

历经了1800余年的风刀霜剑，再加上汶川大地震的无情蹂躏，今日的平阳府君阙已是遍体鳞伤，磨蚀不堪，在脚手架的包裹之下显得格外苍老。

好在今日我们还能依稀分辨出那些雕刻的样子，用以遥想它当年的辉煌。

英文翻译 English Translation

Que is a type of building in ancient China, similar to gate-type markers on both sides of a road, generally erected in front of official temples and tomb gates, used to提示 visitors that they have entered a certain designated area.

Mianyang has many surviving Han dynasty ques; and this pair of Pingyang Fujun Que standing in front of the new Mianyang Science and Technology Museum was built in the late Eastern Han dynasty, with both double ques complete and each having mother-and-child ques; it is said to have the largest que spacing, the most complete preservation, and the largest que body among Han dynasty ques nationwide.

Because of its important historical value, it was listed in China's first batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units.

In 1939, when architectural master Liang Sicheng surveyed and mapped this que, he named it Pingyang Fujun Que based on county gazetteer records.

Regarding the origin of this name, one account is that the Mianyang County Gazetteer transcribed the name recorded in the book of Qing dynasty Mianzhou talent Li Tiaoyuan, but during transcription Yang was mistakenly copied as Yang (different character), and as a result this error has been used to this day; another account is that the owner of the tomb que may have been a Fu County person named Li Fu recorded in Records of the Three Kingdoms: Shu Annals; he died of illness in the 3rd year of Yanxi while accompanying General Jiang Wan on an expedition to Hanzhong; because Shu's state name was Han, and Li Fu was a Fu County person, being buried in Fu County and called Lord Pingyang is entirely possible.

Pingyang Fujun Que is a tomb que, composed of two mother-and-child ques of similar size, 26.2m apart north-south.

Both mother-and-child ques consist of six parts: que base, que body, que cover, que eave, intermediate stone, and que top.

The left mother que is 5.14m high, the child que 3.34m; the right mother que is 5.12m high, the child que about 3.3m.

The que body is built by stacking 15 layers of slightly yellowish blue-grey sandstone, without any adhesive between them, neat and solid, demonstrating superb stone processing skills.

The relief carvings on Pingyang Fujun Que also have extremely high artistic value; on the front face and various details such as bracket sets and intermediate stones, various lively relief carvings are densely engraved.

The relief content includes fine large narrative scenes such as chariot and horse procession, dance and music, and pig-chasing scenes; vivid and powerful totems such as lions and tigers, strongmen, flood dragons, and vermilion birds; both ques originally had inscriptions, but the left que is already damaged and unrecognizable, while the right que still retains characters such as Han Ping...

Jun...

In Liang dynasty, some people also destroyed the original carvings and chiseled Buddha statue inscriptions and other content.

After over 1,800 years of wind and frost, plus the merciless devastation of the Wenchuan earthquake, today's Pingyang Fujun Que is already covered with wounds, eroded and unbearable, looking especially aged under the wrapping of scaffolding.

Fortunately, today we can still vaguely distinguish the appearance of those carvings, to remotely imagine its former glory.

鱼泉寺

Yuquan Temple
国家级 东汉 宗教寺庙
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty东汉
地址 Address绵阳市游仙区徐家镇鱼泉村西南1公里
类型 Type宗教寺庙
看点 Highlights: 建筑格局 斗拱 彩绘

中文描述 Description

鱼泉寺坐落于绵阳市游仙区东宣乡鱼泉村的鱼泉山顶，传说寺有泉池不涸，有鱼游泳自如而得名。

鱼泉寺坐南向北，以两重并列院落组成，现占地面积1399平方米，建筑面积1214平方米。

由于鱼泉山的山梁方向为东西向，正好与古建筑群轴线贯通南北的惯例相悖，所以古人在修建鱼泉寺时采取横向排列布局，南北中轴线上，因地形所限只建了山门和大雄宝殿两重建筑。

西院为寺庙的主体部分，北面是鱼泉寺的山门，下面是山门通道，上为灵官楼。

灵官楼两侧为天王殿，东配殿为地藏或文昌殿，西配殿为观音殿，南为正殿大雄宝殿。

东面由祖师殿、方丈室、僧舍组成，均为清代所建。

鱼泉寺建筑造在层层条石垒砌而成的高台之上。

这样因山就势的布局，为寺院建筑格局的多样性提供了独到的资料。

据载，该寺建筑始建于明正统元年(1436年)，修复于清，至今尚存的明代建筑唯有大雄殿。

殿中柱、梁、枋用材硕大，斗拱保留完好，具有明代建筑特征，前檐上存有大明正统元年题记；

其梁枋、斗拱均遍布彩绘；

这些彩绘的线条、设色等具有浓郁的时代和地方特征，有一定的艺术价值。

此外，前殿、灵官楼、大雄宝殿等建筑上保留的20多幅清代水墨壁画构图讲究，内容丰富，也具有很强的观赏价值。

英文翻译 English Translation

Yuquan Temple is located on the summit of Yuquan Mountain, Yuquan Village, Dongxuan Township, Youxian District, Mianyang City.

Legend says the temple has a spring pool that never dries up, with fish swimming freely, hence the name.

Yuquan Temple faces north, composed of two parallel courtyards; currently it covers 1,399 sq m, with a building area of 1,214 sq m.

Because the ridge direction of Yuquan Mountain is east-west, exactly contrary to the convention of ancient building complexes having axes running north-south, the ancients adopted a horizontal arrangement layout when building Yuquan Temple; on the north-south central axis, limited by the terrain, only two layers of buildings were built: the mountain gate and the Mahavira Hall.

The west courtyard is the main part of the temple; to the north is the mountain gate of Yuquan Temple, below is the mountain gate passage, above is the Lingguan Tower.

On both sides of the Lingguan Tower are the Heavenly Kings Halls; the east side hall is the Ksitigarbha or Wenchang Hall, the west side hall is the Guanyin Hall, and to the south is the main hall, the Mahavira Hall.

The east side consists of the Patriarch Hall, abbot's quarters, and monk quarters, all built in Qing dynasty.

Yuquan Temple buildings are constructed on high platforms built by layering dressed stones.

This layout following the mountain terrain provides unique materials for the diversity of temple building layouts.

According to records, the temple buildings were first built in the 1st year of Zhengtong (1436), Ming, restored in Qing; the only surviving Ming dynasty building to this day is the Mahavira Hall.

The columns, beams, and tie beams in the hall use large materials; the bracket sets are well preserved, with Ming dynasty architectural features; on the front eave there is an inscription from the 1st year of Zhengtong of the Great Ming; its beams, tie beams, and bracket sets are all covered with polychrome paintings; the lines and color application of these paintings have strong era and local characteristics, with certain artistic value.

In addition, the over 20 Qing dynasty ink murals preserved on buildings such as the front hall, Lingguan Tower, and Mahavira Hall have refined compositions and rich content, also with strong ornamental value.

马鞍寺

Ma'an Temple
国家级 清 宗教寺庙
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address绵阳市游仙区刘家镇曾家垭村东北1公里
类型 Type宗教寺庙
看点 Highlights: 乐楼 壁画

中文描述 Description

马鞍寺是一座保存较为完整的儒释道三教合一的寺庙，始建于明正德年间，因战乱毁于明崇祯年间，重建于清康熙十六年(1677年)。

寺庙坐北朝南，建筑面积3100平方米，占地面积6400平方米。

建筑群组严格按照佛教寺庙建筑的格局依中轴线呈纵向并列布局。

马鞍寺的主体建筑包括天王殿、大雄宝殿、观音殿、玉皇殿等，有趣的是这些主体建筑分别建于清康熙、乾隆、道光、同治等时期，分别体现了清中早中晚不同时期的建筑风格与手法。

马鞍寺内藏有十余通石碑以及壁上的壁画都是很珍贵的文物，其中大雄宝殿的彩绘二十四诸天十八罗汉图等都具有很高的艺术价值。

这里独特的水墨壁画更是清新淡雅，脱俗超凡。

此外值得一提的是，马鞍寺的一幢独特的建筑——乐楼。

乐楼又名戏楼、戏台子，在马鞍寺中与寺庙倒座，形成面对殿堂的关系。

这座乐楼面阔三间13米，进深二间12米，高二层4.3米，歇山顶。

建筑以粗壮的石础支撑，以一种轻盈的姿态面向蓝天，在静寂的岁月里，刻下自己鲜活的剪影。

英文翻译 English Translation

Ma'an Temple is a relatively well-preserved temple integrating Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism.

It was first built during the Ming Zhengde era, destroyed by war during the Ming Chongzhen era, and rebuilt in the 16th year of Kangxi (1677), Qing.

The temple faces south, with a building area of 3,100 sq m and a site area of 6,400 sq m.

The building complex strictly follows the layout of Buddhist temple architecture, arranged longitudinally and in parallel along the central axis.

The main buildings of Ma'an Temple include the Heavenly Kings Hall, Mahavira Hall, Guanyin Hall, and Jade Emperor Hall; interestingly, these main buildings were respectively built during the Qing Kangxi, Qianlong, Daoguang, and Tongzhi eras, respectively reflecting the architectural styles and techniques of the early, middle, and late Qing periods.

Ma'an Temple contains over ten stone steles and murals on the walls, all very precious cultural relics; among them, the painted Twenty-Four Devas and Eighteen Arhats in the Mahavira Hall all have high artistic value.

The unique ink murals here are even more fresh and elegant, transcending the mundane.

In addition, it is worth mentioning a unique building of Ma'an Temple — the Music Tower.

The Music Tower, also called the theater tower or stage, is positioned opposite to the temple in Ma'an Temple, forming a relationship facing the hall.

This Music Tower is 3 bays wide (13m), 2 bays deep (12m), two stories high (4.3m), with a xieshan roof.

The building is supported by sturdy stone plinths, facing the blue sky with a light posture, carving its own vivid silhouette in the silent years.

李杜祠

Memorial Hall of Li Bai and Du Fu
省级 清 名人宗祠
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address绵阳市游仙区一环路东段121号
类型 Type名人宗祠
看点 Highlights: 诗仙诗圣同祭的宗祠

中文描述 Description

李杜祠位于芙蓉溪畔、富乐山下依山傍水的宝地。

此处历来是文气汇聚之地：该建筑群始建于唐，当时名为治平书院，唐宝应元年杜甫在此暂居期间，或至芙蓉溪岸边观鱼打渔，或与诗酬答，并留下多篇歌颂绵州风土人物的诗作，并在诗中称此馆舍为左绵公馆。

之后，陆游、唐庚、李调元等文人名士都曾先后到这里寻踪问迹，亦留下许多妙文佳句。

因李白系绵州人，杜甫也曾寓居绵州，都是我国唐代伟大的爱国主义诗人，所以清光绪二十六年(1900年)绵州拔贡吴朝品为纪念李白、杜甫而集资将治平书院改建成今天的李杜祠。

这里是全国唯一一处将李白、杜甫合祠祭祀之地。

李杜祠建筑布局错落有致，采用典型的四川地方建筑手法，将祠宇建筑的庄严与园林建筑的优雅完美融合，是四川地区现存祠堂建筑和园林建筑的代表之作，具有独特的文化内涵。

祠内古建筑有八字型牌门、照壁、仙圣堂、问鱼舫等。

李杜祠内藏品众多，包括李杜祠记古春酣亭记宋绍熙劳军碑等石碑15通以及馆藏碑帖300余件。

不巧的是，我们去探访李杜祠的时候那里正在进行重新整修，只见得巴西第一胜景的屏风后边是满目疮痍，问鱼舫门户紧闭，就连李白杜甫比肩而坐的仙圣堂前，日月同辉的匾额下都放着破旧的草帽和脚手架。

虽然不无遗憾，但我们还是可以在这里依稀想见它过去的风韵，以及未来的神采。

期待着这里未来的样子，我想，我和李杜祠还有个约定。

英文翻译 English Translation

Memorial Hall of Li Bai and Du Fu is located on the treasured land beside Furong Stream and at the foot of Fule Mountain, against the mountain and beside the water.

This place has always been a gathering place for literary spirit: the building complex was first built in Tang, then named Zhiping Academy; in the 1st year of Baoying of Tang, during Du Fu's temporary stay here, he either went to the banks of Furong Stream to watch and catch fish, or exchanged poems in reply, leaving many poems praising the local customs and people of Mianzhou, and calling this residence Zuomian Mansion in his poems.

Later, literati and famous scholars such as Lu You, Tang Geng, and Li Tiaoyuan all successively came here to trace their footsteps, also leaving many wonderful lines and fine sentences.

Because Li Bai was a Mianzhou native and Du Fu also once resided in Mianzhou, both great patriotic poets of Tang dynasty China, in the 26th year of Guangxu (1900), Wu Chaopin, a Mianzhou provincial graduate, raised funds to convert Zhiping Academy into today's Memorial Hall of Li Bai and Du Fu to commemorate Li Bai and Du Fu.

This is the only place in the country where Li Bai and Du Fu are jointly worshipped in one shrine.

The building layout of the Memorial Hall of Li Bai and Du Fu is well-proportioned and orderly, adopting typical Sichuan local architectural techniques, perfectly integrating the solemnity of shrine architecture with the elegance of garden architecture; it is a representative work of surviving shrine and garden architecture in the Sichuan region, with unique cultural connotations.

The ancient buildings in the shrine include the eight-character-style gate, screen wall, Xiansheng Hall, Wenyu Boat, etc.

The Memorial Hall of Li Bai and Du Fu has numerous collections, including 15 stone steles such as Record of the Memorial Hall of Li Bai and Du Fu, Record of the Ancient Spring-Han Pavilion, and Song Shaoxi Labor-Appreciation Stele, as well as over 300 collected rubbings.

Unfortunately, when we went to visit the Memorial Hall of Li Bai and Du Fu, it was undergoing renovation; we only saw that behind the screen of the Finest Scene in Western Brazil was devastation everywhere, the doors of Wenyu Boat were tightly closed, and even in front of the Xiansheng Hall where Li Bai and Du Fu sit side by side, under the plaque of Sun and Moon Shining Together, there were worn straw hats and scaffolding.

Although not without regret, we can still vaguely imagine its past charm and future splendor here.

Looking forward to the future appearance of this place, I think I still have an appointment with the Memorial Hall of Li Bai and Du Fu.

碧水寺摩崖造像

Cliffside Statues of Bishui Temple
国家级 唐—清 宗教造像、石雕
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty唐—清
地址 Address绵阳市游仙区涪江东岸绵山路17号
类型 Type宗教造像、石雕
看点 Highlights: 摩崖造像 山水

中文描述 Description

碧水寺位于绵阳市涪江东岸的碧水岩边、越王楼下。

它的形状很是别致，呈现一个宽仅4米，长逾百米的条带状，沿着涪江铺展开一道秀丽的风景。

在这个狭长的滨江公园里，寺庙与园林完美结合，建筑利用河堤高差依势而建错落有致，寺中有寺、园中套园，楼台亭轩各具风姿。

其中一些景观包括北亭、越王台、环香楼、灵龟洞、碧波亭、碧山亭、碧岩阁、碧潭亭、望江亭、碧水轩等，都恰如其分地点缀着这个公园，使它一步一景，更充满细节，更富有层次。

总体看来，山光水色与人文古迹交相辉映，在这涪江之泮，龟山之下绵延成一幅优美的长卷。

这小小的碧水寺也有其悠久的历史，它始建于唐代，唐宋时期曾称水阁院，因为崖壁上终年泉水流淌、叮咚悦耳。

故民国时期又称作滴水寺。

宋代，僧众信士依碧水崖扩建寺庙，易名碧水寺。

碧水寺历经兴废，清嘉庆年间重修后易为今名，民国以后逐渐倾颓。

而这里的石刻则是由已被设施修建破坏的西岸崖壁上搬运而来，这些精美传神、法相庄严的唐代石刻经历了风雨的洗礼，正向人们诉说着古老的故事。

英文翻译 English Translation

Bishui Temple is located beside Bishui Cliff on the east bank of the Fu River, Mianyang City, below the Yuewang Tower.

Its shape is quite unique, presenting a strip shape only 4m wide and over 100m long, spreading a beautiful scenery along the Fu River.

In this narrow riverside park, the temple and garden are perfectly combined; the buildings are built in a well-proportioned and orderly manner using the height difference of the river embankment, with temples within temples and gardens within gardens; the towers, terraces, pavilions, and verandas each have their own charm.

Some of the landscapes include the North Pavilion, Yuewang Platform, Huanxiang Tower, Linggui Cave, Bibo Pavilion, Bishan Pavilion, Biyan Pavilion, Bitan Pavilion, Wangjiang Pavilion, Bishui Veranda, etc., all appropriately adorning this park, making it a scene with every step, even more full of details and layers.

Overall, mountain light and water color complement each other with cultural and historical relics; along this bank of the Fu River and below Turtle Mountain, they stretch into a beautiful long scroll.

This small Bishui Temple also has its long history; it was first built in Tang dynasty, and was called Shuige Courtyard during Tang-Song period, because spring water flows year-round on the cliff wall, tinkling pleasantly.

Hence in the Republican era it was also called Dripping Temple.

In Song dynasty, monks and believers expanded the temple according to Bishui Cliff, renaming it Bishui Temple.

Bishui Temple experienced rises and falls; after reconstruction during the Qing Jiaqing era it received its current name, and gradually fell into disrepair after the Republican era.

And the stone carvings here were transported from the west bank cliff wall that had been damaged by facility construction; these exquisite, vivid, and solemnly-appearing Tang dynasty stone carvings, having experienced the baptism of wind and rain, are telling ancient stories to the people.

绵阳圣水寺

Shengshui Temple in Mianyang
省级 清 宗教寺庙
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address绵阳市涪城区长虹大道北段357号
类型 Type宗教寺庙
看点 Highlights: 山势 彩塑等 佛像 塔林

中文描述 Description

绵阳圣水寺的历史可以上溯至唐代，至今已经有1300多年历史，堪称川西北历史悠久的古刹之一。

据《绵阳县志》载，寺中壁上原有《圣水龙湫记》摩崖题刻，正处有龙渊，祈雨即应验，所以于此地建造寺庙，唐代称为甘泉，元为阜民泉，明时称圣水。

或许是因为离市中心较近，绵阳市佛学研习中心常在此开展活动，又时常有省内外高僧大德亲临开示，所以圣水寺佛事活动频繁、信众云集，非常难得的保持着宗教氛围。

时至今日，此地仍在不断加建与扩大，并且在向内容更为丰富、功能更为多元的方向发展。

来到圣水寺，远远就看见铺陈了半壁青山的各式建筑。

进得山门，里面还在施工；

只见整座寺庙依山而建，盘桓向上，亭、台、楼、阁、榭错落复杂，各色殿宇包括天王殿、观音殿、伽蓝殿、地藏殿、老和尚纪念堂、观音亭、祖师殿、观音阁、老和尚灵骨塔、钟楼、鼓楼、唱经楼等一应俱全。

令我们目不暇接。

紧邻的罗汉寺也是独具特色：这里有纯白无瑕的塔林，横亘半山的巨大卧佛，有九龙盘桓罗汉肃立的蹬道，还有雕满诸天神佛的长廊……固然这里气势之宏伟超过了其他各处，但说实话走在其中，我感受到的更多的是一种崭新的浮华，难勘的芜乱和未经洗礼的躁动。

时隔半年在网上又看到了那里扩建的新进展，但是，或许，这里更需要的是时光磨砺后留下的沉静。

英文翻译 English Translation

The history of Shengshui Temple in Mianyang can be traced back to Tang dynasty, and to this day it has over 1,300 years of history, truly one of the ancient temples with a long history in northwestern Sichuan.

According to the Mianyang County Annals, on the wall inside the temple there was originally a Cliffside Inscription of Record of the Holy Water Dragon Pool; right at the place there was a dragon abyss, and praying for rain would immediately be verified, hence a temple was built at this place; in Tang it was called Ganquan (Sweet Spring), in Yuan it was Fumin Spring, and in Ming it was called Shengshui (Holy Water).

Perhaps because it is relatively close to the city center, the Mianyang Buddhist Studies Center often carries out activities here, and eminent monks and great virtues from inside and outside the province often come personally to give teachings; therefore Buddhist activities at Shengshui Temple are frequent and believers gather in crowds, very rarely maintaining a religious atmosphere.

To this day, this place is still continuously being added to and expanded, and developing in a direction of richer content and more diverse functions.

Coming to Shengshui Temple, from afar one sees various buildings spread across half the green mountain.

Entering the mountain gate, construction is still ongoing inside; one sees the entire temple built according to the mountain, winding upward, with pavilions, terraces, towers, attics, and verandas in complex variety; various halls including the Heavenly Kings Hall, Guanyin Hall, Garan Hall, Ksitigarbha Hall, Old Monk Memorial Hall, Guanyin Pavilion, Patriarch Hall, Guanyin Pavilion, Old Monk Relic Stupa, Bell Tower, Drum Tower, Sutra-Chanting Tower, etc., are all present — making us dizzy with sights.

The adjacent Arhat Temple is also unique: here there is a pure white and flawless stupa forest, a giant reclining Buddha spanning half the mountain, a stairway with nine dragons coiling and Arhats standing solemnly, and a long corridor carved with all the heavenly deities and Buddhas...

Of course the grandeur of momentum here surpasses other places, but to be honest walking among it, what I felt more was a kind of brand-new ostentation, hard-to-fathom chaos, and untested restlessness.

Half a year later I saw online the new progress of its expansion, but perhaps what this place needs more is the tranquility left behind after the tempering of time.

盐亭文星庙

Wenxing Shrine in Yanting
省级 明—清 宗教寺庙
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address绵阳市盐亭县安家镇鹅溪村西1公里
类型 Type宗教寺庙
看点 Highlights: 斗拱 壁画

中文描述 Description

在距鹅溪古庙300米的地方，有一座后依凤凰山，门对梓江状元桥的文星庙，它又称文星宫孔圣庙。

文星庙由何人、因何故而修建，目前还没有可考的史料记载，目前大致认为其始建于明，清雍正年间(1723—1735年)曾经进行过较为全面的维修。

文星庙最初是由正殿、偏殿、前后殿和厢房组成，为一个四合院落。

至今日，庙内建筑仅剩三间，但还是可以从饱经沧桑的主殿看出它的端庄气势，此殿面阔三间12.3米，进深三间12.5米，抬梁式梁架，歇山顶，檐下有斗拱4朵。

整座大殿端坐于高约2米的基础之上，地基边沿由一块块条石砌筑，四根柱子粗壮有力，不施粉饰，极为古朴。

与柱梁的简朴相比，文星庙的斗拱却极为华丽，卷曲的昂头似菊花怒放，又像龙爪盘曲，令人眼前一亮，也成为独特的研究样本。

此外室内墙壁上在众多今人涂鸦之间还有一幅作于清初的壁画，也是文星庙历史的佐证。

英文翻译 English Translation

At a place 300m from the ancient Exi Temple, there is a Wenxing Shrine backed by Fenghuang (Phoenix) Mountain, with its gate facing the Zhuangyuan Bridge of the Zijiang River; it is also called Wenxing Palace or Confucius Sage Temple.

By whom and for what reason Wenxing Shrine was built, there is currently no verifiable historical record; currently it is generally believed to have been first built in Ming, and underwent relatively comprehensive maintenance during the Qing Yongzheng era (1723-1735).

Wenxing Shrine was originally composed of the main hall, side halls, front and rear halls, and wing rooms, forming a siheyuan courtyard.

To this day, only three rooms of buildings remain in the temple, but one can still see its dignified momentum from the weathered main hall; this hall is 3 bays wide (12.3m), 3 bays deep (12.5m), with a post-and-lintel beam frame, xieshan roof, and 4 bracket sets under the eaves.

The entire main hall sits on a foundation about 2m high; the edge of the foundation is built of dressed stone blocks, and the four columns are sturdy and powerful, without plaster decoration, extremely simple and ancient.

Compared with the simplicity of the columns and beams, the bracket sets of Wenxing Shrine are extremely gorgeous; the curled ang (lever arm) heads are like chrysanthemums in full bloom, and also like coiled dragon claws, catching the eye, and also becoming a unique research sample.

In addition, on the interior walls, among numerous modern graffiti, there is also a mural made in early Qing, also evidence of Wenxing Shrine's history.

花林寺

Hualin Temple
省级 明—清 宗教寺庙
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address绵阳市盐亭县富驿镇火星村三社宗教宗
类型 Type宗教寺庙
看点 Highlights: 大雄宝殿

中文描述 Description

花林寺又名花莲寺，至今遗留的古建筑正是大雄殿，该殿始建于唐代，明万历年间重修，至今已有400多年历史。

自花林寺改为小学校之后，花林寺大雄殿就从里面分离出来，单列为文物保护单位，里面也没有一般寺庙必备的神像等物。

大雄殿面阔三间11.8米，进深一间12米，通高8.2米，悬山顶，抬梁式梁架。

大殿木构粗壮有力，结构清晰、不事装潢，无宝顶和雕梁画栋，以实用为主。

其结构的合理性或许正是它能保存至今的重要因素。

一踏进现今的花林寺山门，首先为白居易纪念堂，内有白居易雕像等，门口有沧桑的石狮雕塑，旁边为史纪碑亭，堂亭后面山崖上有鸟翁洞，碑亭边为正殿观音殿。

要问为什么这里会有白居易纪念堂和鸟翁洞，还要从一个传说讲起。

相传唐代大诗人白居易晚年仕途失意，不能苟同于黑暗的官场，一夜梦见仙人指点他跟随鹦鹉鹩寻找隐居之地，次日果然见到一只奇异鹦鹉，便携家小尾随其寻至绵阳花林，在此觅得世外桃源，组织村民耕田务桑，同建家园。

此地如今尚有白氏岩白村沟等地名，传为白居易后人散落劳作场地。

所以鸟翁洞正是纪念那只鹦鹉的所在。

虽然不知道白居易的故事是否真实，但是唐代天文学家李淳风常来花林会真观夜观天象、上报朝廷却是确有其事。

他曾为此处留诗云：月照郊原绿满川，会真风景不虚传；

宜将抱杖登观斗，仰视银河天外天。

另外，花林寺地处兵家必争之要塞，史载花林历烽烟不息：三国张飞，西晋李特，明末农民革命军八大王张献忠，晚清义和团地方首领、花林人蒲定川等均在这里上演过传奇的故事，并留有相关史迹。

昔日辉煌的花林，今朝精彩仍在继续。

英文翻译 English Translation

Hualin Temple, also known as Hualian Temple, the ancient building surviving to this day is precisely the Mahavira Hall; this hall was first built in Tang dynasty, rebuilt during the Ming Wanli era, and to this day has over 400 years of history.

Since Hualin Temple was converted into a primary school, the Mahavira Hall of Hualin Temple was separated from it, listed separately as a cultural relic protection unit, and inside there are also no deity statues and other objects necessary for a general temple.

The Mahavira Hall is 3 bays wide (11.8m), 1 bay deep (12m), 8.2m total height, with overhanging gable roof and post-and-lintel beam frame.

The timber structure of the main hall is sturdy and powerful, with clear structure, no decoration, no precious top or carved beams and painted pillars, prioritizing practicality.

The rationality of its structure is perhaps precisely the important factor that enabled it to be preserved to this day.

Upon stepping into the current mountain gate of Hualin Temple, first is the Bai Juyi Memorial Hall, containing a Bai Juyi statue, etc.; at the entrance there is a weathered stone lion sculpture; beside it is the Historical Record Stele Pavilion; behind the hall and pavilion on the cliff there is the Bird-Old Man Cave; beside the stele pavilion is the main hall, the Guanyin Hall.

To ask why there is a Bai Juyi Memorial Hall and Bird-Old Man Cave here, one must start from a legend.

According to legend, the great Tang poet Bai Juyi, frustrated in his official career in his later years and unable to conform to the dark officialdom, one night dreamed that an immortal guided him to follow a parrot myna to find a place of seclusion; the next day he indeed saw a strange parrot, and took his family to follow it to Hualin in Mianyang, where he found a paradise beyond the world, organizing villagers to plow fields and tend mulberries, jointly building their home.

This place today still has place names such as Bai's Rock and Bai Village Gully, said to be the scattered work sites of Bai Juyi's descendants.

Therefore the Bird-Old Man Cave is precisely the place commemorating that parrot.

Although it is unknown whether Bai Juyi's story is true, it is indeed a fact that Tang dynasty astronomer Li Chunfeng often came to Hualin Huizhen Temple to observe celestial phenomena at night and report to the court.

He once left a poem for this place: The moon shines on the suburbs, green fills the river plain; Huizhen scenery is not falsely transmitted.

One should take a staff to climb and observe the stars, looking up at the Milky Way beyond the sky.

In addition, Hualin Temple is located at a strategic pass contested by military forces; historical records show Hualin has experienced endless beacon fires: Zhang Fei of Three Kingdoms, Li Te of Western Jin, the Eight Great King Zhang Xianzhong of the late Ming peasant revolutionary army, and the local leader of the late Qing Boxer Rebellion, Hualin native Pu Dingchuan, etc., all staged legendary stories here and left related historical traces.

The formerly glorious Hualin, its splendor continues today.

蓝池庙

Lanchi Shrine
省级 明—清 宗教寺庙
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address绵阳市盐亭县富驿镇火星村三社宗教宗
类型 Type宗教寺庙
看点 Highlights: 明代木构 诗词

中文描述 Description

蓝池庙位于三台县东北30公里的塔山镇蓝池村，庙前有水泥路与塔山镇相通，周边为蓝池村村民聚居点，地处偏僻，游客稀少。

现有资料显示蓝池庙始建于宋代，毁于元代，明初重建，明末再毁，清乾隆年间复修扩建。

同治后人造荒芜，成为潼川府三台县有名的鬼庙。

今存为四合院格局，沿中轴线分布有蓝池、山门、前殿、正殿、后殿，两侧则分布有侧殿、十殿和厢房等。

庙门两侧有两株上千年的古柏，格外引人注目。

现存较有价值的是正殿，又名岱岳殿。

前有垂带式踏道七级，抬梁式木结构，重檐歇山顶，檐下有斗拱28朵。

梁上有大明弘治二年墨书题记。

现在蓝池庙的维护情况不算理想，大部分建筑较为破旧，不算合理的保护性加建使得古建筑格局遭受破坏，没有了僧侣的寺庙亦是早已衰颓失去了宗教气氛。

庙前有一大片农田四时耕作郁郁葱葱，村民在这里来来往往，蓝池庙的历史已经少有人知晓。

另有研究表明，杜甫的一首名作《题玄武禅师屋壁》：何年顾虎头，满壁画沧洲。

赤日石林气，青天江海流。

锡飞常近鹤，杯渡不惊鸥。

似得庐山路，真随惠远游。

很有可能是作于蓝池庙，这无疑将这座古庙的历史渊源再次向前推进至唐代了。

英文翻译 English Translation

Lanchi Shrine is located in Lanchi Village, Tashan Town, 30km northeast of Santai County; in front of the shrine there is a cement road connecting to Tashan Town, surrounded by Lanchi Village residential clusters, located in a remote area with few tourists.

Existing data shows Lanchi Shrine was first built in Song dynasty, destroyed in Yuan, rebuilt in early Ming, destroyed again at the end of Ming, and restored and expanded during the Qing Qianlong era.

After Tongzhi it became desolate, becoming the famous Ghost Temple of Santai County, Tongchuan Prefecture.

Today it survives in a siheyuan layout; along the central axis are distributed Lanchi (Blue Pool), mountain gate, front hall, main hall, and rear hall; on both sides are distributed side halls, Ten Halls, and wing rooms, etc.

On both sides of the temple gate there are two over-thousand-year-old ancient cypresses, particularly eye-catching.

The more valuable surviving building is the main hall, also called Daiyue Hall.

In front there are seven垂带式 steps, with a post-and-lintel timber structure, double-eave xieshan roof, and 28 bracket sets under the eaves.

On the beam there is an ink inscription from the 2nd year of Hongzhi of the Great Ming.

Today the maintenance condition of Lanchi Shrine is not ideal; most buildings are relatively dilapidated, and unreasonable protective additions have caused the ancient building layout to suffer damage; the temple without monks has also long declined and lost its religious atmosphere.

In front of the temple there is a large expanse of farmland cultivated year-round, lush and green; villagers come and go here, and the history of Lanchi Shrine is now rarely known.

Another study shows that a famous work by Du Fu, Inscription on the Wall of Master Xuanwu's Room: In what year did Gu Hutou paint the whole wall with Cangzhou?

The red sun has the qi of stone forests; the blue sky has rivers and seas flowing.

The锡 flying often approaches cranes; the cup crossing does not alarm gulls.

It seems I have found the road to Mount Lu, truly following Huiyuan in travel.

was very likely written at Lanchi Shrine, which undoubtedly pushes the historical origin of this ancient temple forward again to Tang dynasty.

尊胜寺

Zunsheng Temple
国家级 明—清 宗教寺庙
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address绵阳市三台县争胜乡争胜村
类型 Type宗教寺庙
看点 Highlights: 大雄殿 藏经阁 明代木构

中文描述 Description

和大多数饱受风雨之苦，命运起伏坎坷的古建筑一样，尊胜寺始建于南宋嘉泰年间，元初毁于战火，明永乐十三年(1415年)重建；

明末清初战乱再毁，清康熙二十六年(1687年)恢复重建，解放后一度式微，现今在恢复发展的过程中。

现在绵(阳)三(台)公路和绵(阳)遂(宁)高速公路的修建均途经争胜乡，为尊胜寺文物旅游资源的开发利用创造了前所未有的机遇。

尊胜寺现存明清古建筑占地3605平方米，建筑面积934255平方米。

由南而北，依序排列，轴线分明；

其主体建筑依次为伽蓝殿、大雄殿、藏经楼，其中除大雄殿为明代建筑，另两座皆为清代建筑。

寺内存有明碑1通，清碑3通。

寺中藏经楼是珍藏佛教《大藏经》的殿阁，《大藏经》由经、律、论三藏构成，是释迦牟尼及其传人指导弟子修行的理论汇编。

尊胜寺所藏《大藏经》现已移至四川省图书馆等处收藏。

藏经楼由于建在地处河滩，地下水位较高之处，所以建筑对柱础的稳定和立柱的承重、防潮要求较高，故柱础高大，柱径加粗，这种现象在省内古建筑中很少见。

藏经楼建成300多年来，梁柱未出现倾斜、下沉，是古建筑建造因地制宜的典范。

此外，唐宋时期木构建筑形制粗犷，刚劲有力的歇山顶就是很好的体现。

英文翻译 English Translation

Like most ancient buildings that have suffered from wind and rain with ups and downs in fate, Zunsheng Temple was first built during the Southern Song Jiatai era, destroyed by war at the beginning of Yuan, and rebuilt in the 13th year of Yongle (1415), Ming; destroyed again by war at the end of Ming and beginning of Qing, restored and rebuilt in the 26th year of Kangxi (1687), Qing; after liberation it once declined, and is now in the process of recovery and development.

Today, the construction of the Mianyang-Santai Highway and the Mianyang-Suining Expressway both pass through Zhengsheng Township, creating unprecedented opportunities for the development and utilization of Zunsheng Temple's cultural relic tourism resources.

The existing Ming-Qing ancient buildings of Zunsheng Temple cover 3,605 sq m, with a building area of 9,342.55 sq m.

From south to north, arranged in sequence, with a clear axis; its main buildings are依次 the Garan Hall, Mahavira Hall, and Scripture Library; among them, except for the Mahavira Hall which is a Ming dynasty building, the other two are both Qing dynasty buildings.

Inside the temple there is 1 Ming stele and 3 Qing steles preserved.

The Scripture Library in the temple is the hall pavilion for treasuring the Buddhist Tripitaka; the Tripitaka consists of the three collections of Sutras, Vinaya, and Abhidharma, a theoretical compilation of Shakyamuni and his successors guiding disciples in practice.

The Tripitaka collected by Zunsheng Temple has now been moved to collections such as the Sichuan Provincial Library.

Because the Scripture Library was built at a place located on a river beach with a high groundwater level, the building has high requirements for the stability of column bases and the load-bearing and moisture-proofing of columns; hence the column bases are tall and the column diameters are thickened — this phenomenon is rare among ancient buildings in the province.

Since the Scripture Library was built over 300 years ago, the beams and columns have not tilted or sunk; it is a model of ancient building construction adapting to local conditions.

In addition, the timber architecture of the Tang-Song period had a rough and rugged form, and the powerful xieshan roof is a good reflection.

三台潼川古城墙及东、南城门

Ancient City Wall and East Gate or South Gate of Tongchuan in Santai
国家级 明—清 城墙、城门
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address绵阳市三台县潼川镇皂角城、凯江社区
类型 Type城墙、城门
看点 Highlights: 古城墙 谯楼 标语

中文描述 Description

经过多次问路和长途的寻找，眼前却始终是杂乱曲折的街巷，车子一个转弯忽然看到夕阳余晖下的潼川古城墙，那一刹那令人有些难以置信。

刚刚的浮躁心绪也一下子浸染了某种悠悠渺渺的意味。

潼川古城自晋代咸宁四年(278年)立县，刘宋元嘉中(434年)筑州城以来，已历经1500多年，虽经历代官维修改建，但是城池基址一直未变。

而这潼川古城墙，则是始建于南宋，经明朝修葺，又于清乾隆三十二年(1767年)在原基础上重新翻修而成。

至于三台的历史，唐代这里为剑南东川节度使所在地，与西川节度使所在地成都，同为管辖四川的两大都市，诗圣杜甫也曾在此居住两年；

明朝时三台为潼川府衙所在，亦是兵家必争之地。

但是在城门下环顾四周，我看到的是杂乱的小铺，破败的平房和泥泞的土路。

如果不看资料，很难想象这是一座有上千年历史的古城，更难想象这里曾经是与成都并列的首要之地。

但近年来，在郑碧娴、舒乙等人士的呼吁之下，城墙已得到更多重视和保护，并已被列入第七批全国重点文物保护单位。

城门现存有东门(凤山)与南门(印台)，其南门至老西门段长约860米，以及东门至三台中学段约280米，总长2139米。

城墙外层均用长1.2米、高宽0.3~0.4米的砂岩条石错缝叠压浆砌而成，内以夯土填实，墙体下宽上窄，收分明显。

虽经数百年风霜洗礼，墙体结构仍然坚固稳定，无下沉问题。

中南门上建有谯楼，为二层重檐歇山顶建筑，面阔三间12米，穿斗式梁架，檐上留有明嘉靖清乾隆等题记。

今天的城墙上还保存存旧时雕刻的毛主席语录，虽已褪色了，但凹凸之间仍然留下强烈的历史印记。

想想旅游景点里那些万人景仰的古迹，再看看这里被电线纠缠的城墙，我忽然觉得这就是大隐于市的隐者，多了一份带着岁月磨砺带来的淡然与沉静，它默默地俯视那些寒来暑往，悲欢离合。

英文翻译 English Translation

After asking for directions many times and searching for a long distance, what was before my eyes was always chaotic and winding streets; the car made a turn and suddenly I saw the Tongchuan Ancient City Wall under the afterglow of the setting sun — at that moment it was somewhat unbelievable.

The just-now impetuous mood was also suddenly infused with a certain long-distant and faint meaning.

Since the establishment of the county in the 4th year of Xianning of Jin (278), and the building of the prefectural city in the mid-Yuanjia period of Liu Song (434), the ancient city of Tongchuan has gone through over 1,500 years; although it has undergone repairs and reconstructions by officials of various dynasties, the base site of the city wall has remained unchanged.

And this Tongchuan Ancient City Wall was first built in Southern Song, repaired in Ming, and rebuilt on the original foundation in the 32nd year of Qianlong (1767), Qing.

As for the history of Santai, in Tang dynasty this place was the seat of the Jiannan Dongchuan Jiedushi (military governor), and together with Chengdu, the seat of the Xichuan Jiedushi, were the two major cities governing Sichuan; the Poet Sage Du Fu also lived here for two years; in Ming dynasty Santai was the seat of the Tongchuan Prefecture yamen, also a place contested by military forces.

But looking around under the city gate, what I saw were chaotic small shops, dilapidated bungalows, and muddy dirt roads.

Without looking at materials, it is hard to imagine that this is an ancient city with over a thousand years of history, even harder to imagine that this was once a primary place on par with Chengdu.

But in recent years, under the appeals of people such as Zheng Bixian and Shu Yi, the city wall has received more attention and protection, and has been listed in the 7th batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units.

The city gates currently surviving are the East Gate (Fengshan) and South Gate (Yintai); the section from the South Gate to the Old West Gate is about 860m long, and the section from the East Gate to Santai Middle School is about 280m, with a total length of 2,139m.

The outer layer of the city wall is all built with staggered and overlapping mortar-laid sandstone dressed stones 1.2m long and 0.3-0.4m high and wide; the interior is filled with rammed earth; the wall body is wide at the bottom and narrow at the top, with obvious tapering.

Although baptized by hundreds of years of wind and frost, the wall structure is still solid and stable, with no subsidence problems.

On the Central-South Gate there is built a watchtower, a two-story double-eave xieshan roof building, 3 bays wide (12m), with a chuan-dou beam frame; on the eaves there are inscriptions from Ming Jiajing and Qing Qianlong, etc.

Today's city wall still preserves Chairman Mao's quotations carved in old times; although faded, the凹凸 still leave a strong historical imprint.

Thinking of the historic sites admired by ten thousand people at tourist attractions, and then looking at the city wall here entangled by wires, I suddenly feel that this is the hermit who greatly conceals himself in the city, with an extra touch of indifference and tranquility brought by the tempering of years; it silently overlooks those comings and goings of cold and heat, sorrows and joys.

三台东塔及北塔

East Pagoda and North Pagoda of Santai
省级 明—清 古塔
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address绵阳市三台县东塔镇南100米、北坝镇北塔村东南500米
类型 Type古塔
看点 Highlights: 砖石作，题刻，修复

中文描述 Description

三台县东塔位于四川省绵阳市三台县城东面的东山公园之上，塔前半山腰为东山寺原址。

东塔建于明万历三十一年(1603年)，为六角九层楼阁式砖塔，塔内有楼梯可以盘旋至顶，与涪江对岸的北塔遥相对望。

北塔则与东塔形制几乎相同，建于清嘉庆十八年(1813年)。

在目前绵阳境内保存的古塔中，三台东塔是修建最早的一座。

它的修建颇具传奇因素，据史料载，明朝潼川州知州顾云凤观察三台县城地形时发现三台三面环山，唯有东南角相对较低，从风水上看不够完美，因此顾云凤捐约两千银子筹建修塔。

三台永明人张正学组织募捐和施工，几次停工复工，经十余年才建成。

当然这座塔不仅仅是起到风水上的作用，它更是为古代涪江航运提供了显要的地理坐标。

这样的古塔岂能与文人墨客无缘，塔门两边便有明代潼川知府陈南金所题石刻对联：九级浮图，举步凌云霄之上；

三巴砥柱，陶情在山水之间。

塔顶亦刻有明万历潼川吏科张正学的七律诗句添了几许人文色彩。

今昔公园内的苏母教子像、东林晚钟图亦是具有一番韵味。

汶川地震时东塔六层以上部分倒塌，现已修复如初，并树碑记载。

英文翻译 English Translation

The East Pagoda of Santai County is located on Dongshan Park, east of Santai County town, Mianyang City, Sichuan Province; on the mountainside in front of the pagoda is the original site of Dongshan Temple.

The East Pagoda was built in the 31st year of Wanli (1603), Ming; it is a hexagonal nine-story pavilion-style brick pagoda, with stairs inside that can spiral to the top, echoing the North Pagoda across the Fu River from afar.

The North Pagoda is almost identical in form to the East Pagoda, built in the 18th year of Jiaqing (1813), Qing.

Among the ancient pagodas currently preserved in Mianyang, the East Pagoda of Santai is the earliest built one.

Its construction is quite legendary; according to historical records, when Gu Yunfeng, the prefect of Tongchuan Prefecture in Ming, observed the terrain of Santai County town, he found that Santai is surrounded by mountains on three sides, with only the southeast corner relatively low, not perfect enough in terms of fengshui; therefore Gu Yunfeng donated about two thousand taels of silver to raise funds for building the pagoda.

Zhang Zhengxue, a native of Yongming in Santai, organized fundraising and construction; work was stopped and resumed several times, and it took over ten years to complete.

Of course this pagoda not only played a role in fengshui, but also provided a prominent geographical coordinate for ancient Fu River shipping.

How could such an ancient pagoda have no connection with literati and scholars?

On both sides of the pagoda gate there are stone-carved couplets inscribed by Chen Nanjin, the prefect of Tongchuan in Ming: Nine-story stupa, stepping up to the clouds and sky; Sanba pillar, cultivating sentiment among mountains and waters.

The pagoda top is also engraved with a seven-character regulated verse by Zhang Zhengxue, an official of the Tongchuan吏 section in Ming Wanli, adding a bit of humanistic color.

The Su Mother Teaching Son statue and Donglin Evening Bell picture in today's park also have a certain charm.

During the Wenchuan earthquake, the part above the sixth story of the East Pagoda collapsed; it has now been restored to its original state, with a stele erected to record it.

云台观

Yuntai Taoist Temple
国家级 明—清 城墙、城门
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address绵阳市三台县安居镇云台村东20米
类型 Type城墙、城门
看点 Highlights: 牌坊 规模完整的庙观

中文描述 Description

巍巍胜境类蓬莱茅屋云台天下无正是描述云台观的诗句。

因云台观不属唐代以前的名山胜境，所以不在46大小洞天和72福地之列，但其自然环境和宫观规模已经超过了很多现存的洞天福地，是仅次于青城山的四川省第二大道教名观。

在《云台胜纪》一书中，其作者曾将其与武当山相提并论。

云台观始建于南宋时期，本名祐圣观，因现存明代玄天宫、券拱门、石华表、云台胜境坊玉带桥以及清代青龙白虎殿、降魔殿、香亭和钟鼓楼等。

坐落在三台县安居镇云台山，又名云台观。

云台山山清水秀，草木葱郁，云蒸霞蔚，风光迷人；

云台观亦是规模宏大，依山附势，被文物专家誉为全国罕见的从宋式过渡到明清式的官式建筑实例。

云台观于宋元损毁，明清重建，又经汶川地震考验，现存明代玄天宫、券拱门、石华表、云台胜境坊玉带桥以及清代青龙白虎殿、降魔殿、香亭和钟鼓楼等。

我们来到云台观时天色已晚，观门已经关闭，只得在周边观摩，由周边贩卖香火的摊子依稀可见白日里香客登临的繁忙景象，正门彩绘、石狮及壁画都是较为精美的，还有零星古建散落在外。

虽未进得观内，亦见其上雕梁画栋，细部精美独特，边上还有一座静园，也是清幽雅致。

在外面转了数圈细细端详之后，乘着夜色叹惋而归。

英文翻译 English Translation

The towering sacred realm resembles Penglai; thatched cottage and cloud platform have no equal under heaven — this is precisely the poem describing Yuntai Taoist Temple.

Because Yuntai Taoist Temple does not belong to the famous mountain sacred realms before Tang dynasty, it is not among the 46 major and minor cave heavens and 72 blessed lands; but its natural environment and palace-temple scale have already surpassed many existing cave heavens and blessed lands, and it is the second largest Daoist famous temple in Sichuan Province, second only to Qingcheng Mountain.

In the book Record of Yuntai Sacred Realm, its author once compared it with Wudang Mountain.

Yuntai Taoist Temple was first built in Southern Song dynasty, originally named Yousheng Temple; because of the surviving Ming dynasty Xuantian Palace, arched gate, stone ornamental column, Yuntai Sacred Realm Archway, Jade Belt Bridge, as well as Qing dynasty Qinglong-Baihu Hall, Xiangmo Hall, incense pavilion, and bell and drum towers, etc.

It is located on Yuntai Mountain, Anju Town, Santai County, also known as Yuntai Taoist Temple.

Yuntai Mountain has beautiful mountains and clear waters, lush vegetation, steaming clouds and glowing sunset, with charming scenery; Yuntai Taoist Temple is also large-scale, built according to the mountain and following its momentum, praised by cultural relic experts as a rare nationwide example of official-style architecture transitioning from Song style to Ming-Qing style.

Yuntai Taoist Temple was damaged in Song-Yuan, rebuilt in Ming-Qing, and又 tested by the Wenchuan earthquake; currently surviving are the Ming dynasty Xuantian Palace, arched gate, stone ornamental column, Yuntai Sacred Realm Archway, Jade Belt Bridge, as well as Qing dynasty Qinglong-Baihu Hall, Xiangmo Hall, incense pavilion, and bell and drum towers, etc.

When we arrived at Yuntai Taoist Temple it was already late, and the temple gate was already closed; we had to observe from the surroundings.

From the stalls selling incense around, one can vaguely see the busy scene of pilgrims visiting during the day; the main gate paintings, stone lions, and murals are all relatively exquisite, and there are also scattered ancient buildings outside.

Although we did not enter the temple, we also saw its carved beams and painted pillars above, with exquisite and unique details; beside it there is also a Jingyuan (Quiet Garden), also serene and elegant.

After walking around outside several times and examining carefully, we returned with sighs under the night.

开禧寺

Kaixi Temple
国家级 明 宗教建筑
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty明
地址 Address绵阳市安县塔水镇开禧寺村
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 明代木构 修复

中文描述 Description

开禧寺地处四川省绵阳市安县南部，始建于明永乐年间，距今已有609年的历史。

原开禧寺占地约5万平方米，主要包括文昌殿、接引殿、千手观音殿等十余座建筑，在文化大革命期间开禧寺受到了严重的破坏，目前仅大雄殿保存较为完好。

开禧寺于1991年被选为省级文物保护单位，在2013年又被国务院评为第七批全国重点文物保护单位。

大雄殿进深四间，面宽三间，殿梁上有明永乐四年(1406年)题记，说明此殿建造年代。

大殿总建筑面积约170平方米，屋顶铺有青瓦，四角屋檐向上高高翘起，极为独特。

四周墙上共有斗拱20朵，颇为古朴。

在2008年的汶川大地震中，开禧寺又一次遭受到了破坏，不过幸运的是国家及时拨款对开禧寺展开修复工作，除了大雄殿的维修之外，其他殿宇也进行了维修重建，同时也对开禧寺周围环境进行绿化。

现在的开禧寺整个建筑规模宏大、气势磅礴，身处周围竹林民居之中，别有一派祥和景象。

英文翻译 English Translation

Kaixi Temple is located in the south of Anxian County, Mianyang City, Sichuan Province.

It was first built during the Ming Yongle era, and to date has a history of 609 years.

The original Kaixi Temple covered about 50,000 sq m, mainly including over ten buildings such as Wenchang Hall, Reception Hall, and Thousand-Armed Guanyin Hall.

During the Cultural Revolution, Kaixi Temple suffered severe damage; currently only the Mahavira Hall is relatively well preserved.

Kaixi Temple was selected as a provincial cultural relic protection unit in 1991, and in 2013 was again rated by the State Council as the 7th batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units.

The Mahavira Hall is 4 bays deep and 3 bays wide; on the hall beam there is an inscription from the 4th year of Yongle (1406), Ming, indicating the construction date of this hall.

The total building area of the main hall is about 170 sq m; the roof is covered with grey tiles, and the four corner eaves soar high upward, extremely unique.

On the surrounding walls there are a total of 20 bracket sets, quite simple and ancient.

In the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake, Kaixi Temple suffered damage once again; but fortunately the state promptly allocated funds to carry out restoration work on Kaixi Temple.

Besides the maintenance of the Mahavira Hall, other halls were also repaired and rebuilt, while the surrounding environment of Kaixi Temple was also greened.

Today's Kaixi Temple has an entire building complex of grand scale and majestic momentum, situated among surrounding bamboo forests and folk residences, with a unique and auspicious scene.
