南龛摩崖造像

Cliffside Statues of Nankan
国家级 隋—唐 摩崖造像
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty隋—唐
地址 Address巴中市南龛山
类型 Type摩崖造像
看点 Highlights: 造像 经幢

中文描述 Description

南龛摩崖造像位于四川省巴中市，始建于隋唐，是巴中地区保存最完整、最集中的造像，于1988年由国务院列为全国重点文物保护单位。

坐落于南龛山上的南龛石窟，历经隋唐以来数代打造，现有石窟174龛、2000余尊保存完好的造像、4则新建碑、10则造像碑、14座经幢、一幅严武(唐巴州牧)的奏表碑、52首诗文、52条题记。

南龛石窟里的造像各个匠心独运、栩栩如生，当中有气质浑厚的天王、神态庄严的佛像、体态优美的飞天、神情潇洒的伎乐等，极为珍贵。

英文翻译 English Translation

The Cliffside Statues of Nankan are located in Bazhong City, Sichuan Province.

They were first built in Sui-Tang, and are the most completely preserved and most concentrated statues in the Bazhong area; in 1988 they were listed by the State Council as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit.

The Nankan Grottoes, located on Nankan Mountain, have been created through generations since Sui-Tang; currently there are 174 niches, over 2,000 well-preserved statues, 4 new steles, 10 statue steles, 14 scripture pillars, one memorial stele of Yan Wu (Tang Bazhou Governor), 52 poems, and 52 inscriptions.

The statues in the Nankan Grottoes are each ingeniously designed and lifelike; among them there are heavenly kings with vigorous temperament, Buddha statues with solemn expressions, flying apsaras with graceful postures, and musicians with elegant expressions, etc., extremely precious.

水宁寺摩崖造像

Cliffside Statues of Shuining Temple
国家级 唐 摩崖造像
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty唐
地址 Address巴中市巴州区清江镇
类型 Type摩崖造像
看点 Highlights: 造像

中文描述 Description

水宁寺摩崖造像位于巴中市巴州区水宁寺镇，现存佛教造像300余尊，是唐代摩崖石刻的典型代表，于2001年与南龛摩崖造像合并为全国第五批重点文物保护单位。

水宁寺的摩崖造像多为盛唐时期造刻，也有少数的晚唐作品。

主要的内容有药师三尊变释迦说法像等佛教题材。

这些造像体现出典型的唐代造像特征，体态丰腴，形象端庄。

佛像安详，力士勇猛，飞天、侍者、佛龛供养人等则展现出各异的神态与肢体语言，形象生动，令人惊异于唐代造像的高超造诣。

川渝地区唐代摩崖造像留存较多，是我国古代文化艺术史上的精品，水宁寺造像虽不甚知名，但其历史价值却不容小觑。

英文翻译 English Translation

The Cliffside Statues of Shuining Temple are located in Shuining Temple Town, Bazhou District, Bazhong City.

Currently there are over 300 surviving Buddhist statues, a typical representative of Tang dynasty cliffside stone carvings; in 2001 they were merged with the Cliffside Statues of Nankan as the 5th batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units.

Most of the cliffside statues of Shuining Temple were carved during the High Tang period, with a few works from the late Tang.

The main contents include Buddhist themes such as the Triad of Medicine Master and the Shakyamuni Preaching Dharma Statue.

These statues reflect typical Tang dynasty statue characteristics, with plump postures and dignified images.

The Buddha statues are serene, the guardian warriors are fierce, and the flying apsaras, attendants, and niche donors show various expressions and body language, with vivid images, making one marvel at the superb attainment of Tang dynasty statue carving.

The Tang dynasty cliffside statues in the Sichuan-Chongqing region have survived in relatively large numbers, and are fine works in the history of ancient Chinese cultural art; although the Shuining Temple statues are not very well known, their historical value should not be underestimated.

白石寺

Baishi Temple
省级 清 宗教建筑
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address巴中市通江县文胜乡白石寺村
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 木构 题记 雕刻

中文描述 Description

白石寺位于四川省巴中市通江县文胜乡白石寺村的沙溪河旁，是一座典型的清代古寺。

白石寺建筑的原有规模宏大，由前、中、后三殿组成，经过了数百年的历史风霜，现后殿已毁，仅存前殿和中殿两座古迹斑驳的单体建筑，分别建于清康熙五十五年(1716年)和清乾隆三十年(1771年)。

白石寺现已被选入第八批四川省重点文物保护单位。

白石寺的建筑格局为轴对称形式，前殿和中殿依次沿着中轴线呈对称分布。

白石寺的前殿和中殿的名称分别为佛爷殿和老君殿，大殿的主体虽已残破不堪，但其粗大高耸的立柱仍屹立不倒，可见当初建造时所用木料之上乘。

此外，殿中还留存有精美的构件镂空雕刻，饰有花鸟图案，显示着设计修建工匠的高超技艺。

房屋与雕饰精美协调的布局，不得不令人赞叹。

英文翻译 English Translation

Baishi (White Stone) Temple is located beside the Shaxi River in Baishisi Village, Wensheng Township, Tongjiang County, Bazhong City, Sichuan Province.

It is a typical Qing dynasty ancient temple.

The original scale of the Baishi Temple building was grand, composed of front, middle, and rear halls; after hundreds of years of historical vicissitudes, the rear hall has now been destroyed, and only two weathered single buildings, the front hall and middle hall, survive, respectively built in the 55th year of Kangxi (1716) and the 30th year of Qianlong (1771), Qing.

Baishi Temple has now been selected into the 8th batch of Sichuan Provincial Key Cultural Relics Protection Units.

The architectural layout of Baishi Temple is in an axisymmetric form; the front hall and middle hall are sequentially distributed symmetrically along the central axis.

The names of the front hall and middle hall of Baishi Temple are respectively the Buddha Hall and the Laojun Hall; although the main body of the main hall is already in ruins, its thick and towering columns still stand firm, showing the high quality of the timber used in the original construction.

In addition, exquisite component openwork carvings remain in the hall, decorated with flower and bird patterns, showing the superb skills of the design and construction craftsmen.

The exquisite and coordinated layout of the houses and carvings has to be admired.

鲁班寺

Luban Temple
省级 明—清 宗教建筑
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address巴中市通江县诺水河镇鲁坝村
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 轴线 雕刻 明清木构

中文描述 Description

鲁班寺位于巴中市通江县诺水河镇鲁坝村长滩河旁，坐落在环境优美的诺水河国家级风景名胜区中。

鲁班寺始建于明末，后于清朝进行重修，建筑格局保存相对完好，现被收入四川省重点文物保护单位。

鲁班寺的建筑格局为对称院落形式，现留存有较为完整的前殿、正殿与左右厢房。

建筑的外墙虽已剥落，但内部的建筑结构却保存得较为完好，是研究明末清初建筑风格艺术不可多得的艺术珍品。

大殿的建筑风格较为质朴，飘逸的飞檐与青瓦之上并无更多点缀。

但殿内留存着精美的镂空花窗和纹刻梁柱，绘有祥云、花叶等图案，可以依稀想见，鲁班寺建成之初大殿内部雕梁画栋的精美景象。

可惜岁月流逝，时光的剥蚀使得这里层层积灰，孤寂异常。

英文翻译 English Translation

Luban Temple is located beside Changtan River, Luba Village, Nuoshuihe Town, Tongjiang County, Bazhong City, situated in the beautifully landscaped Nuoshui River National Scenic Area.

Luban Temple was first built in the late Ming, later rebuilt in Qing dynasty; its architectural layout is relatively well preserved, and is now included in the Sichuan Provincial Key Cultural Relics Protection Units.

The architectural layout of Luban Temple is in a symmetrical courtyard form; currently there survive relatively complete front hall, main hall, and left and right wing rooms.

Although the outer walls of the building have peeled off, the internal building structure is relatively well preserved, and is a rare artistic treasure for studying the architectural style and art of the late Ming and early Qing.

The architectural style of the main hall is relatively simple, with no more decorations on the elegant flying eaves and grey tiles.

But inside the hall there remain exquisite hollowed-out flower windows and carved beam columns, painted with patterns such as auspicious clouds and flower leaves; one can vaguely imagine the exquisite scene of carved beams and painted pillars inside the main hall when Luban Temple was first completed.

Unfortunately, as time passes, the erosion of time has made layers of dust accumulate here, extremely lonely.

燊海井

Shenhai Well
国家级 清 盐井
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address自贡市大安区长堰塘旁
类型 Type盐井
看点 Highlights: 千米盐井 天车 井盐生产 大木结构

中文描述 Description

自贡市素以盐之都、龙之乡、灯之城的美誉而闻名于世。

其中，最让人印象深刻的便是其独特的井盐文化了，而燊海井便是其典型代表。

燊海井位于自贡市大安区长堰塘旁，占地面积约为3亩(1亩约等于666.7平方米)，井位海拔约为341.4米，井深约为1001.42米，是世界上第一口超过千米的深井。

燊海井历时13年于道光十五年(1835年)得以竣工，它曾经是一口卤气同采的高产井，至今仍在生产井盐。

自贡也因为其鼎盛的盐业成为中国井矿盐中心。

靠近燊海井，立即映入眼帘的便是称为天车的木质建筑，实为井架。

由竹篾将圆木紧紧捆绑而成的天车高高耸立在井边，远远望去颇具汉字中人的形象。

作为自贡市的标志性建筑之一，古老而沧桑的天车，像一位长者一样，注视着他所钟爱的城市的发展变化，见证着自贡井盐文化的发展壮大。

由于盐卤长年累月的浸泡、沉淀，井口周围已经腐蚀、发黄，俨然斑斑岁月的痕迹。

盐卤便是通过器皿深入井口，从这千米之下打捞而出。

由于没有机械的帮助，打捞卤水全靠原始木质器械完成。

这便是其中最重要的工具——大车，它利用木块和粗绳搭建捆绑而成，具有转动灵活、牵引力大等特点。

正因为其独创性与代表性，燊海井于1988年正式被入全国重点保护文物；

自贡传统采盐技术也是国家非物质文化遗产中的重要一员。

英文翻译 English Translation

Zigong City is world-famous for its reputation as the Capital of Salt, Hometown of Dinosaurs, and City of Lanterns.

Among them, the most impressive is its unique well-salt culture, and Shenhai Well is its typical representative.

Shenhai Well is located beside Changyantang, Da'an District, Zigong City, covering an area of about 3 mu (1 mu ≈ 666.7 sq m); the well site is at an altitude of about 341.4m, and the well depth is about 1,001.42m — it is the first deep well in the world to exceed one thousand meters.

Shenhai Well took 13 years to be completed in the 15th year of Daoguang (1835); it was once a high-yield well extracting both brine and gas, and is still producing well salt to this day.

Zigong also became the center of China's well and rock salt due to its prosperous salt industry.

Approaching Shenhai Well, what immediately comes into view is the timber building called the Heavenly Cart, actually a well derrick.

The Heavenly Cart, tightly bound from round logs by bamboo strips, stands tall beside the well; from afar it quite resembles the Chinese character for person (人).

As one of the landmark buildings of Zigong City, the ancient and weathered Heavenly Cart, like an elder, watches the development and changes of the city he loves, witnessing the development and growth of Zigong's well-salt culture.

Due to years of soaking and precipitation by salt brine, the area around the well mouth has corroded and turned yellow, clearly showing traces of time.

Salt brine is retrieved by inserting vessels deep into the well mouth, hauled up from a thousand meters below.

Without the help of machinery, hauling brine relies entirely on primitive timber instruments.

This is the most important tool among them — the Great Cart; it is built and bound from wood blocks and thick ropes, with features such as flexible rotation and large traction.

Precisely because of its originality and representativeness, Shenhai Well was officially listed as a National Key Protected Cultural Relic in 1988; Zigong's traditional salt-extraction technology is also an important member of the national intangible cultural heritage.

自贡桓侯宫

Huanhou Hall in Zigong
国家级 清 祠庙
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address自贡市自流井区新民街与中华路口交界处
类型 Type祠庙
看点 Highlights: 布局 结构 桓侯宫门 戏楼 正殿

中文描述 Description

位于四川省自贡市自流井区的桓侯宫，始建于清代乾隆年间，于同治四年至光绪元年(1865—1875年)原址复建，2013年被列入全国重点文物保护单位。

建在小山坡上的桓侯宫，整个建筑群看起来气势磅礴，宏伟壮观。

靠近桓侯宫，映入眼帘的是其庄严肃穆的大门。

面阔三间20.6米，高14.2米，正楼檐下竖匾为桓侯宫，山门屹立着弧形封火墙，瞬间给桓侯宫增添一种古老而神秘的色彩。

特别值得一提的是，桓侯宫的雕刻巧夺天工。

不仅由于其保存完好，更由于其刻艺精湛，使得桓侯宫中无论是石雕还是木雕，都显得其雕刻艺术登峰造极，从进门两边的门墩就可见一斑。

这一对石雕，左为龙，右为凤，活灵活现，栩栩如生。

仔细观察这些雕刻，纹路清晰，刀法细腻，宛如行云流水，游刃有余。

进入桓侯宫，在门厅之上的建筑，称为戏楼。

拾级而上便是正殿，面阔三间13.55米，进深四间21.15米，高13.82米，歇山顶，穿斗式梁架。

这里的戏台、正殿、钟鼓楼等建筑，与大多数古代建筑相去不远，但是能够在建筑面积并不大的桓侯宫内井然有序地布置这样的建筑格局而不产生拥挤之感，确实让人对建筑师的高超能力拍案叫绝。

英文翻译 English Translation

Huanhou Hall, located in Ziliujing District, Zigong City, Sichuan Province, was first built during the Qing Qianlong era, rebuilt on the original site from the 4th year of Tongzhi to the 1st year of Guangxu (1865-1875), and was listed as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit in 2013.

Huanhou Hall, built on a small hillside, has an entire building complex that looks majestic and spectacular.

Approaching Huanhou Hall, what comes into view is its solemn and majestic gate.

It is 3 bays wide (20.6m) and 14.2m high; under the eave of the main tower there is a vertical plaque reading Huanhou Hall; the mountain gate stands with an arc-shaped fire-sealing wall, instantly adding an ancient and mysterious color to Huanhou Hall.

Particularly worth mentioning is that the carvings of Huanhou Hall are a marvel of craftsmanship.

Not only because it is well preserved, but even more because of its exquisite carving skills, making both stone carvings and wood carvings in Huanhou Hall appear to have reached the peak of carving art — this can be seen from the door piers on both sides of the entrance.

This pair of stone carvings, with a dragon on the left and a phoenix on the right, are vivid and lifelike.

Carefully observing these carvings, the lines are clear and the knife technique is delicate, like flowing clouds and running water, with effortless mastery.

Entering Huanhou Hall, the building above the entrance hall is called the theater tower.

Ascending the steps is the main hall, 3 bays wide (13.55m), 4 bays deep (21.15m), 13.82m high, with xieshan roof and chuan-dou beam frame.

The buildings here, such as the stage, main hall, and bell and drum towers, are not far from most ancient buildings; but being able to orderly arrange such a building layout within Huanhou Hall, whose building area is not large, without creating a sense of crowding, truly makes one marvel at the superb ability of the architect.

西秦会馆

Xi qin Guild Hall
国家级 清 会馆
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address自贡市自流井区解放路107号
类型 Type会馆
看点 Highlights: 布局 武圣宫大门 戏楼 院落

中文描述 Description

位于自贡市自流井区解放路的西秦会馆，坐落在风景秀美的龙凤山下，后靠自贡市的母亲河——釜溪河，巍然耸立，庄重不凡。

该馆原是清代陕西盐商为了联络议事等而修建的会馆，故称西秦会馆；

又因为馆内供奉关羽像，也被称为关帝庙。

1988年被列为全国重点文物保护单位，后设有自贡市盐业历史博物馆。

会馆始建于清乾隆元年(1736年)，于道光七至九年(1827—1828年)大规模扩建并维修，新中国成立后曾几度维修，目前为三进四合院布局，坐南向北，占地面积3451平方米，建筑面积约3000平方米。

主要建筑有武圣宫大门、献技楼、大观楼、福海楼、抱厅、参天阁、中殿、正殿等。

武圣宫大门高大威武、庄严肃穆，大门上金色图案和各种精美的雕刻，十分夺目。

门前的石狮排列整齐、对立而视，表情自然而又生动，身姿挺拔，形象威猛。

门后殿阔四间32.85米，进深8.1米，高16.8米，重檐歇山顶，穿斗式梁架。

除了武圣宫之外，戏楼、中殿、正殿等依次排列在会馆中轴线上，随地形变化有所起伏，标高变化丰富。

整体看来西秦会馆内各建筑造型典雅、别致，相互之间采用布局均衡，园林式的整体呈现出一种有机的凝聚感。

殿内各处的彩绘、泥塑以及木雕石雕向人们讲述着从神话到历史中各种各样的民俗故事，令人流连忘返。

这俨然就是一幅绝美的园林画卷。

英文翻译 English Translation

The Xi qin (Western Shaanxi) Guild Hall, located on Jiefang Road, Ziliujing District, Zigong City, is situated at the foot of the scenic Longfeng Mountain, backed by the mother river of Zigong City — the Fuxi River, towering majestically and solemnly.

This hall was originally a guild hall built by Shaanxi salt merchants in Qing dynasty for liaison and discussion, hence called Xi qin Guild Hall; also because a statue of Guan Yu is enshrined inside the hall, it is also called the Guandi Temple.

In 1988 it was listed as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit, and later the Zigong Salt Industry History Museum was established.

The guild hall was first built in the 1st year of Qianlong (1736), Qing, and underwent large-scale expansion and maintenance from the 7th to 9th year of Daoguang (1827-1828); after the founding of New China it was repaired several times.

Currently it has a three-courtyard siheyuan layout, facing north, covering 3,451 sq m, with a building area of about 3,000 sq m.

The main buildings include the Wusheng Palace Gate, Performance Tower, Daguan Tower, Fuhai Tower, Embracing Hall, Cantian Pavilion, Middle Hall, Main Hall, etc.

The Wusheng Palace Gate is tall and mighty, solemn and majestic; the golden patterns and various exquisite carvings on the gate are very eye-catching.

The stone lions in front of the gate are neatly arranged, facing each other, with natural and vivid expressions, upright postures, and fierce images.

Behind the gate, the hall is 4 bays wide (32.85m), 8.1m deep, 16.8m high, with double-eave xieshan roof and chuan-dou beam frame.

Besides the Wusheng Palace, the theater tower, middle hall, main hall, etc.

are sequentially arranged on the central axis of the guild hall, undulating with terrain changes, with rich elevation changes.

Overall, each building in the Xi qin Guild Hall has an elegant and unique shape; they adopt a balanced layout among each other, and the garden-style whole presents an organic sense of cohesion.

The colored paintings, clay sculptures, and wood and stone carvings everywhere in the halls tell people various folk stories from mythology to history, making people linger and forget to return.

This is simply a beautiful garden painting scroll.

王爷庙

Wangye Shrine
省级 清 宗教建筑
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address自贡市自流井区釜溪河畔
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 水景 院落 戏台 雕刻

中文描述 Description

自贡市素以盐之都著称，自清道光、咸丰年间，自流井地区已然发展形成了四川省的主要盐场。

为了紧锁财源，当时信奉风水的盐商巨贾们于同治年间在釜溪河边建庙镇江，建成了如今的王爷庙。

王爷庙坐落在釜溪河边，背倚龙凤山，与附近的西秦会馆、桓侯宫形成鼎立之势。

远观王爷庙，一栋形态奇特的建筑傲然矗立，伴着粼粼波光，幽幽绿树，显得是那么恬静优雅，不像是坐落在市中心的古建筑，仿佛超脱喧闹，自然和谐。

靠近王爷庙，浓浓的古色古香的氛围便扑面而来。

庙墙以砖红色为主，点点绿叶红花探墙而出，美不胜收。

王爷庙大门虽系后来重建，但大门匾额上书有王爷庙三个大字，仿佛也在含蓄地透露着其岁月的痕迹。

王爷庙内的布局好似南方园林一般，这里绿树成荫，闲情惬意。

配有假山、石桌等装饰，显得那么不拘一格，但又那么紧密配合。

而王爷庙中最著名的要数那保存相当完好的清代川剧戏台。

该戏台为抬梁式木结构，单檐歇山式屋顶，造型不仅典雅大方，色彩更加绚丽斑斓。

据记载，王爷庙后因修建公路拆毁了部分建筑，因此余下且保存完好的戏楼便显得格外珍贵。

特别值得一提的是，戏台之上的雕刻也十分精致，主题丰富，华丽精美。

即使是岁月无情地冲刷，也不能掩盖这些雕刻所蕴含的极高的艺术价值和观赏价值。

英文翻译 English Translation

Zigong City is known as the Capital of Salt; since the Qing Daoguang and Xianfeng eras, the Ziliujing area had already developed into the main salt field of Sichuan Province.

To lock in financial resources, the wealthy salt merchants who believed in fengshui at that time built a temple by the Fuxi River during the Tongzhi era to subdue the river, completing today's Wangye (River Lord) Shrine.

Wangye Shrine is located by the Fuxi River, backed by Longfeng Mountain, forming a tripartite balance with the nearby Xi qin Guild Hall and Huanhou Hall.

Viewing Wangye Shrine from afar, a building with a peculiar shape stands proudly, accompanied by glistening waves and serene green trees, appearing so tranquil and elegant, not like an ancient building located in the city center, as if transcending the noise, natural and harmonious.

Approaching Wangye Shrine, a strong ancient and elegant atmosphere blows in.

The temple walls are mainly brick-red, with dots of green leaves and red flowers peeking out over the wall, beautiful beyond description.

Although the main gate of Wangye Shrine was rebuilt later, the plaque on the gate bears the three large characters Wangye Shrine, as if subtly revealing its traces of time.

The layout inside Wangye Shrine is like a southern garden; here green trees form shade, with a leisurely and comfortable mood.

Equipped with decorations such as rockeries and stone tables, it appears so unconventional, yet so closely coordinated.

And the most famous in Wangye Shrine is the quite well-preserved Qing dynasty Sichuan opera stage.

This stage is of post-and-lintel timber structure, with single-eave xieshan roof; its shape is not only elegant and graceful, but its colors are even more gorgeous and resplendent.

According to records, Wangye Shrine later had part of its buildings demolished due to road construction, hence the remaining and well-preserved theater tower appears particularly precious.

Particularly worth mentioning is that the carvings on the stage are also very exquisite, with rich themes, gorgeous and refined.

Even the merciless erosion of time cannot conceal the extremely high artistic value and ornamental value contained in these carvings.

荣县镇南塔

Zhennan Pagoda in Rong County
省级 宋 砖石塔
级别 Level省级
年代 Dynasty宋
地址 Address自贡市荣县旭阳镇南
类型 Type砖石塔
看点 Highlights: 地形态 雕刻

中文描述 Description

位于四川省自贡市荣县旭阳镇南的镇南塔，始建于宋代，明清皆有重修。

至今除了塔刹被毁之外，其余部分基本保存完好。

镇南塔为方形11层楼阁砖石塔，通高23.85米，占地面积60.84平方米，巍然耸立，气势不凡。

虽然由于岁月的冲刷使得塔身部分地方变黑，但通体仍为白色，当地人乐于称其为白塔而并非镇南塔。

远观镇南塔，矗立在山巅的它犹如一股浩然正气凝视着山川大地。

塔底树木环绕，绿树成荫，形态各异，美不胜收。

仿佛是为了给白塔以碧绿的点缀，如诗如画，一点儿也不显得突兀，恰好形成了塔与自然融为一体的美妙感觉。

此时白塔全貌尽入眼帘，若天公作美，雾气萦绕之时远眺白塔，此时的白塔在雾中若隐若现，配上点点碧绿，好似仙境一般。

近观镇南塔，塔身逐层内收，各层均以壁柱做成四柱三间形态，模拟楼阁属性。

除一层中部开有真假拱门之外，以上各层均有开窗，极为规整。

塔内有中心塔柱，可沿蹬道绕柱而上，但今已封闭，未能登高望远，一览全城风景实为一憾。

特别值得注意的是，镇南塔第五层塑有一僧人像，虽历经风蚀雨浸，但仍然形态完整，五官清晰。

该僧人坐姿端正，目视前方，嘴角上扬，仿佛凝视着这苍茫大地，直面这沧海桑田。

而这不也正是镇南塔所经历着的吗？

英文翻译 English Translation

Zhennan (South-Suppressing) Pagoda, located south of Xuyang Town, Rong County, Zigong City, Sichuan Province, was first built in Song dynasty, and was rebuilt in both Ming and Qing.

To this day, except for the destroyed pagoda finial, the rest is basically well preserved.

Zhennan Pagoda is a square 11-story pavilion-style brick-stone pagoda, with a total height of 23.85m, covering 60.84 sq m, towering majestically with extraordinary momentum.

Although due to the erosion of time parts of the pagoda body have turned black, the whole body is still white; local people are pleased to call it the White Pagoda rather than Zhennan Pagoda.

Viewing Zhennan Pagoda from afar, standing on the mountain top, it is like a stream of noble righteousness gazing at the mountains and rivers.

At the bottom of the pagoda, trees surround it, with green trees forming shade, in various shapes, beautiful beyond description.

As if to give the White Pagoda a verdant ornament, it is poetic and picturesque, not at all obtrusive,恰好 forming a wonderful feeling of the pagoda integrating with nature.

At this time the full view of the White Pagoda comes into sight; if the weather is favorable, viewing the White Pagoda from afar when mist wraps around it, the White Pagoda at this time looms in and out of the mist, paired with dots of verdant green, like a fairyland.

Viewing Zhennan Pagoda up close, the pagoda body tapers inward layer by layer; each layer uses wall columns to form a four-column three-bay shape, simulating the attributes of a pavilion.

Except for the middle of the first layer which has real and fake arched doors, all layers above have windows opened, extremely regular.

Inside the pagoda there is a central pagoda column, and one can climb along the stairway around the column, but it is now closed; being unable to climb high and look far, taking in the whole city scenery is truly a regret.

Particularly noteworthy is that the fifth layer of Zhennan Pagoda has a statue of a monk; although experiencing wind erosion and rain immersion, it still has a complete form with clear facial features.

The monk sits upright, gazing forward, with the corners of his mouth turned up, as if gazing at this vast land, facing this vicissitude of life.

And isn't this exactly what Zhennan Pagoda has experienced?

荣县大佛石窟

Dafo Grottoes in Rong County
国家级 唐—今 石窟、宗教建筑
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty唐—今
地址 Address自贡市荣县县城东郊大佛山山麓
类型 Type石窟、宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 大佛石窟 大雄禅寺 远瞻与近观

中文描述 Description

荣县大佛坐落在四川省自贡市荣县城东郊大佛山山麓上，与乐山大佛相去不远但各有特点，故而有嘉州大佛雄，荣州大佛美的美誉。

2006年被国务院列入全国重点文物保护单位。

荣县大佛石窟始建于唐代，于山崖中凿窟成佛。

佛像高36.67米，肩宽12.67米，据称是世界第一大释迦牟尼佛(现世佛)造像。

佛像造型饱满，神情庄重，历经千年而保存完好，全面体现了唐代造像特征。

荣县大佛所在庙宇，唐代时名为开化寺，后称为大佛禅寺。

寺庙依山而建，因应山势，使得大佛石窟落在寺庙的中轴线上。

从大佛寺中拾级而上，穿过重重殿宇，便能接近荣县大佛。

这种将巨佛与建筑相互结合的做法，独具匠心，更是世间罕有。

最靠近大佛的是大雄宝殿，不同于其他庙宇将佛像置于殿中的做法，这里佛像就是大佛本身，因此大雄宝殿也成为大佛殿。

站在大佛前近观巨大佛足，经过近年改建，人们还可以攀登而上，在不同层高近距离观赏佛像，独特经历不禁令人叹为观止。

英文翻译 English Translation

The Rong County Great Buddha is located at the foot of Dafo (Great Buddha) Mountain, in the eastern suburbs of Rong County town, Zigong City, Sichuan Province.

It is not far from the Leshan Great Buddha but each has its own characteristics, hence there is the reputation of the Great Buddha of Jiazhou being majestic and the Great Buddha of Rongzhou being beautiful.

In 2006 it was listed by the State Council as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit.

The Rong County Great Buddha Grottoes were first built in Tang dynasty, with a cave chiseled in the cliff to form a Buddha.

The Buddha statue is 36.67m high with a shoulder width of 12.67m; it is said to be the world's largest statue of Shakyamuni Buddha (the Buddha of the present world).

The Buddha statue has a full shape and solemn expression, well preserved after a thousand years, fully reflecting the characteristics of Tang dynasty statue carving.

The temple where the Rong County Great Buddha is located was named Kaihua Temple in Tang dynasty, later called Dafo Chan Temple.

The temple was built according to the mountain, adapting to the mountain terrain, so that the Great Buddha Grotto falls on the central axis of the temple.

Ascending the steps from within the Great Buddha Temple, passing through layers of halls, one can approach the Rong County Great Buddha.

This method of combining the giant Buddha with architecture is ingenious and even more rare in the world.

Closest to the Great Buddha is the Mahavira Hall; unlike other temples that place Buddha statues inside the hall, here the Buddha statue is the Great Buddha itself, hence the Mahavira Hall also becomes the Great Buddha Hall.

Standing in front of the Great Buddha and closely viewing the giant Buddha feet, after recent renovations people can also climb up and view the Buddha statue at close range from different story heights — the unique experience cannot help but make one marvel.

富顺文庙

Temple of Confucius in Fushun
国家级 清 文庙
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address自贡市富顺县富世镇解放街大南门
类型 Type文庙
看点 Highlights: 棂星门 九龙桥 大殿

中文描述 Description

文庙亦称孔庙，是祭祀孔子的庙宇，在全国各地均有分布。

我国保存完好的文庙为数不多，而坐落于四川省自贡市富顺县的富顺文庙，就是其中之一。

富顺文庙始建于北宋庆历四年(1044年)，于2001年被国务院列为全国重点文物保护单位。

富顺文人辈出，故而富顺文庙的显赫地位可见一斑。

初见富顺文庙，一股历史的气息便扑面而来。

虽说从棂星门中仿佛可以看到曲阜文庙的影子，但是它也有自己的特色。

略带星色的红墙庄严肃穆，给文庙营造出一种神圣的氛围。

棂星门上的石柱雕刻着数十条形态各异的龙，与刻有优雅文字的浮雕横匾相辅相成，细腻精致、美观大方，配上岁月所赋予的点点青苔，仿佛更加超凡脱俗、自然和谐。

顺着棂星门向下看去便是泮池，泮池上有一座九龙桥。

据说九龙桥是为状元准备的，因此其修建与雕刻的精细自然不言而喻。

在青青的映衬下，桥上蜿蜒起伏的石龙愈加活灵活现、栩栩如生，一种敬畏之情油然而生。

富顺文庙的大殿坐落于第二个院落，年久失修的大殿虽有些破败，但仍然可以看出其精美的雕刻与宏大的规模。

英文翻译 English Translation

The Confucian Temple, also called the Kong Temple, is a temple for sacrificing to Confucius, distributed throughout the country.

There are not many well-preserved Confucian temples in China, and the Fushun Confucian Temple, located in Fushun County, Zigong City, Sichuan Province, is one of them.

The Fushun Confucian Temple was first built in the 4th year of Qingli of Northern Song (1044), and was listed by the State Council as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit in 2001.

Fushun has produced many literati, hence the prominent status of the Fushun Confucian Temple is evident.

At first sight of the Fushun Confucian Temple, a breath of history blows in.

Although from the Lingxing Gate one can as if see the shadow of the Qufu Confucian Temple, it also has its own characteristics.

The red walls, slightly tinged with star color, are solemn and majestic, creating a sacred atmosphere for the Confucian temple.

The stone columns on the Lingxing Gate are carved with dozens of dragons in various shapes, complementing the relief horizontal plaques engraved with elegant text — delicate and exquisite, beautiful and graceful; paired with the dots of moss bestowed by time, it seems even more transcendent, natural, and harmonious.

Looking down along the Lingxing Gate is the Pan Pool, and on the Pan Pool there is a Nine-Dragon Bridge.

It is said that the Nine-Dragon Bridge was prepared for the top scholar, hence the fineness of its construction and carving is self-evident.

Against the backdrop of green, the winding and undulating stone dragons on the bridge become even more vivid and lifelike, and a feeling of reverence arises spontaneously.

The main hall of the Fushun Confucian Temple is located in the second courtyard; although the long-unrepaired main hall is somewhat dilapidated, one can still see its exquisite carvings and grand scale.

处项目

通远门

Tongyuan Gate
国家级 明—清 古城墙
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address渝中区七星岗
类型 Type古城墙
看点 Highlights: 城墙 城门

中文描述 Description

重庆城共有三次大规模修筑城墙的记载：公元前316年，为巩固秦朝统治，张仪在巴国国都江州(今重庆渝中半岛)始筑城墙；

南宋时期蒙古南侵，彭大雅据半岛地势筑城，基本形成重庆古城墙格局；

明太祖洪武四年(1371年)，戴鼎在旧址建成象征九宫八卦的九开八闭共十七座城门，关于这十七门还有这样一首民谣《重庆歌》：朝天门，大码头，迎官接圣。

千厮门，花包子，白雪如银。

洪崖门，广船开，杀鸡敬神。

临江门，粪码头，肥田有本。

定远门，较场坝，舞刀弄棍。

通远门，锣鼓响，看埋死人。

金汤门，木棺材，大小齐整。

南纪门，菜篮子，涌出涌进。

凤凰门，川道拐，牛羊成群。

金紫门，恰对着，镇台衙门。

储奇门，药材帮，医治百病。

人和门，火炮响，总爷出巡。

太平门，老鼓楼，时辰报准。

太安门，太平仓，积谷利民。

东水门，正对着，鲤跳龙门。

翠微门，挂彩缎，五色鲜明。

复兴门，溜跑马，快如腾云。

可惜如今十七门中保存较好的只余两处，其一就是通远门。

位于正西面的通远门是通往外地的陆路起点，出门向西即为佛图关，是通往四川成都的要道，故称通远。

由于地处要道，通远门见证了多场惨烈的战事，张献忠围攻重庆那场最甚，由于死伤过多，使通远门外七星岗一带由此成为乱葬岗，遂有民谣中通远门，锣鼓响，看埋死人的说法。

据史料记载，明末清初，张献忠率部60万，以10倍于守军的数量依然无法正面强攻，只能绕道江津从菜园坝登陆，夺取佛图关，卡死明军唯一退路，最后的主战场就在通远门。

经过6天激战，张献忠派人掘开城外坟墓，取棺材板令士兵顶在头上以挡矢石，在城下挖地道埋火药，炸塌通远门转角城墙，方才攻入重庆。

如今通远门遗址公园矗立着几组筑城、守城、攻城的铜雕，再现了当年那场激烈的战斗，也诉说着通远门城墙600多年的历史变迁与战乱动荡。

通远门现存城墙及城门为明洪武年间遗址，城门为双拱形门洞，重庆特有的毛青条石砌墙，城门高5.33米，宽3.5米，厚7.41米。

1929年，国民政府首任重庆市长潘文华授意凿穿通远门，600年不破的城墙终被打通，如今只余100米左右残存在城门两边，而原有瓮城更是早已全毁。

以崖为墙，是通远门的雏形。

通远门城墙整齐有序顺山崖而筑，居高临下，呈现出典型具有山地特色的古城墙。

而随着城区扩展，通远门现在位于渝中主干道上，四条公路在这里交汇。

每天车水马龙，人流不断，城上城下市井生活悠然自得。

原来用作战事守卫的关隘如今成为人民安居乐业的场所，这座600多岁的古城墙，将继续守护着重庆城和重庆人。

英文翻译 English Translation

Chongqing City has records of three large-scale city wall constructions: in 316 BC, to consolidate Qin dynasty rule, Zhang Yi first built a city wall at Jiangzhou (today's Chongqing Yuzhong Peninsula), the capital of the Ba State; during the Southern Song period when the Mongols invaded southward, Peng Daya built a city wall according to the peninsula terrain, basically forming the layout of Chongqing's ancient city wall; in the 4th year of Hongwu of Ming Taizu (1371), Dai Ding built on the old site a total of seventeen city gates — nine open and eight closed — symbolizing the Nine Palaces and Eight Trigrams.

About these seventeen gates there is such a folk ballad, the Chongqing Song: Chaotian Gate, great wharf, welcoming officials and receiving saints.

Qiansi Gate, flower buns, white as snow.

Hongya Gate, wide boats open, killing chickens to honor gods.

Linjiang Gate, manure wharf, fertilizer has its source.

Dingyuan Gate, drill ground, wielding swords and staffs.

Tongyuan Gate, gongs and drums sound, watching the burial of the dead.

Jintang Gate, wooden coffins, large and small all neat.

Nanji Gate, vegetable baskets, surging in and out.

Fenghuang Gate, Sichuan road bend, cattle and sheep in groups.

Jinzi Gate, directly facing, the garrison commander's yamen.

Chuqi Gate, medicine merchants, curing all diseases.

Renhe Gate, cannons sound, the general goes on patrol.

Taiping Gate, old drum tower, time reported accurately.

Tai'an Gate, Taiping granary, storing grain for the people.

Dongshui Gate, directly facing, carp leaping the dragon gate.

Cuiwei Gate, hanging colored satin, five colors vivid.

Fuxing Gate, galloping horses, fast as soaring clouds.

Unfortunately, among the seventeen gates today only two remain relatively well preserved, one of which is Tongyuan Gate.

Tongyuan Gate, located on the due west side, was the starting point of the land route leading to other places; going out westward was Fotu Pass, the main road leading to Chengdu, Sichuan, hence called Tongyuan (Leading Far).

Because it was located on a main road, Tongyuan Gate witnessed many tragic battles; the siege of Chongqing by Zhang Xianzhong was the most severe.

Due to excessive deaths, the area around Qixinggang outside Tongyuan Gate thus became a mass burial ground, hence the folk saying in the ballad: Tongyuan Gate, gongs and drums sound, watching the burial of the dead.

According to historical records, at the end of Ming and beginning of Qing, Zhang Xianzhong led 600,000 troops, and with ten times the number of defenders still could not launch a frontal assault; he could only detour to Jiangjin and land from Caiyuanba, seize Fotu Pass, and cut off the only retreat route of the Ming army; the final main battlefield was at Tongyuan Gate.

After six days of fierce fighting, Zhang Xianzhong sent people to dig open graves outside the city, took coffin boards and ordered soldiers to hold them over their heads to block arrows and stones, dug tunnels under the city to bury gunpowder, and blew up the corner city wall of Tongyuan Gate, only then entering Chongqing.

Today, the Tongyuan Gate Ruins Park stands with several groups of bronze sculptures of city-building, city-defending, and city-attacking, recreating that fierce battle of those years, and also recounting the 600-plus years of historical changes and war turmoil of the Tongyuan Gate city wall.

The existing city wall and gate of Tongyuan Gate are ruins from the Ming Hongwu period; the gate is a double-arch doorway, with Chongqing's unique rough bluestone dressed stones for the wall; the city gate is 5.33m high, 3.5m wide, and 7.41m thick.

In 1929, Pan Wenhua, the first mayor of Chongqing under the Nationalist government, authorized the drilling through of Tongyuan Gate; the 600-year-unbroken city wall was finally breached.

Today only about 100m remains on both sides of the gate, and the original barbican has long been completely destroyed.

Using the cliff as a wall was the prototype of Tongyuan Gate.

The Tongyuan Gate city wall is neatly and orderly built along the mountain cliff, commanding a high position, presenting a typical ancient city wall with mountain characteristics.

With urban expansion, Tongyuan Gate is now located on the main road of Yuzhong, where four roads intersect.

Every day there is heavy traffic and constant crowds; city life above and below the wall is leisurely and content.

The pass originally used for war defense has now become a place where people live and work in peace and contentment; this over-600-year-old ancient city wall will continue to guard Chongqing City and the people of Chongqing.

东水门及城墙

Dongshui Gate and City Wall
国家级 明—清 古城墙
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address渝中区望龙门东正街1号
类型 Type古城墙
看点 Highlights: 城墙 城门

中文描述 Description

九开八闭十七门中保存较好的除了通远门，还有鲤跳龙门的东水门。

从朝天门往南，重庆城墙大都建在长江边山崖上。

东水门为老城正东的大门，城门向北，距朝天门约800米，与通远门同为明洪武年间遗址，门上城楼已不复存在，城墙现保存从芭蕉院到东水门下巷的古城墙约230米。

城门宽3.1米、高4.5米、厚6.6米，属石卷顶城门洞。

也许是其所处地势险要，易守难攻的缘故，该门未设瓮城，是开门中的中小城门。

东水门是旧重庆的水码头之一，历史上是重庆城出城过长江到南岸的重要通道，也是到贵州、云南的必经之路。

凭借水码头的优势，这一带曾是旧时城内最繁华的商业区之一，在通向水门的青石梯两边，商铺、茶楼、客栈、酒肆林立。

这里也是会馆集中区，当时重庆城内有八大会馆，这里就集中了三所，即江南会馆、湖广会馆和广东会馆。

后由于水码头迁至望龙门，东水门才逐渐衰落。

如今，一道东水门长江大桥横跨大江，替代水门成为到南岸的通道。

大桥下的旧城门远远地离开了我们的视线，过去城墙下的旧房被改建一新的黑瓦白墙的仿古建筑所替代，四周是开阔平坦的滨江公路，不时有汽车从这里急驶而过，让人很难想象这里曾经的市井繁华。

只有长年累月被下来往的苦力与船客的双脚蹬踏的石阶上露出斑驳的痕迹，在多雨的时节里，散发出岁月的气息。

英文翻译 English Translation

Among the seventeen gates (nine open, eight closed) that are relatively well preserved, besides Tongyuan Gate, there is also Dongshui Gate of Carp Leaping the Dragon Gate.

Going south from Chaotian Gate, most of Chongqing's city walls are built on the cliffs by the Yangtze River.

Dongshui Gate was the main gate due east of the old city, with the gate facing north, about 800m from Chaotian Gate; it is a ruin from the same Ming Hongwu period as Tongyuan Gate.

The gate tower on top no longer exists; the city wall currently preserves about 230m of ancient city wall from Bajiao Courtyard to Dongshui Gate Lower Alley.

The city gate is 3.1m wide, 4.5m high, and 6.6m thick, belonging to a stone-vaulted gate opening.

Perhaps due to its strategically dangerous terrain, easy to defend and difficult to attack, this gate did not have a barbican, and is a medium-small gate among the open gates.

Dongshui Gate was one of the old Chongqing water wharves; historically it was an important passage out of Chongqing City across the Yangtze River to the south bank, and also the only way to Guizhou and Yunnan.

By virtue of the water wharf advantage, this area was once one of the most prosperous commercial districts in the old city; on both sides of the bluestone steps leading to the water gate, shops, teahouses, inns, and taverns stood in great numbers.

This was also a guild hall concentration area; at that time there were eight major guild halls in Chongqing city, and three were concentrated here — namely the Jiangnan Guild Hall, Huguang Guild Hall, and Guangdong Guild Hall.

Later, because the water wharf moved to Wanglongmen, Dongshui Gate gradually declined.

Today, a Dongshui Gate Yangtze River Bridge spans the great river, replacing the water gate as the passage to the south bank.

The old city gate under the bridge has far left our sight; the old houses under the past city wall have been replaced by newly renovated black-tile white-wall antique buildings, surrounded by open and flat riverside roads, with cars speeding by from time to time, making it hard to imagine the past urban prosperity here.

Only the mottled traces exposed on the stone steps, trodden for years by the feet of coolies and boat passengers coming and going, emit the breath of time in the rainy season.

湖广会馆

Huguang Guild Hall
国家级 清 会馆
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address渝中区东水门正街4号
类型 Type会馆
看点 Highlights: 戏楼 封火墙 院落

中文描述 Description

在东水门向东南方向望去，不远处即是一大片古色古香的明清建筑——重庆湖广会馆建筑群。

会馆是各地客商按籍贯在某一地方设立的办事处。

过去人们出门在外，院里家乡亲友，遇事孤立无援，会馆则将一地的同乡同业者组织团结到一起，起到互帮互助、排难解纷的作用。

历史上重庆明清时期的商业繁盛，吸引了外地大量商人进入重庆市场，尤其是两广、两湖和山西、陕西、福建、江西、云贵等省的商人。

各商帮自乾隆时期就陆续在城里设立会馆。

昔日重庆城著名的八大会馆，都具有相当的规模和经济实力，它们是湖广会馆(又名禹王宫，在东水门内)、江西会馆(又名万寿宫，在东水门内)、广东会馆(又名南华宫)、陕西会馆(又名三元庙，在朝天门内)、福建会馆(又名天后宫，在陕西街)、云贵会馆(在绣壁街)、山西会馆(在人和湾)、同庆公所等。

当年的八大会馆中，建筑最宏伟气派的要数财力雄厚的湖广会馆和江西会馆。

这两大会馆和相毗邻的广东公所都在商业集中繁华的下半城的东水门内，形成庞大的建筑群，也就是今天我们所统称的湖广会馆建筑群。

如今参观湖广会馆，主要分为三部分：禹王宫，齐安公所，广东公所，另外还有两个博物馆：移民博物馆和匾额博物馆。

禹王宫即湖广会馆，由早期移民中的湖南、湖北富商、乡绅捐资兴建，始建于清乾隆二十四年(1759年)，因祀大禹故名禹王宫。

史料载湖广之名始于元代湖广行中书省，该省辖湖北、湖南全境及广东、广西部分。

明代设湖广布政使司时，只辖湖北、湖南两省了，且湖广之名沿用，实际上湖广仅指两湖之城了。

两湖之地水患严重，故有借禹王镇邪防灾的意思。

殿前三重飞檐直插云霄，动感非常。

正殿宽敞的天井前供奉着高大的禹王铜像，令人肃然起敬。

每年正月，这里都要举行盛大的禹王庙会，祭祀大禹以求平安，活动内容丰富多彩，影响范围较大，受到人民群众的喜爱，因此这一习俗被沿袭下来，成为饶有趣味的过年内容。

禹王宫大殿后面依山而上就是齐安公所和广东公所。

齐安公所又名帝王宫，祭祀主宰天宫地官水官之神的三元大帝，由湖北黄州府移民修建，始建于清嘉庆年间，目前保留下来的建筑为清光绪年间重建。

因为唐代湖北黄州一带曾设置过齐安郡，所以命名为齐安公所。

齐安公所的大门与传统会馆大门建在中轴线不同，位于建筑侧面，斜向东方，朝向移民的家乡湖北黄州府方向，既有风水的讲究，也寄托了移民对祖籍地的思乡之情。

广东公所又名南华宫，由广东移民捐资兴建。

广东公所现存主体结构呈四合院布局，入口大门为牌楼式，四柱三间五楼，各楼翘角飞檐，楼面房脊、瓦垅、滴水俱全，上有广东公所四个金灿灿的大字。

该会馆的后殿建筑在修建解放路小学时被拆除，叫人扼腕。

要解读湖广会馆的精致，离不开会馆中的戏楼。

禹王宫保留下的三面外伸的戏楼，两边有厢楼，专供贵宾、台下的场地供一般观众使用。

戏台两边供配乐人员使用的乐楼很小，檐下的额枋雕刻着各种鬼怪故事。

齐安公所的戏楼进深更大，专供贵宾的看厅在戏台的对面而不是两厢，乐楼也比禹王宫的大得多，额枋雕刻的内容已从鬼怪故事变为二十四孝图三国演义封神演义鱼樵图等，每个故事旁边都刻有寓意福气的蝙蝠、花草、瑞兽等。

广东公所的戏楼是四座戏楼中保存最好、最为气派精致的。

戏楼为木结构歇山式淡绿加黄色琉璃瓦顶，两侧耳楼为观戏楼厢，中为天井，后有看厅。

此看厅雕刻非常丰富，卷棚檐口下，四个撑拱的镂空戏雕精美绝伦，是极其珍贵的戏曲文物。

重庆戏曲在这一时期发展较快，当年的湖广会馆一年开戏200余次，差不多每两天就有一台戏看。

开戏的目的多为看戏娱神，无论官商公子、富家小姐，还是袍哥大爷、青楼名媛，三教九流，每到下午戌时，看客爆满，人声鼎沸。

湖广会馆的围墙样式，是明清时期常见的黄色封火墙，以直线构图而呈阶梯状叠落，又称码头墙，是典型的江南建筑风格。

从对岸远远望去，湖广会馆的建筑从山坡上直冲而下，围墙连绵不断，给人震撼的视觉冲击。

如今，无数的人们到这里寻根。

川流不息的游客将目光锁定在一件件文物上，顾盼流连，议论纷纷。

透过这些历尽沧桑的物品，人们仿佛看见了故土麻城的山岭，看见了八百里秦川，看见了洞庭湖上的帆影，看见了长江三峡的激流洪波，看见了漫长岁月里无数动人的故事，为之欣喜，为之感怀，为之拥有无穷无尽的力量。

英文翻译 English Translation

Looking southeast from Dongshui Gate, not far away is a large expanse of antique Ming-Qing buildings — the Chongqing Huguang Guild Hall building complex.

A guild hall was an office established by merchants from various places according to their native place in a certain location.

In the past, when people went out, away from home, with relatives and friends in their hometown, they were isolated and helpless in case of trouble; the guild hall organized and united fellow townsmen and fellow tradesmen from one place together, playing a role in mutual help and resolving disputes.

Historically, the commercial prosperity of Chongqing during the Ming-Qing period attracted a large number of merchants from other places to enter the Chongqing market, especially merchants from Guangdong and Guangxi, Hubei and Hunan, and Shanxi, Shaanxi, Fujian, Jiangxi, Yunnan and Guizhou provinces.

Various merchant groups successively established guild halls in the city from the Qianlong period.

The famous eight major guild halls of old Chongqing City all had considerable scale and economic strength; they were the Huguang Guild Hall (also called Yuwang Palace, inside Dongshui Gate), Jiangxi Guild Hall (also called Wanshou Palace, inside Dongshui Gate), Guangdong Guild Hall (also called Nanhua Palace), Shaanxi Guild Hall (also called Sanyuan Temple, inside Chaotian Gate), Fujian Guild Hall (also called Tianhou Palace, on Shaanxi Street), Yunnan-Guizhou Guild Hall (on Xiubi Street), Shanxi Guild Hall (in Renhewan), and Tongqing Public Office, etc.

Among the eight major guild halls of those days, the most grand and imposing buildings were the financially powerful Huguang Guild Hall and Jiangxi Guild Hall.

These two major guild halls and the adjacent Guangdong Public Office were all inside Dongshui Gate in the prosperous lower half city with concentrated commerce, forming a庞大 building complex, which is what we collectively call the Huguang Guild Hall building complex today.

Visiting Huguang Guild Hall today, it is mainly divided into three parts: Yuwang Palace, Qi'an Public Office, and Guangdong Public Office; in addition there are two museums: the Immigration Museum and the Plaque Museum.

Yuwang Palace is the Huguang Guild Hall, built with donations from wealthy merchants and gentry of Hunan and Hubei among the early immigrants, first built in the 24th year of Qianlong (1759), Qing; because it sacrifices to Yu the Great, it is named Yuwang Palace.

Historical records show that the name Huguang originated from the Huguang Branch Secretariat of Yuan dynasty, which governed the whole territory of Hubei and Hunan and parts of Guangdong and Guangxi.

When the Huguang Administrative Commissioner was established in Ming, it only governed Hubei and Hunan provinces, and the name Huguang continued to be used, actually Huguang only referred to the two Hubei and Hunan regions.

The two Hubei and Hunan regions had severe flood disasters, hence there was the meaning of borrowing Yu the Great to suppress evil and prevent disasters.

In front of the hall, three layers of flying eaves pierce straight into the sky, very dynamic.

In front of the spacious courtyard of the main hall, a tall bronze statue of Yu the Great is enshrined, making one feel awe-inspiring respect.

Every first lunar month, a grand Yuwang Temple Fair is held here, sacrificing to Yu the Great to seek peace; the activities are rich and colorful, with a large influence range, loved by the people, hence this custom has been passed down, becoming an interesting New Year content.

Going up the mountain behind the main hall of Yuwang Palace are the Qi'an Public Office and Guangdong Public Office.

Qi'an Public Office, also called Diwang Palace, sacrifices to the Three Great Emperors who rule the gods of heaven, earth, and water; built by immigrants from Huangzhou Prefecture, Hubei, first built during the Qing Jiaqing era, the currently preserved buildings were rebuilt during the Qing Guangxu era.

Because the area around Huangzhou, Hubei was once established as Qi'an Commandery in Tang dynasty, it was named Qi'an Public Office.

The gate of Qi'an Public Office differs from traditional guild hall gates built on the central axis; it is located on the side of the building, slanting toward the east, facing the direction of the immigrants' hometown Huangzhou Prefecture, Hubei — both having fengshui considerations and entrusting the immigrants' homesickness for their ancestral home.

Guangdong Public Office, also called Nanhua Palace, was built with donations from Guangdong immigrants.

The currently preserved main structure of Guangdong Public Office has a siheyuan layout; the entrance gate is in archway style, with four columns, three bays, and five stories; each story has upturned corners and flying eaves, with roof ridges, tile ridges, and drips all complete on the building surface, with the four glittering characters Guangdong Public Office on top.

The rear hall building of this guild hall was demolished when Jiefang Road Primary School was built, regrettable.

To interpret the exquisiteness of Huguang Guild Hall, one cannot do without the theater towers in the guild hall.

The three-sided outward-extending theater tower preserved by Yuwang Palace has wing towers on both sides, exclusively for distinguished guests; the area under the stage is for general audiences.

The music towers on both sides of the stage for accompaniment personnel are very small; under the eaves, the architraves are carved with various ghost and monster stories.

The theater tower of Qi'an Public Office has a greater depth; the viewing hall exclusively for distinguished guests is opposite the stage rather than on both sides, and the music tower is also much larger than that of Yuwang Palace; the content carved on the architraves has changed from ghost and monster stories to the Twenty-Four Filial Exemplars, Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Investiture of the Gods, Fisherman-Woodcutter Pictures, etc.; beside each story are carved bats, flowers and plants, and auspicious beasts symbolizing good fortune.

The theater tower of Guangdong Public Office is the best preserved and most imposing and exquisite among the four theater towers.

The theater tower is of timber structure with a xieshan-style light-green plus yellow glazed tile roof; the side ear towers on both sides are theater-viewing tower wings, with a courtyard in the middle and a viewing hall behind.

This viewing hall has very rich carvings; under the curved eave opening, the openwork theatrical carvings of the four supporting brackets are exquisite beyond compare, being extremely precious opera cultural relics.

Chongqing opera developed relatively fast during this period; in those days, Huguang Guild Hall held operas over 200 times a year, almost every two days there was an opera to watch.

The purpose of holding operas was mostly to watch operas and entertain the gods; whether official and merchant young masters, wealthy young ladies, or Paoge (brotherhood) masters, famous courtesans, people of all walks of life, every afternoon at the xu hour (7-9pm), the audience was packed and voices were bustling.

The wall style of Huguang Guild Hall is the yellow fire-sealing wall common in the Ming-Qing period, with straight-line composition presenting stepped cascading, also called wharf wall, a typical Jiangnan architectural style.

Viewed from afar on the opposite bank, the buildings of Huguang Guild Hall rush straight down from the hillside, with continuous walls, giving a shocking visual impact.

Today, countless people come here to seek their roots.

The endless stream of tourists locks their eyes on each cultural relic, looking around and lingering, discussing.

Through these weather-beaten objects, people as if see the mountains of their hometown Macheng, see the eight hundred li of Qinchuan, see the sail shadows on Dongting Lake, see the rapids and waves of the Three Gorges of the Yangtze, see countless moving stories in the long years, rejoicing for them, feeling for them, and possessing endless power from them.

东华观藏经楼

Depository of Scriptures of Donghua Taoist Temple
市级 明 宗教建筑
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty明
地址 Address渝中区凯旋路64号
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 木结构 琉璃瓦

中文描述 Description

自唐代开始，重庆曾经是道教的重点活动地区，留下了宝贵的道观文化遗迹。

在重庆市渝中区凯旋路上，就隐藏着这样一座距今已有700多年历史的道观遗迹——东华观藏经楼。

东华观始建于隋，其后多次重修。

明《蜀中名胜记》记载：城中有东华观，观后有东华十八洞，皆相通。

今土人呼其处为神仙口，相传东华真君于此得道。

可惜院中建筑多已毁坏，现仅存藏经阁。

据《重庆渝中区文史资料》记载，东华观藏经楼修建于元代，重建于明。

如今的藏经楼掩映于绿荫之下，整体构架破败不堪。

过去的琉璃瓦，在风吹雨打之下已呈青色。

檐角残缺不全，瓦当、木梁被腐蚀成了黑色，摇摇欲坠。

憔悴的外表之下还有它外的命运。

1939年，该楼被日军轰炸，内藏的部分经书及建筑被炸毁。

文革时期，楼内供奉的神像全部遭到毁坏。

1962年，该楼又突遭大火焚烧。

后来重庆印刷厂一一厂房逐渐占据了藏经楼正门，至今没有搬迁。

藏经楼现存建筑面积不到原先的三分之一。

过去东华观大门两侧有过这样一副对联：看涂山云影飞来无限天光供一府，问字水梅花开放几分春色到三巴。

风光已逝，空余此楼，如果没有人们的关注和保护，所有的记忆将和它一起，继续沉睡。

英文翻译 English Translation

Since Tang dynasty, Chongqing was once a key activity area for Daoism, leaving precious Taoist temple cultural relics.

On Kaixuan Road, Yuzhong District, Chongqing City, there hides such a Taoist temple ruin with a history of over 700 years — the Depository of Scriptures of Donghua Taoist Temple.

Donghua Taoist Temple was first built in Sui dynasty, and later rebuilt multiple times.

The Ming dynasty Scenic Spots of Shu records: In the city there is Donghua Taoist Temple; behind the temple there are eighteen Donghua caves, all connected.

Today locals call this place Shenxian (Immortal) Mouth; legend has it that the Donghua True Lord attained the Dao here.

Unfortunately, most of the buildings in the temple have been destroyed, and now only the Scripture Depository survives.

According to the Cultural and Historical Materials of Yuzhong District, Chongqing, the Scripture Depository of Donghua Taoist Temple was built in Yuan dynasty and rebuilt in Ming.

Today's Scripture Depository is hidden under green shade, with its overall frame in ruins.

The past glazed tiles have turned blue under wind and rain.

The eave corners are incomplete, and the tile ends and timber beams have corroded into black, crumbling.

Beneath its haggard appearance is also its external fate.

In 1939, this building was bombed by the Japanese army, and part of the scriptures and buildings stored inside were blown up.

During the Cultural Revolution, all the deity statues enshrined inside the building were destroyed.

In 1962, this building suddenly suffered a fire again.

Later, a factory building of Chongqing Printing Factory gradually occupied the main entrance of the Scripture Depository, and has not been relocated to this day.

The existing building area of the Scripture Depository is less than one-third of the original.

In the past, on both sides of the main gate of Donghua Taoist Temple there was such a couplet: Watching the cloud shadows of Tushan Mountain fly in, infinite heavenly light serves one prefecture; asking the plum blossoms of Zishui to bloom, how much spring color reaches the Three Ba.

The scenery has passed, leaving only this building; if there is no people's attention and protection, all memories will, together with it, continue to sleep.

弹子石摩崖造像

Danzishi Cliffside Statues
国家级 元—清 石刻
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty元—清
地址 Address南岸区弹子石街道德聚村1号
类型 Type石刻
看点 Highlights: 雕像 石窟寺

中文描述 Description

元末明初，红巾军将领明玉珍统一全川，国号大夏，定都重庆。

其时，传说长江岸边一座人头山有妖魔作怪，使得滩险浪急，船只时常触礁。

为镇压妖魔，明玉珍命大将邹兴在长江南岸凿石刻像，保佑船只平安。

这便是位于南岸区大佛鸿集村长江边上的临江大佛。

明永乐十九年(1421年)这里又凿造了五尊佛。

清代时，这里逐渐形成佛教寺院群落，气势恢宏。

英文翻译 English Translation

At the end of Yuan and beginning of Ming, Ming Yuzhen, a general of the Red Turban Army, unified all of Sichuan, with the state name Daxia, and made Chongqing the capital.

At that time, legend has it that a demon was causing trouble at a Human-Head Mountain on the bank of the Yangtze River, making the shoals dangerous and waves rapid, with ships often hitting reefs.

To suppress the demon, Ming Yuzhen ordered his great general Zou Xing to chisel stone statues on the south bank of the Yangtze River, to bless the safety of ships.

This is the riverside Great Buddha located on the edge of the Yangtze River in Dafo Hongji Village, Nan'an District.

In the 19th year of Yongle (1421), Ming, five more Buddha statues were chiseled here.

During Qing dynasty, a Buddhist temple complex gradually formed here, with grand momentum.

塔子山文峰塔

Wenfeng Pagoda of Tazishan
市级 清 砖石塔
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address江北区寸滩街道东北650米
类型 Type砖石塔
看点 Highlights: 双塔对峙 题刻 远眺

中文描述 Description

从前，取道水路坐船来的人，只要看见长江北岸塔子山上那个高耸挺拔的白塔，就知道重庆城到了。

此白塔便是江北塔子山文峰塔，因为南山的黄桷垭文峰塔在先，所以它也被称为寸滩塔。

它与黄桷垭文峰塔隔江遥相对峙，像一对兄弟镇守着重庆。

据《重修文峰塔记》载，此塔建于清光绪十四年(1888年)，为六角七层空心楼阁式砖塔。

塔身呈六角形，通高26.64米。

塔壁厚1.2米。

内阁七层，楼层已毁，逐层内收，各层开一窗，底层设门。

除底层用条石砌成外，以上六层均为青砖所砌，每块砖上都有文峰塔三字，塔身存裂纹。

门券刻大清光绪十四年戊子岁孟夏吉旦三里士民恭建等字样，门额匾刻繁体题名胜迹四字。

塔子山文峰塔的左右各架起一座气势如虹的大桥——大佛寺大桥与朝天门大桥；

长江、嘉陵江汇合处的重庆大剧院也可尽收眼底；

远处，渝中半岛上拔地而起的高楼，用无法抗拒的现代化气息，改变着人们关于这座城市的记忆。

幸好，这古塔仍在，静静地驻守着一段老城的回忆，使人们不致在城市的快速变化中迷失自己。

英文翻译 English Translation

In the past, people who came by boat via the water route, as soon as they saw the tall and upright White Pagoda on Tazi Mountain on the north bank of the Yangtze River, knew that Chongqing City had arrived.

This White Pagoda is the Wenfeng Pagoda of Tazi Mountain in Jiangbei; because the Wenfeng Pagoda at Huangjueya on South Mountain came first, it is also called the Cuntan Pagoda.

It faces the Wenfeng Pagoda at Huangjueya across the river from afar, like a pair of brothers guarding Chongqing.

According to the Record of Rebuilding Wenfeng Pagoda, this pagoda was built in the 14th year of Guangxu (1888), Qing; it is a hexagonal seven-story hollow pavilion-style brick pagoda.

The pagoda body is hexagonal, with a total height of 26.64m.

The pagoda wall is 1.2m thick.

The inner pavilion has seven stories; the floors have been destroyed, tapering inward layer by layer, each layer opens a window, and the bottom layer has a door.

Except for the bottom layer built of dressed stones, the above six layers are all built of grey bricks; each brick has the three characters Wenfeng Pagoda on it, and the pagoda body has cracks.

On the door arch are engraved characters such as Auspicious Day of Early Summer in the Wuzi Year, the 14th Year of Guangxu of the Great Qing, Respectfully Built by the Scholars and People of Three Li; on the door lintel plaque are engraved the four traditional characters of Title, Famous Scenic Spot.

On the left and right of the Wenfeng Pagoda of Tazi Mountain, there are each spanned a bridge with imposing momentum like a rainbow — the Dafo Temple Bridge and the Chaotian Gate Bridge; the Chongqing Grand Theater at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing Rivers can also be fully seen; in the distance, the high-rise buildings rising from the ground on the Yuzhong Peninsula, with an irresistible modern atmosphere, are changing people's memories about this city.

Fortunately, this ancient pagoda is still here, quietly guarding a memory of the old city, so that people do not lose themselves in the rapid changes of the city.

觉林寺报恩塔

Bao'en Pagoda of Juelin Temple
市级 清 砖石塔
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address南岸区下浩觉林寺街95号
类型 Type砖石塔
看点 Highlights: 塔形

中文描述 Description

报恩塔，又名下浩塔，位于南岸区下浩觉林寺街，是原觉林寺附属建筑。

觉林寺建于南宋绍兴年间，明末毁于兵火，清康熙二年(1663年)僧雪痕复建，清乾隆二十二年(1757年)僧月江增建石塔、山门等。

据《巴县志》记载，报恩塔是月江和尚为报母恩所建，但塔未成即圆寂，由其弟子善明续修，历16年完成。

此塔为八角九层空心楼阁式砖石塔，坐南向北，通高45米。

塔基每边长5.7米，前有垂带台阶2级。

塔身逐层内收，各层挑檐，并开窗、开门，有佛龛，塔身内外有多处石刻题记。

塔刹为攒尖葫芦宝顶，由金属铸成。

围垣门是一座小牌坊，上书报恩塔三字，两旁柱刻因传心法分三教，为建浮屠报四恩对联。

清代文人何彤云有一首《游览觉林寺》诗：一径入苍翠，寻幽来化城。

小池鱼可唤，深树鸟无名。

孤塔江中影，飞泉石上声。

僧闲能导客，筇履尽情行。

描写的便是100多年前的觉林寺。

新中国成立后，此处先后兴办了新华皮鞋、新民塑料厂、合成纤维厂。

为扩大厂址，佛祖菩萨塑像陆续被毁，所有亭阁殿堂面目全非，只剩下报恩塔一座旧迹。

文革期间，原寺址全部改成厂房、职工宿舍和居民住宅，塔也遭到破坏。

经1985年维修，目前保存状况较好，孤独地守望着这片曾经的神圣土地。

英文翻译 English Translation

Bao'en (Requiting Kindness) Pagoda, also called Xiahao Pagoda, is located on Juelin Temple Street, Xiahao, Nan'an District, and was an ancillary building of the original Juelin Temple.

Juelin Temple was built during the Southern Song Shaoxing era, destroyed by war and fire at the end of Ming, rebuilt by Monk Xuehen in the 2nd year of Kangxi (1663), Qing, and with the stone pagoda and mountain gate added by Monk Yuejiang in the 22nd year of Qianlong (1757), Qing.

According to the Ba County Annals, Bao'en Pagoda was built by Monk Yuejiang to requite his mother's kindness, but he passed away before the pagoda was completed; it was continued and finished by his disciple Shanming, taking 16 years to complete.

This pagoda is an octagonal nine-story hollow pavilion-style brick-stone pagoda, facing south, with a total height of 45m.

Each side of the pagoda base is 5.7m long, with 2垂带-style steps in front.

The pagoda body tapers inward layer by layer, with each layer having overhanging eaves, and opening windows and doors, with Buddhist niches; there are many stone inscriptions inside and outside the pagoda body.

The pagoda finial is a pyramidal gourd precious top, cast from metal.

The enclosure gate is a small archway, with the three characters Bao'en Pagoda written on it; on the pillars on both sides are engraved the couplet Because transmitting the mind-dharma divides three teachings, to build a stupa requites four kindnesses.

The Qing literatus He Tongyun has a poem Touring Juelin Temple: A path enters the verdant, seeking seclusion comes to the transformation city.

Small pool fish can be called, deep trees birds have no name.

Lonely pagoda shadow in the river, flying spring sound on stone.

Monk idle can guide guests, staff and shoes walk to their heart's content.

This describes Juelin Temple over 100 years ago.

After the founding of New China, Xinhua Leather Shoes, Xinmin Plastic Factory, and Synthetic Fiber Factory were successively established here.

To expand the factory site, the statues of Buddha and Bodhisattvas were successively destroyed, and all pavilions and halls were beyond recognition, leaving only the old trace of Bao'en Pagoda.

During the Cultural Revolution, the original temple site was all converted into factory buildings, staff dormitories, and residential houses, and the pagoda was also damaged.

After maintenance in 1985, it is currently in relatively good preservation condition, lonely watching over this once sacred land.

涂山寺

Tushan Temple
市级 清 宗教建筑
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address南岸区黄桷垭镇真武山15号
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 院落 诗词 古树

中文描述 Description

涂山寺高踞涂山之侧，回龙桥之上，四周古树参天，苍翠欲滴。

古往今来，涂山寺以名胜古刹闻名遐迩，朝山拜佛者和游客众多。

唐代著名诗人白居易，在任忠州(今忠县)刺史时，来到此地，写下一首《涂山寺独游》：野径行无伴，僧房宿无期。

涂山来路熟，唯是马蹄知。

传说此地为远古时代涂山氏族所居之地。

夏禹疏通九河时，到此娶涂山氏之女，四月后外出治水，三过家门而不入。

古人为了纪念夏禹治水功绩，在涂山顶建禹王祠涂后祠，祠内壁有夏禹和涂后像。

其后建为真武山，供奉真武祖师。

明永乐十一年(1413年)贵州铁瓦寺道洪、正旭二僧来广化寺(今老君洞)任住持，随后将广化寺与真武山进行置换，真武山改为佛教寺庙。

但因保持有道教的真武、祖师两殿，保留了真武寺的名称，山为真武山；

又因与禹王祠旧址合并，又有涂山寺之称谓。

整个庙分左右殿两部分，一为真武殿等属道教，一为大雄殿等属佛教，是佛道和睦共处的庙院。

现存多为清代建筑，飞檐翘角，宏伟壮观。

大雄殿又叫佛殿，供奉华严三圣。

1954年后改为密宗布喇供奉宗喀巴，叫宗喀巴殿。

殿前置有五尺长的大方形香炉一个、千斤重的大化钱炉一口，台阶上有石雕狮子一对，殿檐上悬国民革命陆军上将四川督军熊克武献立的大雄宝殿四个金字大匾一块。

大殿为悬山顶，脊饰宝瓶，两端鱼吻，姿态活泼。

1965年重庆市无线电一厂进驻庙内，把殿堂改为了车间或库房，1966年文革开始，庙内外碑记、石刻、佛像、雕塑、具有密宗布置特色的殿宇建筑、历史文物等悉被毁坏。

1984年1月，地方政府贯彻落实宗教政策，将房产发还给涂山寺。

1986年1月，经重庆市政府批准，修复开放涂山寺，经20余年修复，寺院面貌发生了很大变化，2000年列为重庆市文物保护单位，2014年列为国家级文物保护单位，继续吸引着善男信女与游人访客的到来。

英文翻译 English Translation

Tushan Temple perches high on the side of Tushan Mountain, above the Huilong Bridge, surrounded by ancient trees towering to the sky, verdant and dripping.

Through the ages, Tushan Temple has been famous far and wide as a famous scenic ancient temple, with many mountain-worshipping Buddhists and tourists.

The famous Tang poet Bai Juyi, when serving as the prefect of Zhongzhou (today's Zhongxian County), came to this place and wrote a poem Solo Tour of Tushan Temple: Wild path walks with no companion, monk room stays with no fixed date.

Tushan Mountain coming road familiar, only the horse's hooves know.

Legend has it that this place was the residence of the Tushan clan in ancient times.

When Xia Yu dredged the nine rivers, he came here and married the daughter of the Tushan clan; after four months he went out to control floods, passing his home three times without entering.

To commemorate Xia Yu's achievements in flood control, ancient people built the Yuwang Shrine and Tuhou Shrine on the top of Tushan Mountain, with statues of Xia Yu and Tuhou on the inner walls.

Later it was built as Zhenwu Mountain, enshrining the Zhenwu Patriarch.

In the 11th year of Yongle (1413), Ming, two monks Daohong and Zhengxu from the Iron Tile Temple in Guizhou came to Guanghua Temple (today's Laojun Cave) to serve as abbots, then exchanged Guanghua Temple with Zhenwu Mountain, and Zhenwu Mountain was converted to a Buddhist temple.

But because it retained the two Daoist halls of Zhenwu and Patriarch, it retained the name Zhenwu Temple, and the mountain is Zhenwu Mountain; also because it merged with the old site of Yuwang Shrine, it also has the appellation Tushan Temple.

The entire temple is divided into two parts, left and right halls: one is the Zhenwu Hall etc.

belonging to Daoism, and one is the Daxiong (Mahavira) Hall etc.

belonging to Buddhism — a temple where Buddhism and Daoism coexist harmoniously.

Most of the existing buildings are Qing dynasty, with flying eaves and upturned corners, grand and spectacular.

The Daxiong Hall is also called the Buddha Hall, enshrining the Three Sages of Huayan.

After 1954 it was changed to the Tantric Bula enshrining Tsongkhapa, called the Tsongkhapa Hall.

In front of the hall there is a five-chi-long square incense burner, a thousand-jin-large money-burning furnace, and a pair of stone-carved lions on the steps; on the hall eave hangs a large four-gold-character plaque of Daxiong Baodian (Mahavira Hall) presented and erected by Xiong Kewu, General of the National Revolutionary Army and Sichuan Military Governor.

The main hall has an overhanging gable roof, with a precious vase on the ridge and fish-shaped ornaments at both ends, with lively postures.

In 1965, Chongqing Radio Factory No.

1 moved into the temple, converting the halls into workshops or warehouses; in 1966, when the Cultural Revolution began, stele inscriptions, stone carvings, Buddha statues, sculptures, hall buildings with Tantric arrangement characteristics, and historical relics inside and outside the temple were all destroyed.

In January 1984, the local government implemented the religious policy and returned the property to Tushan Temple.

In January 1986, with the approval of the Chongqing Municipal Government, Tushan Temple was restored and opened; after over 20 years of restoration, the temple's appearance has undergone great changes.

In 2000 it was listed as a Chongqing Municipal Cultural Relics Protection Unit, and in 2014 it was listed as a National Cultural Relics Protection Unit, continuing to attract devout men and women and tourists and visitors.

黄桷垭文峰塔

Wenfeng Pagoda of Huangjueya
市级 清 砖石塔
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address南岸区黄桷垭街道文峰峰山
类型 Type砖石塔
看点 Highlights: 塔形 电影

中文描述 Description

重庆主城区的人都听说过三塔不相见的说法。

这三塔由北到南沿长江分布，分别是江北塔子山顶的文峰塔，下浩莲花山麓觉林寺中的报恩塔，以及南山上的黄桷垭文峰塔。

前文已经介绍过另外两座古塔，下面，就让我们来认识这三塔的最后一塔。

建成于清道光三十一年(1851年)的黄桷垭文峰塔是一座六角七层空心楼阁式砖塔，1986年、2008年有过两次维修。

砖塔通高24米，素面条石塔基，每边长3.28米。

塔身逐层内收，挑檐极富韵律，塔顶为六角攒尖葫芦顶。

塔内一、二层楼道为石梯，三至七层为木梯，但目前文峰塔已经不对外开放，不能进入。

真正使得黄桷垭文峰塔广为人知的是一部20世纪50年代的惊险小说《一双绣花鞋》。

这个故事发生在解放初期的重庆，黄桷垭文峰塔在其中扮演了重要的角色。

据其改编的电影、电视剧，都曾在文峰塔下取景拍摄。

英文翻译 English Translation

People in the main urban area of Chongqing have all heard of the saying that the three pagodas do not see each other.

These three pagodas are distributed along the Yangtze River from north to south, respectively the Wenfeng Pagoda on the top of Tazi Mountain in Jiangbei, the Bao'en Pagoda in Juelin Temple at the foot of Lianhua Mountain in Xiahao, and the Wenfeng Pagoda of Huangjueya on South Mountain.

The other two ancient pagodas have been introduced above; below, let us get to know the last of these three pagodas.

The Wenfeng Pagoda of Huangjueya, built in the 31st year of Daoguang (1851), Qing, is a hexagonal seven-story hollow pavilion-style brick pagoda; it underwent two repairs in 1986 and 2008.

The brick pagoda has a total height of 24m, with a plain dressed-stone pagoda base, each side 3.28m long.

The pagoda body tapers inward layer by layer, with overhanging eaves full of rhythm; the pagoda top is a hexagonal pyramidal gourd top.

Inside the pagoda, the corridors of the first and second layers are stone steps, and the third to seventh layers are wooden ladders; but currently the Wenfeng Pagoda is no longer open to the public and cannot be entered.

What really made the Wenfeng Pagoda of Huangjueya widely known is a thriller novel of the 1950s, A Pair of Embroidered Shoes.

This story took place in Chongqing in the early days of liberation, and the Wenfeng Pagoda of Huangjueya played an important role in it.

The movies and TV series adapted from it have all shot scenes under the Wenfeng Pagoda.

宝轮寺正殿

Main Hall of Baolun Temple
市级 明至今 宗教建筑
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty明至今
地址 Address沙坪坝区磁器口白岩山
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 木结构 斗拱 书法

中文描述 Description

宝轮寺位于重庆沙坪坝区磁器口古镇，坐落于嘉陵江畔、白岩山(也叫白崖山)上。

其始建年代有多种说法，有传说为唐朝时由尉迟恭主持修建，也有说是西魏年间(535—556年)所建，而官府所修的《巴县志》则称是宋真宗咸平年间(998—1003年)所建。

宝轮寺因山而初名白岩寺(或白崖寺)，明朝时成帝朱允炆被朱棣篡位，避难于此，白岩寺遂易名为龙隐寺。

清朝改为宝轮寺。

寺院在鼎盛时期有殿宇16座，佛像372尊，可惜殿宇毁于明末战火，近代又经日寇轰炸，只留下大雄宝殿和紧邻其后的药师殿。

重庆解放后办过校、住过居民，改革开放后政府拨款将其修缮，进行保护及重建工作，新建了川主殿、四面千手观音殿、天王殿、经楼和禅房等建筑。

寺院于1988年对外开放，再续千年盛景。

如今宝轮寺山门邻街，外面是热闹的磁器口古街，里边台阶之上是一块书有龙隐禅院的石牌坊，原物毁于明末战火，现在看到的是改革开放后仿制之物。

寺庙正殿为大雄宝殿，为明宣德七年(1432年)所建，占地约400平方米。

殿坐南向北，面阔三间、进深三间、高15米，重檐歇山琉璃瓦顶，屋顶脊饰轻盈起翘，檐下斗拱玲珑透漏，整体风格古朴精致。

大殿为全木结构建筑，殿柱粗壮，两人也不能合抱。

大雄宝殿牌匾上四个大字为著名书法家赵朴初所题。

如今来此参拜的多为游览磁器口古镇的游客，虽然大殿前的香火台常年香火不断，但了解这里历史的人已经不多了。

英文翻译 English Translation

Baolun Temple is located in the ancient town of Ciqikou, Shapingba District, Chongqing, situated by the Jialing River and on Baiyan Mountain (also called Baiya Mountain).

There are various sayings about its founding date; some legends say it was presided over and built by Yuchi Gong in Tang dynasty, some say it was built during the Western Wei period (535-556), while the officially compiled Ba County Annals say it was built during the Song Zhenzong Xianping era (998-1003).

Baolun Temple was initially named Baiyan Temple (or Baiya Temple) after the mountain; in Ming dynasty, when Emperor Chengdi Zhu Yunwen was usurped by Zhu Di and took refuge here, Baiyan Temple was renamed Longyin (Dragon-Hidden) Temple.

In Qing dynasty it was changed to Baolun Temple.

In its heyday, the temple had 16 halls and 372 Buddha statues; unfortunately, the halls were destroyed in the war fires at the end of Ming, and in modern times it was bombed by the Japanese army, leaving only the Mahavira Hall and the Medicine Buddha Hall adjacent behind it.

After Chongqing's liberation, schools were run and residents lived here; after the reform and opening up, the government allocated funds to repair it, carrying out protection and reconstruction work, newly building halls such as the Chuanzhu Hall, Four-Faced Thousand-Armed Guanyin Hall, Heavenly Kings Hall, scripture tower, and meditation rooms.

The temple opened to the public in 1988, continuing its thousand-year prosperity.

Today, the mountain gate of Baolun Temple is adjacent to the street; outside is the bustling Ciqikou ancient street, and inside above the steps is a stone archway inscribed with Longyin Chan Courtyard; the original was destroyed in the war fires at the end of Ming, and what is seen now is an imitation after the reform and opening up.

The main hall of the temple is the Mahavira Hall, built in the 7th year of Xuande (1432), Ming, covering about 400 sq m.

The hall faces south, 3 bays wide, 3 bays deep, 15m high, with double-eave xieshan glazed tile roof; the roof ridge ornaments are lightly upturned, and the bracket sets under the eaves are exquisite and openwork, with an overall style simple and refined.

The main hall is an all-timber structure building; the hall columns are sturdy, and two people cannot wrap their arms around them.

The four large characters on the plaque of the Mahavira Hall were inscribed by the famous calligrapher Zhao Puchu.

Today, most of those who come to worship here are tourists visiting the ancient town of Ciqikou; although the incense burner in front of the main hall has constant incense year-round, not many people understand the history here.

盘溪无铭阙

Wuming Tower in Panxi
市级 东汉 石阙
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty东汉
地址 Address江北区石马河盘溪香炉湾石门街道500米
类型 Type石阙
看点 Highlights: 汉阙 雕刻

中文描述 Description

盘溪和嘉陵江交接的地方有一高丘，叫作香炉湾，这里有着重庆最为古老的石刻艺术品——无铭阙。

因阙身无铭文，故名无铭阙，也称香炉石。

建于东汉晚期，属墓阙。

左阙早塌，残石存重庆中国三峡博物馆，现存右阙，坐东向西，通高4.15米。

石阙分为阙基、阙身和仿木楼部三部分。

阙基为单层实质，表面朴素。

阙身为单一石块刻成，高2.26米，下宽1.15米，上宽0.80米，下部进深0.64米，上部进深0.54米。

四角有隐柱形，左侧面刻有浮雕白虎衔璧，右侧面则是女娲捧月。

上部仿木结构由四层构成，刻有护斗、枋子、角神鸳鸯交手拱等元素，形态丰富。

文保机构于20世纪80年代已建亭保护阙，亭身较为封闭，慕名而来的人们只能从窗子外观看石阙。

据附近居民介绍，这一带正大力开发房地产，可能会搬迁石阙进入新建好的小区内。

英文翻译 English Translation

At the place where Panxi meets the Jialing River there is a high hill called Xiangluwan (Incense Burner Bay), where there is Chongqing's oldest stone carving artwork — the Wuming (Uninscribed) Tower.

Because the tower body has no inscription, it is named Wuming Tower, also called Incense Burner Stone.

Built in the late Eastern Han, it belongs to a tomb tower.

The left tower collapsed early, and the remnant stone is stored in the Chongqing China Three Gorges Museum; the existing right tower faces west, with a total height of 4.15m.

The stone tower is divided into three parts: tower base, tower body, and imitation-timber section.

The tower base is a single-layer solid mass, with a plain surface.

The tower body is carved from a single stone block, 2.26m high, 1.15m wide at the bottom, 0.80m wide at the top, 0.64m deep at the lower part, and 0.54m deep at the upper part.

At the four corners there are hidden column shapes; on the left side is carved a relief of a White Tiger holding a jade disk, and on the right side is Nüwa holding the moon.

The upper imitation-timber structure consists of four layers, carved with elements such as bracket blocks, lintels, corner deities, and mandarin-duck hand-in-hand bracket sets, with rich forms.

The cultural relic protection institution built a pavilion to protect the tower in the 1980s; the pavilion body is relatively enclosed, and people who come especially to see it can only view the stone tower from outside the window.

According to nearby residents, this area is vigorously developing real estate, and the stone tower may be relocated into a newly built residential community.

华岩寺

Huayan Temple
市级 清 宗教建筑
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address九龙坡区华岩镇华岩村
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 华岩洞天 院落 寺内藏品 宗教文化

中文描述 Description

华岩寺历史悠久，规模宏大，为西南十大丛林之一，有巴山灵境之称。

始建于明万历二十七年(1599年)，后多次重修、扩修，现存建筑为清代遗构，由华岩洞、华岩寺、接引殿，以及北侧新建的七佛塔等独立院落组成，总建筑面积8280平方米，为重庆市内最大的佛教禅院。

华岩洞庙又称小寺，为华岩寺之祖庙，位于南部。

传说盛唐时期，有僧依岩结庵修行，名华严，久之讹称华岩。

明万历及清同治两次重修，现存上、下两殿，依山崖而建，有着神秘的宗教氛围。

清时圣可大师任住持，授徒传戒讲学，另于对面山地建设华岩寺，即今日的大寺。

华岩寺坐北朝南，中轴线上分布有天王殿、大雄宝殿、圣祖可祖师堂、观音堂，两侧绕长廊。

其中，大雄宝殿四根通天中柱每颗长达十几米，重数十吨，极为壮观。

接引殿位于大寺东北侧，建于清道光五年(1825年)，坐西向东，四合院布局。

中轴线上依次有放生池、牌坊、前殿(大门)、正殿(三圣殿)。

牌坊上的石刻造像栩栩如生。

英文翻译 English Translation

Huayan Temple has a long history and large scale, being one of the Ten Great Monasteries in Southwest China, known as the Bashan Spiritual Realm.

It was first built in the 27th year of Wanli (1599), Ming, and later rebuilt and expanded multiple times; the existing buildings are Qing dynasty surviving structures, composed of independent courtyards such as the Huayan Cave, Huayan Temple, Jieyin (Receiving and Guiding) Hall, and the newly built Seven-Buddha Pagoda on the north side, with a total building area of 8,280 sq m, making it the largest Buddhist monastery in Chongqing.

The Huayan Cave Temple, also called the Small Temple, is the ancestral temple of Huayan Temple, located in the south.

Legend has it that during the High Tang period, a monk built a thatched hut by the cliff for practice, named Huayan; over time it was mispronounced as Huayan.

It was rebuilt twice in Ming Wanli and Qing Tongzhi; the existing upper and lower halls are built against the cliff, with a mysterious religious atmosphere.

In Qing dynasty, Master Shengke served as abbot, teaching disciples, transmitting precepts, and giving lectures; he separately built Huayan Temple on the opposite mountain land, which is today's Great Temple.

Huayan Temple faces south; on the central axis are distributed the Heavenly Kings Hall, Mahavira Hall, Shengzu Ke Patriarch Hall, and Guanyin Hall, with long corridors on both sides.

Among them, the four sky-reaching central columns of the Mahavira Hall are each over ten meters long and weigh dozens of tons, extremely spectacular.

The Jieyin Hall is located on the northeast side of the Great Temple, built in the 5th year of Daoguang (1825), Qing, facing east, with a siheyuan layout.

On the central axis are sequentially the Free Life Pond, archway, front hall (main gate), and main hall (Three Sages Hall).

The stone-carved statues on the archway are lifelike.

塔坪寺塔

Pagoda of Taping Temple
市级 南宋 砖石塔
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty南宋
地址 Address北碚区静观镇塔坪村
类型 Type砖石塔
看点 Highlights: 宋塔 园林 轴线

中文描述 Description

塔坪寺始建于南宋绍兴十六年(1146年)，原名小昆仑古藏寺。

经明万历四十年(1612年)重修，改称塔坪寺。

清嘉庆二十四年(1819年)后再次重修。

布局沿袭中原唐以后已经失传的以塔为中心的格局，中轴线上依次排列山门、宋塔、大雄殿、藏经楼、后殿等建筑，结构古朴。

寺中耸立的宋代石塔，享有朝天文笔插空稳，拔地楼阁依势牢的赞誉。

石塔建于南宋乾道丁亥年(1167年)，为方形楼阁式砖结构空心塔，高14.4米，底边周长6.2米。

塔身逐层内收，四角屋檐上挑。

塔身四周有用各种彩色瓷片镶成而成的图案，内容为动物、花卉等，造型生动。

塔内有17尊浮雕神像，以及历代游人留书，极为珍贵。

塔中狭窄的斜式石梯上下连通，可助人登上塔顶远眺。

寺内还存有明清石坊、清代铁塔、经幢、华表等文物。

伴随其间的是遍布四处的参天古木与园林花草，它们给予寺院特有的清净氛围，亦成塔坪寺胜景之一。

英文翻译 English Translation

Taping Temple was first built in the 16th year of Shaoxing (1146), Southern Song, originally named Xiao Kunlun Ancient Cang Temple.

After being rebuilt in the 40th year of Wanli (1612), Ming, it was renamed Taping Temple.

It was rebuilt again after the 24th year of Jiaqing (1819), Qing.

Its layout follows the pagoda-centered pattern that has been lost in the Central Plains after Tang; on the central axis are sequentially arranged the mountain gate, Song pagoda, Mahavira Hall, scripture tower, rear hall, and other buildings, with a simple and unsophisticated structure.

The Song stone pagoda standing in the temple enjoys the praise of The heavenly writing brush pierces the sky steadily, the ground-pulled pavilion relies on the terrain firmly.

The stone pagoda was built in the Dinghai year of Qiandao (1167), Southern Song; it is a square pavilion-style brick-structure hollow pagoda, 14.4m high, with a bottom perimeter of 6.2m.

The pagoda body tapers inward layer by layer, with the four-corner eaves upturned.

Around the pagoda body there are patterns inlaid with various colored porcelain pieces, with contents of animals, flowers and plants, etc., with vivid modeling.

Inside the pagoda there are 17 relief deity statues, as well as inscriptions left by tourists of various dynasties, extremely precious.

The narrow slanted stone steps inside the pagoda connect up and down, helping people climb to the top of the pagoda to look into the distance.

The temple also preserves cultural relics such as Ming-Qing stone archways, Qing iron pagoda, stone pillars (jingchuang), and ornamental columns (huabiao).

Accompanying them are towering ancient trees and garden flowers and plants spread everywhere; they give the temple its unique pure atmosphere, and also become one of the scenic spots of Taping Temple.

温泉寺

Wenquan Temple
市级 明 宗教建筑
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty明
地址 Address北碚区澄江镇北温泉内
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 木结构 院落 山势 园林

中文描述 Description

重庆以山城著称于世，也是俗称长江三大火炉之一。

因夏季炎热，人们纷纷向郊外寻找清凉避暑之地，其中，北温泉便是人们的首选。

北温泉人文景观众多，以温泉寺最负盛名。

温泉寺创建于南朝刘宋景平元年(423年)，最初是缙云寺的下院，南齐中设东阳郡后，寺内香火兴旺，庙宇广大。

后经北周武帝和唐武宗两次灭佛，遭受严重破坏。

唐贞观时期重建庙宇，并在后山岩间刻摩崖佛像。

北宋景德四年(1007年)，温泉寺受朝廷封赐为崇胜禅院。

据说，南宋开庆元年(1259年)蒙哥大汗于钓鱼城被炮火击中，于此寺中病逝。

此后，崇胜禅院因山岩崩塌而毁坏，明代迁现址重建。

目前整个建筑群占地4200平方米，总建筑面积800余平方米。

各殿宇依山而建，层层叠落，与自然环境和谐并存。

寺内有四座殿堂为明代遗构，依次为关圣殿、接引殿、大佛殿、观音殿。

关圣殿也是山门，面积137平方米，小青瓦单檐屋面，民居风格强烈。

接引殿面积173平方米，抬梁式木构架，重檐歇山顶，琉璃瓦屋面。

殿后有一山泉细流汇成的方池，池上石桥栏杆上刻有麒麟、芭蕉及花鸟等图案，皆为明代遗存。

大佛殿面积200余平方米，重檐歇山顶，小青瓦屋面，装修华丽，脊饰精致。

压轴的是观音殿，因其屋面为金属瓦盖，也称铁瓦殿，整体造型简洁古朴。

四大殿周围有古香园、石刻园、观鱼池、乳花洞、五潭印月等景点。

其中古香园为崇胜禅院旧址，园中植物繁茂，古木参天，存有宋、明、清三代僧人墓塔。

石刻园内有宋、明、清等三代多处石碑，部分宋石刻极为珍贵。

英文翻译 English Translation

Chongqing is known to the world as a Mountain City, and is also commonly called one of the Three Great Furnaces along the Yangtze.

Because of the hot summer, people go to the suburbs one after another to find cool summer retreats; among them, the North Hot Spring is people's first choice.

The North Hot Spring has many cultural landscapes, with Wenquan (Hot Spring) Temple being the most famous.

Wenquan Temple was founded in the 1st year of Jingping (423) of Liu Song, Southern Dynasties; originally it was the lower courtyard of Jinyun Temple.

After Dongyang Commandery was established in the middle of Southern Qi, the temple's incense flourished and the temple buildings were vast.

Later, after two Buddhist persecutions by Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou and Emperor Wuzong of Tang, it suffered severe damage.

During the Tang Zhenguan era, the temple buildings were rebuilt, and cliffside Buddha statues were carved in the rocks of the back mountain.

In the 4th year of Jingde (1007), Northern Song, Wenquan Temple was bestowed by the court as the Chongsheng Chan Courtyard.

It is said that in the 1st year of Kaiqing (1259), Southern Song, the Great Khan Möngke was hit by cannon fire at Diaoyu City and died of illness in this temple.

Thereafter, the Chongsheng Chan Courtyard was destroyed due to mountain rock collapse, and was rebuilt at the current site in Ming.

At present, the entire building complex covers 4,200 sq m, with a total building area of over 800 sq m.

Each hall is built according to the mountain, cascading layer by layer, coexisting harmoniously with the natural environment.

There are four halls in the temple that are Ming dynasty surviving structures, sequentially the Guansheng (Holy Lord Guan) Hall, Jieyin (Receiving and Guiding) Hall, Dafo (Great Buddha) Hall, and Guanyin Hall.

The Guansheng Hall is also the mountain gate, with an area of 137 sq m, small grey tile single-eave roof, with a strong folk-house style.

The Jieyin Hall has an area of 173 sq m, with a抬梁式 (beam-lifting) timber frame, double-eave xieshan roof, and glazed tile roof.

Behind the hall there is a square pool formed by a mountain spring trickle; on the stone bridge railings over the pool are carved patterns of qilin, banana, flowers and birds, etc., all Ming dynasty remains.

The Dafo Hall has an area of over 200 sq m, with double-eave xieshan roof, small grey tile roof, ornate decoration, and exquisite ridge ornaments.

The finale is the Guanyin Hall; because its roof is covered with metal tiles, it is also called the Iron Tile Hall, with an overall shape simple and unsophisticated.

Around the four halls there are scenic spots such as the Ancient Fragrance Garden, Stone Carving Garden, Fish-Viewing Pond, Ruhua Cave, and Five Pools Reflecting the Moon.

Among them, the Ancient Fragrance Garden is the old site of the Chongsheng Chan Courtyard; in the garden plants are luxuriant and ancient trees tower to the sky, preserving monk tomb pagodas of Song, Ming, and Qing dynasties.

In the Stone Carving Garden there are many stone steles of Song, Ming, Qing and other dynasties, and some Song stone carvings are extremely precious.

缙云寺

Jinyun Temple
市级 清 宗教建筑
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address北碚区缙云山
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 木结构 照壁 石牌坊 迦叶古佛

中文描述 Description

缙云古名巴山，因山间常常白云缭绕，早晚间在阳光照射下呈现缤纷色彩，古人称赤多白少为缙，由此得名缙云山。

位于山间的缙云寺始建于刘宋景平元年(423年)，后曾受到历代帝王封赐。

唐名禅宫相思寺，宋改崇胜寺，明为崇教寺，明万历三十年(1602年)神宗皇帝改名为缙云寺，沿用至今。

明末寺庙破败，清康熙二十二年(1683年)由破空大师重建。

缙云寺占地面积2000平方米，坐西北向东南，现存山门、大雄殿、后殿、厢房等建筑。

由于缙云寺为国内唯一的迦叶古佛道场，所以大雄殿里供奉的佛像不是释迦牟尼佛，而是迦叶古佛。

该古佛立于康熙22年，高约两米，左右是大梵天、帝释天等清代塑像。

缙云寺前有青石雕石照壁，高4.0米，宽4.0米，有专家认为是晚唐文物。

石照壁正中为芭蕉麒麟图，图案古朴雅致。

石照壁之上有一座石牌坊，高6米，宽5米，由青石砌成。

坊正面刻有明神宗朱翊钧御笔迦叶道场，背面为明成祖朱棣所题缙云胜境。

坊前有石雕青狮一对，高1.70米，形态勇猛威武。

缙云云寺自古办学，名为缙云书院。

1930年秋，中国佛教协会会长太虚法师在此创建世界佛学苑汉藏教理院，曾培养出如赵朴初等大批佛教人才，被誉为川东佛教圣地。

缙云寺与温泉寺、绍隆寺、白云寺、石华寺、复兴寺、大隐寺、转龙寺并称缙云山八大寺庙。

古寺名山，千年道场，至今仍然吸引大量游客观赏。

英文翻译 English Translation

Jinyun Mountain was anciently called Bashan Mountain; because white clouds often wind around the mountain, presenting colorful hues under sunlight in the morning and evening, ancient people called much red and little white as jin (red silk), hence the name Jinyun Mountain.

Jinyun Temple, located in the mountains, was first built in the 1st year of Jingping (423) of Liu Song, and later received bestowals from emperors of various dynasties.

In Tang it was named the Chan Palace Xiangsi (Lovesickness) Temple; in Song it was changed to Chongsheng Temple; in Ming it was Chongjiao Temple; in the 30th year of Wanli (1602), Ming, Emperor Shenzong renamed it Jinyun Temple, which is still used today.

At the end of Ming the temple fell into disrepair; in the 22nd year of Kangxi (1683), Qing, it was rebuilt by Master Pokong.

Jinyun Temple covers an area of 2,000 sq m, facing southeast from the northwest; the existing buildings include the mountain gate, Mahavira Hall, rear hall, and wing rooms.

Because Jinyun Temple is the only ashram of the ancient Buddha Kasyapa in China, the Buddha statue enshrined in the Mahavira Hall is not Sakyamuni Buddha, but the ancient Buddha Kasyapa.

This ancient Buddha was erected in the 22nd year of Kangxi, about 2m high, with Qing dynasty statues of Great Brahma, Indra, etc.

on the left and right.

In front of Jinyun Temple there is a bluestone-carved stone screen wall, 4.0m high and 4.0m wide; some experts believe it is a late Tang cultural relic.

In the center of the stone screen wall is a Banana-Qilin pattern, with a simple and elegant design.

Above the stone screen wall there is a stone archway, 6m high and 5m wide, built of bluestone.

On the front of the archway is engraved the imperial brush of Emperor Shenzong Zhu Yijun of Ming: Kasyapa Ashram; on the back is inscribed Jinyun Scenic Realm by Emperor Chengzu Zhu Di of Ming.

In front of the archway there is a pair of stone-carved blue lions, 1.70m high, with brave and mighty forms.

Jinyun Temple has run schools since ancient times, named Jinyun Academy.

In the autumn of 1930, the president of the Chinese Buddhist Association, Master Taixu, founded the Han-Tibetan Buddhist Institute of the World Buddhist Academy here, which trained a large number of Buddhist talents such as Zhao Puchu, and is known as the Buddhist Holy Land of Eastern Sichuan.

Jinyun Temple, together with Wenquan Temple, Shaolong Temple, Baiyun Temple, Shihua Temple, Fuxing Temple, Dayin Temple, and Zhuanlong Temple, are called the Eight Great Temples of Jinyun Mountain.

Ancient temple and famous mountain, a thousand-year ashram, still attracts a large number of tourists to visit today.

多功城

Duogong Town
市级 南宋 堡垒
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty南宋
地址 Address渝北区鸳鸯镇翠云街道花朝村西1公里
类型 Type堡垒
看点 Highlights: 城墙遗迹

中文描述 Description

提到重庆的古城堡，大家第一个想到的或许是钓鱼城。
