事实上，除了合川钓鱼城外，南宋末年，川渝地区还修建了江北多功城、泸州神臂岩、金堂云顶山、苍溪大获城、南充青居城、万县天生城等多座城池，形成一道三江八柱防御体系，共同抵御蒙古军的入侵。

其中，重庆江北的翠云山作为战略要地，是南宋末年重庆军民坚持抗元斗争的重要据点，因为屡立战功，山上的城寨由朝廷赐名多功。

据民国《江北厅志》载，该城建于南宋淳祐年间(1127—1278年)，清咸丰三年(1853年)曾补修。

平面形状呈椭圆形，东西长70—100米、南北宽200米，占地面积约1.3万平方米。

现存石砌城墙、石券东城门和西城门。

城墙残长700米，厚3.7米，存高6米。

西城门高2.8米，宽1.9米，进深3.7米。

门洞呈双券拱状，券拱顶部条石上刻有南宋题记端明殿学士大中大夫四川安抚制置大使朱禩孙建。

从西城门进城，即可看到翠云寺遗址。

史料记载，翠云寺建于1021年，比多功城的历史还要早。

不过，寺庙早已破败，铁门紧锁。

抗战期间，不少的大学纷纷迁往重庆。

多功城也被用作学校校址，即江北县女中部。

曾有七八百学生在此就读，建有礼堂等建筑若干。

今天大多建筑已然无存，仅留下古树若干，碧水一池，低声讲述古城数百年的故事。

英文翻译 English Translation

Mentioning Chongqing's ancient castles, the first thing everyone thinks of may be Diaoyu City.

In fact, besides Diaoyu City in Hechuan, at the end of Southern Song, the Sichuan-Chongqing region also built many cities such as Duogong Town in Jiangbei, Shenbi Rock in Luzhou, Yunding Mountain in Jintang, Dahuocheng in Cangxi, Qingjucheng in Nanchong, and Tianshengcheng in Wanxian, forming a Three Rivers Eight Pillars defense system to jointly resist the invasion of the Mongol army.

Among them, Cuiyun Mountain in Jiangbei, Chongqing, as a strategic location, was an important stronghold for Chongqing's military and civilians to persist in the struggle against the Yuan at the end of Southern Song; because of repeated meritorious service, the mountain fortress was bestowed the name Duogong (Many Merits) by the court.

According to the Republic-era Jiangbei District Annals, this city was built during the Southern Song Chunyou era (1127-1278), and was repaired in the 3rd year of Xianfeng (1853), Qing.

Its planar shape is elliptical, 70-100m long east-west, 200m wide north-south, covering an area of about 13,000 sq m.

The existing stone city wall, stone-vaulted east city gate, and west city gate remain.

The city wall has a remnant length of 700m, is 3.7m thick, and has a surviving height of 6m.

The west city gate is 2.8m high, 1.9m wide, and 3.7m deep.

The gate opening is in a double-vaulted arch shape; on the dressed stones at the top of the vault arch are engraved the Southern Song inscription: Built by Zhu Sisun, Duanming Hall Scholar, Grand Master of the Palace, Sichuan Pacification and Military Governor.

Entering the city from the west gate, one can see the ruins of Cuiyun Temple.

Historical records show that Cuiyun Temple was built in 1021, earlier than the history of Duogong Town.

However, the temple has long been dilapidated, with its iron door locked.

During the War of Resistance, many universities moved to Chongqing one after another.

Duogong Town was also used as a school site, namely the Girls' Middle School Department of Jiangbei County.

Once seven or eight hundred students studied here, with several buildings such as an auditorium built.

Today most buildings no longer exist, leaving only several ancient trees and a pool of clear water, quietly telling the story of the ancient city for hundreds of years.

白帝城

Baidi Town
国家级 明—清 建筑群、木结构
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address奉节县白帝镇白帝村1社
类型 Type建筑群、木结构
看点 Highlights: 诗词 三国文化 夔门景色 碑刻

中文描述 Description

白帝城位于瞿塘峡西口的长江北岸，雄奇壮丽的自然景色和著名的历史典故让白帝城素来为诗家青睐。

李白、杜甫、白居易、苏东坡等都曾登临白帝城，留下大量脍炙人口的诗篇。

朝辞白帝彩云间，千里江陵一日还。

两岸猿声啼不住，轻舟已过万重山。

李白的这首诗奠定了许多孩子对于白帝城的第一印象。

白帝城的历史可追溯到西汉末年。

公孙述占据蜀地，自封为白帝，修筑白帝城，时为军政要塞。

述死后，当地人建白帝庙祭奠他。

三国时期，刘备兵败退守白帝城，在此建永安宫，于宫内托孤诸葛亮，这便是三国史上有名的白帝托孤。

后因三国的故事广为流传，自明代之后逐渐形成了白帝庙内只祭祀蜀汉人物而不见白帝踪影的局面。

如今白帝城的主要建筑就是白帝庙。

占地面积约2600平方米，坐北朝南。

传统合院式布局，由东、中、西三品院落组成。

中轴线上依次排列着山门、托孤堂、明良殿等。

明良殿始建于明代，采用抬梁式梁架，硬山顶，殿内供奉着刘、关、张和诸葛亮的彩色塑像。

明良殿西侧为武侯祠，祠内供奉的是诸葛亮及其子孙的塑像，以感念诸葛家族对蜀所做的巨大贡献。

武侯祠前有六角形观星亭，攒尖式屋顶。

亭内的石桌、石墩上镌刻着唐代诗人杜甫在夔州写下的脍炙人口的诗篇《秋兴八首》，诗意浓厚。

东西院建于清代，现内存有从隋至清的70多通碑刻，统称为碑林。

其中不乏《龙山公墓志铭》《金轮寺舍利塔铭》等具有重要历史价值的隋代碑刻。

无论是想雄霸天下的公孙述，还是怀着遗憾死去的刘备，又或是曾在此遇赦而心情大好的李白，都已化为了历史的尘埃。

但如今站在这里，面对着眼前滔滔的江水和险峻的峭壁，仿佛能真切地感受到前人的无奈、痛苦或欢愉。

英文翻译 English Translation

Baidi (White Emperor) Town is located on the north bank of the Yangtze River at the west mouth of Qutang Gorge; its magnificent natural scenery and famous historical allusions have long made Baidi Town favored by poets.

Li Bai, Du Fu, Bai Juyi, Su Dongpo, etc.

all once climbed Baidi Town, leaving a large number of well-loved poems.

Leaving at dawn from Baidi among colored clouds, a thousand li to Jiangling is returned in one day.

The apes on both banks keep crying without stopping, the light boat has already passed ten thousand mountains.

This poem by Li Bai established many children's first impression of Baidi Town.

The history of Baidi Town can be traced back to the late Western Han.

Gongsun Shu occupied the Shu region, proclaimed himself White Emperor, and built Baidi Town, which was then a military and political fortress.

After Shu's death, locals built the White Emperor Temple to worship him.

During the Three Kingdoms period, Liu Bei, after defeat, retreated to Baidi Town, built the Yong'an Palace here, and entrusted his orphan to Zhuge Liang inside the palace — this is the famous Baidi Orphan Entrustment in Three Kingdoms history.

Later, because the Three Kingdoms story spread widely, after Ming dynasty a situation gradually formed where only Shu-Han figures were worshipped in the White Emperor Temple, with no trace of the White Emperor.

Today the main building of Baidi Town is the White Emperor Temple.

It covers an area of about 2,600 sq m, facing south.

It has a traditional courtyard layout, composed of east, central, and west three courtyards.

On the central axis are sequentially arranged the mountain gate, Orphan-Entrustment Hall, Mingliang Hall, etc.

Mingliang Hall was first built in Ming, using a beam-lifting frame, with a flush gable roof; inside the hall are enshrined colored statues of Liu, Guan, Zhang, and Zhuge Liang.

To the west of Mingliang Hall is the Wuhou (Marquis of Wu) Shrine, inside which are enshrined statues of Zhuge Liang and his descendants, to感念 the great contributions of the Zhuge family to Shu.

In front of the Wuhou Shrine there is a hexagonal Star-Observing Pavilion, with a pyramidal roof.

On the stone table and stone stools inside the pavilion are engraved the well-loved poem Eight Autumn Meditations written by the Tang poet Du Fu in Kuizhou, with strong poetic flavor.

The east and west courtyards were built in Qing; currently they preserve over 70 stele carvings from Sui to Qing, collectively called the Stele Forest.

Among them there are Sui dynasty steles with important historical value such as the Epitaph of Lord Longshan and the Relic Pagoda Inscription of Jinlun Temple.

Whether it was Gongsun Shu who wanted to dominate the world, Liu Bei who died with regret, or Li Bai who was in a great mood after being pardoned here, they have all turned into the dust of history.

But standing here today, facing the surging river water and the steep cliffs in front of us, as if one can truly feel the helplessness, pain, or joy of predecessors.

瞿塘峡摩崖题刻

Cliffside Carving of Qutang Gorge
国家级 宋代—近代 摩崖题刻
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty宋代—近代
地址 Address奉节县瞿塘峡南岸白盐山西侧
类型 Type摩崖题刻
看点 Highlights: 石刻 书法

中文描述 Description

瞿塘峡全长八公里，是三峡中最短却最为雄伟的一个。

尤其是西端入口处的夔门，两岸峭壁耸峙，中间宽不及百米，形同门户。

杜甫曾有诗云：众水会涪万，瞿塘争一门。

道出了夔门天下雄的气势。

瞿塘峡北岸为赤甲山，南岸为白盐山，由于碳酸盐岩质附于岩壁表面，岩壁呈灰白色而得名。

在白盐山西侧180余米长的岩壁上，排列着从南宋至民国时期的十三幅碑刻，皆为阴刻。

这些碑刻同八百多年风云变幻的历史一样，内容十分丰富，字体也涉及楷、隶、草、篆等多种风格。

其中最著名的是刻于南宋乾道七年(1171年)的《皇宋中兴圣德颂》，这是最早的一幅题刻。

全文980字，记载了南宋高宗禅位于孝宗一事，赞颂了高宗的美德。

楷书略带行草风味，是南宋著名书法家赵公硕的手迹。

除了颂德之作，题刻中也不乏对夔门自然景观的赞美，如明代诗人沈庆的《赋瞿塘上峡》；

有面对胜景生发的思古之幽情，如《白帝城怀古》；

有从侧面反映近代军阀混乱争战史实的，如马林所书七律诗；

还有表达抗日救国豪情的，如爱国将领冯玉祥将军的踏出夔巫，打走倭寇打出夔门去等。

清代著名书法家刘心源所书夔门二字，古朴苍劲，别具一格；

张伯翔所书瞿塘二字则秀润沉着，也是难得的书法精品。

想着能得一叶扁舟，泛于江上，一边感受这自然峡谷的壮美，一边如欣赏这历代题刻，倘不尽意，靠岸登临，一探究竟，罢了再乘小舟同夕阳携手归去，任那一笔一捺的余味伴着云霞缭绕，必是人间一大美事啊！

英文翻译 English Translation

Qutang Gorge has a total length of 8 km, being the shortest but most magnificent of the Three Gorges.

Especially at the west entrance, the Kuimen (Kuimen Gate), with steep cliffs towering on both banks, the middle is less than 100m wide, shaped like a gate.

Du Fu once wrote a poem: All waters meet at Fu and Wan, Qutang contends for one gate.

This expresses the momentum of Kuimen being the most majestic gate under heaven.

The north bank of Qutang Gorge is Chijia Mountain, and the south bank is Baiyan (White Salt) Mountain; because carbonate rock material adheres to the cliff surface, the cliff is grayish-white, hence the name.

On the over-180m-long cliff on the west side of Baiyan Mountain, thirteen stele carvings from Southern Song to Republic period are arranged, all in intaglio.

These stele carvings, like the over 800 years of changing history, have very rich content, and the calligraphy styles also involve regular, clerical, cursive, seal, and other styles.

Among them, the most famous is the Ode to the Holy Virtue of the Restoration of the Great Song, carved in the 7th year of Qiandao (1171), Southern Song, which is the earliest inscription.

The full text has 980 characters, recording the abdication of Emperor Gaozong of Southern Song to Emperor Xiaozong, praising the virtues of Gaozong.

The regular script has a slight running-cursive flavor, being the handwriting of the famous Southern Song calligrapher Zhao Gongshuo.

Besides works praising virtue, the inscriptions also include praises of the natural landscape of Kuimen, such as the Ming poet Shen Qing's Ode to the Upper Gorge of Qutang; there are nostalgic feelings for the past aroused by facing the scenic beauty, such as Meditating on the Past at Baidi Town; there are those reflecting from the side the chaotic warfare history of modern warlords, such as the seven-character regulated poem written by Ma Lin; and there are those expressing the lofty sentiments of resisting Japan and saving the nation, such as the patriotic General Feng Yuxiang's Step out of Kui-Wu, Beat Away the Japanese Pirates and Go out through Kuimen, etc.

The two characters Kuimen written by the famous Qing calligrapher Liu Xinyuan are simple, vigorous, and unique; the two characters Qutang written by Zhang Boxiang are elegant, moist, and composed, also being rare fine calligraphy works.

Imagine getting a small boat, floating on the river, while feeling the magnificence of this natural gorge, while appreciating these inscriptions of various dynasties; if not fully satisfied, dock and climb to explore, then take the small boat back hand in hand with the setting sun, letting the lingering flavor of each stroke accompany the clouds and mist — it must be a great joy in the world!

磐石城

Panshi Fortress
市级 南宋 堡垒
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty南宋
地址 Address重庆市云阳县双江镇爱国村
类型 Type堡垒
看点 Highlights: 寨门 城楼 军事防御

中文描述 Description

早在唐代，磐石城已是屯兵之处。

唐代宗永泰元年(765年)，杜甫从成都举家东迁，途经云阳时曾作《将晓二首》，其中石城除击柝，铁锁欲开关。

鼓角悲荒塞，星河落九天等诗句，描写的就是磐石城军营黎明时的景象。

南宋淳祐年间，四川安抚处置使余阶率四川中路军民抵抗蒙古军入侵，他依照因山为垒，棋布星分的守备战略，在长江、嘉陵江沿线及一些交通要冲建造完善了15处寨堡，成为抗击蒙古大军的战略防御要点。

磐石城是万州天生城防御体系的重要支点，由余阶部将吕师夔在此驻守，成功抗击蒙古军侵犯，使得磐石城名声大振。

磐石城又名大石城，因为形如巨大磨盘，也称作磨盘寨。

城外四面均为绝壁，唯独山顶地面平坦，总面积约3.5万平方米。

磐石城有前后两寨门，前寨门在偏东方向，门前左方绝壁上镌有磐石城三个颜体大字，右方石壁上镌有清许缵曾的《磐石城记》，已斑驳不能辨认。

寨门由巨石砌筑，厚重坚固，其上设有警楼、炮位等军事防御设施。

后门形制与前门相同，寨门上锈迹斑驳的虎头铁环，造型相当凶猛威武。

元代，寨中曾建有昙华寺。

清雍正、乾隆年间，此地为私人所占，分属谭、柳二姓。

乾隆五十四年(1789年)，涂怀安购得，在城中扩修寨墙，整修寨门，增设枪眼、炮洞。

同时修建房屋数百间，将涂姓人家全部迁至寨上居住，使之成为涂氏一族聚居要塞。

清末民初，名儒涂凤书于此修建祠堂，并作家谱，留有张作霖、阎锡山等民国名人的题序。

今天磐石城中已无人居住，而是辟为景点，因其险要山势与雄奇建筑而成为云阳重要的旅游景点。

英文翻译 English Translation

As early as Tang dynasty, Panshi Fortress was already a place for stationing troops.

In the 1st year of Yongtai (765) of Emperor Daizong of Tang, Du Fu moved his family east from Chengdu; when passing Yunyang he wrote Two Poems at the Approach of Dawn, among which verses such as The stone city removes the night watchman's clapper, the iron lock is about to open the gate.

Drums and horns mourn the desolate frontier, the stars and river fall from the ninth heaven describe the scene at dawn of the Panshi Fortress military camp.

During the Southern Song Chunyou era, Yu Jie, the Sichuan Pacification and Administration Commissioner, led the Sichuan Middle Route military and civilians to resist the Mongol army invasion; he followed the defense strategy of using mountains as fortresses, distributed like chess pieces and stars, and built and improved 15 fortresses along the Yangtze and Jialing Rivers and at some traffic hubs, becoming strategic defense points against the Mongol army.

Panshi Fortress was an important fulcrum of the Tianshengcheng defense system in Wanzhou; it was garrisoned here by Yu Jie's subordinate general Lü Shikui, who successfully resisted the Mongol army's invasion, making Panshi Fortress's reputation soar.

Panshi Fortress is also called Dashi (Great Stone) City; because it is shaped like a huge millstone, it is also called Mopan (Millstone) Fortress.

Outside the fortress all four sides are sheer cliffs, only the mountaintop ground is flat, with a total area of about 35,000 sq m.

Panshi Fortress has front and rear two fortress gates; the front fortress gate is in the偏 east direction; on the sheer cliff to the left in front of the gate are engraved the three large Yan-style characters Panshi City; on the stone wall to the right is engraved the Record of Panshi City by Xu Zanzeng of Qing, already mottled and unrecognizable.

The fortress gate is built of huge stones, heavy and solid, on which are set military defense facilities such as watchtowers and artillery positions.

The rear gate has the same shape as the front gate; the rusty tiger-head iron rings on the fortress gate have a quite fierce and mighty shape.

In Yuan dynasty, the Tanhua Temple was once built in the fortress.

During Qing Yongzheng and Qianlong eras, this place was privately occupied, belonging to the Tan and Liu surnames.

In the 54th year of Qianlong (1789), Tu Huai'an purchased it, expanded and repaired the fortress wall in the city, renovated the fortress gate, and added gun holes and cannon holes.

At the same time, hundreds of houses were built, and all the Tu surname people were moved to live on the fortress, making it a gathering fortress for the Tu clan.

At the end of Qing and beginning of Republic, the famous scholar Tu Fengshu built an ancestral hall here and wrote a family genealogy, preserving prefaces by Republic-era celebrities such as Zhang Zuolin and Yan Xishan.

Today no one lives in Panshi Fortress; it has been opened as a scenic spot, becoming an important tourist attraction in Yunyang due to its dangerous mountain terrain and magnificent architecture.

张桓侯庙

Zhang Huanhou's Shrine
国家级 清 宗教建筑
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address重庆市云阳县盘石镇龙宝村狮子岩下
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 园林 题刻 搬迁

中文描述 Description

张飞，字益德，三国时期蜀汉名将。

驻守阆中时闻关羽死讯，急令部将范疆、张达为兄报仇，不料反被暗害。

二人取其首级投奔东吴，行至云阳，闻吴蜀讲和，便将其首级抛弃江中，为一渔翁捕鱼时打捞上岸，埋葬于飞凤山麓，世人在此立庙纪念。

这便是最早的张飞庙，因为后主刘禅追谥其为桓侯，故也称张桓侯庙，但最广为人知的名称仍然是张飞庙。

经宋、元、明、清历代扩建，张飞庙迄今已有1700多年历史，庙宇多为1870年水患后重建。

因三峡工程建设，作为库区唯一一个远距离整体搬迁的文物单位，张飞庙闭馆拆迁，溯江而上30公里，由飞凤山搬迁至盘石镇龙安村。

2003年7月19日搬旧如旧的新张飞庙正式开馆，与云阳新县城隔江相望，相映增辉。

张飞庙充分利用地形地貌，依山而建，临江迎风。

庙前石壁上刻江上风清四个大字，气势磅礴，天下闻名。

庙内建筑主要有七座，其中正殿、旁殿、结义楼、望云轩、助风阁、得月亭和杜鹃亭为主要建筑。

英文翻译 English Translation

Zhang Fei, courtesy name Yide, was a famous general of Shu-Han during the Three Kingdoms period.

When garrisoning Langzhong, upon hearing the news of Guan Yu's death, he urgently ordered his subordinates Fan Jiang and Zhang Da to avenge his brother; unexpectedly he was assassinated instead.

The two took his head and defected to Eastern Wu; when reaching Yunyang, hearing that Wu and Shu had made peace, they threw his head into the river; it was salvaged ashore by a fisherman while fishing, and buried at the foot of Feifeng Mountain; people built a shrine here to commemorate him.

This is the earliest Zhang Fei Temple; because the later lord Liu Shan posthumously honored him as Huanhou, it is also called Zhang Huanhou's Shrine, but the most widely known name remains Zhang Fei Temple.

Through expansions in Song, Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties, Zhang Fei Temple has a history of over 1,700 years to date; most of the temple buildings were rebuilt after the flood disaster of 1870.

Due to the construction of the Three Gorges Project, as the only cultural relic unit in the reservoir area to be relocated as a whole over a long distance, Zhang Fei Temple closed for demolition and relocation, going 30 km upstream, relocated from Feifeng Mountain to Long'an Village, Panshi Town.

On July 19, 2003, the new Zhang Fei Temple, relocated as old as old, officially opened, facing the new Yunyang county town across the river, enhancing each other's splendor.

Zhang Fei Temple fully utilizes the terrain and landforms, built against the mountain, facing the river and wind.

On the stone wall in front of the temple are engraved the four large characters Clear Wind Above the River, with majestic momentum, famous under heaven.

The temple mainly has seven buildings, among which the main hall, side hall, Sworn-Brotherhood Tower, Wangyun (Cloud-Gazing) Pavilion, Zhufeng (Wind-Assisting) Pavilion, Deyue (Moon-Gaining) Pavilion, and Dujuan (Cuckoo) Pavilion are the main buildings.

彭氏宗祠

Peng's Ancestral Hall
国家级 清 祠堂
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address重庆市云阳县里市乡黎明村
类型 Type祠堂
看点 Highlights: 城堡 院落 雕刻 书画

中文描述 Description

彭氏宗祠又名彭家楼子，是渝东地区仅有的一座保存完整的晚清封建地主庄园。

清乾隆中叶，湖北省武昌府大冶县水灾连连，当地人彭光奎听闻渝东一带十分富庶，便孤身入川，定居云阳，开设一家酿酒作坊，购得当地刘姓老屋。

而后，其子彭宗义持家有道，在当地富甲一方。

清道光二十五年(1845年)，家道中兴的彭氏家族大兴土木，开始修建彭氏宗祠，历时20年，于同治三年(1864年)建成。

该祠坐西向东，占地3500平方米，建筑面积2561平方米，为封闭型城堡复式四合院布局，由前门厅、正门厅、享殿、戏楼、天井、城墙、围墙、厢房、箭楼及四角炮楼组成。

院中心石木结构的九级楼阁通高37米，下部六层为石砌体，厚重朴实，上部为三重檐四角盔顶木构，轻巧灵动。

整个建筑高耸宏大，兼具古朴与精巧，是极为少见的砖石木构混合建筑，是云阳县一心两翼的重点人文景观之一。

彭氏宗祠是祠堂与坞堡结合的群体建筑，集祭祀、防护、住宿为一体，体现了移民氏族聚居建筑的独特性。

祠内现存近代书画石刻13通。

是研究晚清川东民居建筑风格和造型艺术的重要文物史料。

英文翻译 English Translation

Peng's Ancestral Hall, also called Peng Family Tower, is the only well-preserved late-Qing feudal landlord manor in the eastern Chongqing region.

In the mid-Qianlong era of Qing, Daye County, Wuchang Prefecture, Hubei Province, suffered successive floods; local Peng Guangkui heard that the eastern Chongqing area was very prosperous, so he entered Sichuan alone, settled in Yunyang, opened a wine-making workshop, and purchased the old house of the local Liu surname.

Later, his son Peng Zongyi managed the family well, becoming the richest in the area.

In the 25th year of Daoguang (1845), Qing, the Peng family, with its family fortunes revived, undertook large-scale construction and began building Peng's Ancestral Hall, taking 20 years and completed in the 3rd year of Tongzhi (1864).

This ancestral hall faces east, covering 3,500 sq m, with a building area of 2,561 sq m; it has a closed castle-type compound siheyuan layout, composed of the front gate hall, main gate hall, offering hall, theater tower, courtyard, city wall, enclosure wall, wing rooms, arrow tower, and four-corner gun towers.

The nine-story pavilion of stone-timber structure in the center of the courtyard has a total height of 37m; the lower six stories are of stone masonry, heavy and plain, and the upper part is a triple-eave four-corner helmet-top timber structure, light and agile.

The entire building is towering and grand, combining simplicity and exquisiteness; it is an extremely rare mixed brick-stone-timber building, and is one of the key cultural landscapes of the One Center Two Wings of Yunyang County.

Peng's Ancestral Hall is a group building combining an ancestral hall and a fortress (wubao), integrating sacrifice, protection, and accommodation, reflecting the uniqueness of immigrant clan settlement architecture.

Inside the hall there are 13 modern painting-calligraphy stone carvings preserved.

It is important cultural relic material for studying the residential architectural style and plastic arts of eastern Sichuan in the late Qing.

天生城

Tiansheng Fortress
国家级 南宋—清 古战场遗址、城墙、石结构
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty南宋—清
地址 Address万州区天城镇流水村
类型 Type古战场遗址、城墙、石结构
看点 Highlights: 古城墙 山水风光

中文描述 Description

万州天生城又名天子城，与合川钓鱼城一样，同为南宋抗金遗址。

但天生城这一名字却起源于三国，相传刘备伐吴时曾屯兵于此，故名天子城。

南宋淳祐二年，余玠任四川安抚制置使时，迁万州州治于此，并借助山势修建堡垒，成为抵抗蒙古大军的坚固据点。

后蒙军将其占领后并没有毁城，而是继续沿用。

清朝初年，川东抗清三谭之一的谭宏也曾据守其上，足见天生城所具备的极高军事价值。

天生城城垣位于海拔450米的山顶上，平面呈月牙形，由巨石砌筑，极为坚固。

此山南北走向，长约1.5公里，山势险峻，东西均为绝壁，仅一条小路可从中通行。

现存有石砌城墙三层，石阶梯数百级。

第一道城门前，立有一牌，上书全民健身登山步道几个大字。

往上攀登，一路上碰见许多老老少少、男男女女，一副不到山顶非好汉的架势，才知此言不虚。

沿着石阶走到中段，城墙早已不见踪影，而是竹影森森，农田叠叠，屋舍交错，典型的山间农家景象。

这是此山最宽、最平坦的一段。

再往后走，道路渐窄，两旁峭壁渐露，又有了城墙遗迹。

站在山顶俯瞰城区，江水，高楼，群山，和谐地交织在一起，这是长江旁的山城重庆特有的景色。

往山下走，在后城门处偶遇一个拄拐的少女，沿着山路艰难地向上攀登。

据文献记载，天生城内尚存宋代题刻多则和至元十三年(1276年)宣相杨公攻取万州之记碑一则。

不知隐藏在何处，寻访未得见，估计有缘人才有幸一睹吧。

英文翻译 English Translation

Tiansheng (Heaven-Born) Fortress in Wanzhou is also called Tianzi (Son-of-Heaven) City; like Diaoyu City in Hechuan, it is likewise a Southern Song anti-Jin (anti-Mongol) site.

But the name Tiansheng City originated from the Three Kingdoms; legend has it that when Liu Bei invaded Wu, he stationed troops here, hence the name Tianzi City.

In the 2nd year of Chunyou, Southern Song, when Yu Jie served as Sichuan Pacification and Military Governor, he moved the Wanzhou prefectural seat here and built a fortress using the mountain terrain, becoming a strong point resisting the Mongol army.

Later, after the Mongol army occupied it, they did not destroy the city but continued to use it.

At the beginning of Qing, Tan Hong, one of the Three Tans resisting Qing in eastern Sichuan, also garrisoned and defended it, sufficient to show the extremely high military value of Tiansheng City.

The city wall of Tiansheng City is located on the mountaintop at an altitude of 450m; its plane is crescent-shaped, built of huge stones, extremely solid.

This mountain runs north-south, about 1.5 km long, with steep mountain terrain; both east and west are sheer cliffs, with only a small path passing through the middle.

The existing remains include three layers of stone city wall and hundreds of stone steps.

In front of the first city gate, there stands a sign with the large characters National Fitness Mountain-Climbing Trail.

Climbing upward, along the way one meets many old and young, men and women, with an attitude of not being a true man until reaching the mountaintop, only then knowing this saying is not false.

Walking along the stone steps to the middle section, the city wall has long disappeared; instead there are dense bamboo shadows, layered farmland, and interleaved houses — a typical mountain farmhouse scene.

This is the widest and flattest section of this mountain.

Walking further back, the road gradually narrows, and steep cliffs gradually appear on both sides, with city wall remains again.

Standing on the mountaintop overlooking the city, the river water, high-rise buildings, and mountains are harmoniously intertwined — this is the unique scenery of the mountain city Chongqing beside the Yangtze River.

Walking down the mountain, at the rear city gate one encounters a young girl on crutches,艰难地 climbing upward along the mountain road.

According to literature records, inside Tiansheng City there remain many Song dynasty inscriptions and a stele of the Record of Lord Yang, Xuanxiang, Capturing Wanzhou in the 13th year of Zhiyuan (1276).

It is unknown where they are hidden; a search did not find them, presumably only those with good fortune have the chance to catch a glimpse.

梁平文峰塔

Wenfeng Pagoda in Liangping
市级 清 砖石塔
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address梁平县双桂街道青竹村
类型 Type砖石塔
看点 Highlights: 传说 高度

中文描述 Description

文峰塔位于梁平县双桂街道，共11层，高35.68米，是仅次于福建泉州石塔的全国第二高石塔。

石塔始建于清道光七年(1827年)，初名文风塔，光绪年间进行过一次历时10年之久的维修，竣工后更名为文峰塔。

清代徐名湘在《重建考棚并建塔记》一文中记载了文峰塔的来源。

时有当地乡绅捐资修建考棚，剩余银两4700余两。

后来大家商议后决定用这些银两在县城北门外修建高塔，搭配风水，并用于鼓励后学科甲蝉联，文章报国，当有理学名儒，继瞿唐先生而起，为梓里光者，文峰塔由此而来。

文峰塔为楼阁式塔，用质地坚硬的青砂石精细叠砌而成，塔身逐层收分明显，整体呈锥状。

塔基呈八边形，每边长4.71米。

底层门两侧镌刻灵秀文明草书大字。

各层错落开有拱形窗洞。

最令人印象深刻的当属那起翘的檐角。

每层八个角都高高向上翘起，为坚固沉稳的石塔增加了轻盈灵动之感。

顶层檐角本来各挂有一个铜铃，今已不复存在。

第十层正面刻有文峰二字，笔迹遒劲有力。

塔顶攒尖，有宝珠刹。

塔内原有的梯道被毁，后来修建了一到十层的木楼道供人攀登。

关于文峰塔，后世百姓在不清楚其修建缘由的情况下，凭借着超凡的想象力流传过一些风水之说。

原来梁平境内西山与四川大竹交界，西山山岭交错，似一狐狸。

狐狸头朝东，尾朝西，嘴巴正好对着产粮的梁平大坝，不免有吃梁平面肥大竹的嫌疑。

因此梁平人在此修建了高大的文峰塔，望它能撑住那贪吃的狐狸的嘴巴。

这一民间笑谈生动地体现了文峰塔的雄伟形象，有几分意思。

英文翻译 English Translation

Wenfeng Pagoda is located in Shuanggui Subdistrict, Liangping County, with 11 stories and a height of 35.68m; it is the second tallest stone pagoda in the country, second only to the stone pagoda in Quanzhou, Fujian.

The stone pagoda was first built in the 7th year of Daoguang (1827), Qing, initially named Wenfeng (Literary Style) Pagoda; during the Guangxu era it underwent a repair lasting 10 years, and after completion it was renamed Wenfeng (Literary Peak) Pagoda.

The Qing scholar Xu Mingxiang recorded the origin of Wenfeng Pagoda in his article Record of Rebuilding the Examination Shed and Building the Pagoda.

At that time, local gentry donated to build an examination shed, with over 4,700 taels of silver remaining.

Later, after discussion, everyone decided to use this silver to build a high tower outside the north gate of the county seat, to complement fengshui, and to encourage later scholars to have consecutive examination successes, serve the country with their writings, and that there should be famous Neo-Confucian scholars rising after Mr.

Qutang, bringing glory to their hometown — hence Wenfeng Pagoda.

Wenfeng Pagoda is a pavilion-style pagoda, finely stacked and built of hard bluestone; the pagoda body has obvious tapering layer by layer, overall in a conical shape.

The pagoda base is octagonal, each side 4.71m long.

On both sides of the bottom-layer gate are engraved the large cursive characters Lingxiu (Spiritually Beautiful) and Wenming (Civilized).

Each layer has arched window openings staggered.

The most impressive are the upturned eave corners.

Each layer's eight corners are all highly upturned, adding a light and agile feeling to the solid and steady stone pagoda.

The top-layer eave corners originally each had a copper bell hanging, which no longer exist today.

On the front of the 10th layer are engraved the two characters Wenfeng, with vigorous and powerful handwriting.

The pagoda top is pyramidal, with a precious pearl finial.

The original ladder inside the pagoda was destroyed; later, a wooden staircase from the 1st to 10th layer was built for people to climb.

Regarding Wenfeng Pagoda, later generations of common people, without knowing the reason for its construction, spread some fengshui tales with extraordinary imagination.

Originally, in Liangping, the West Mountain borders Dazhu, Sichuan; the West Mountain ridges are intertwined, resembling a fox.

The fox head faces east, tail faces west, and its mouth is exactly facing the grain-producing Liangping Great Plain, inevitably suspected of eating Liangping and fattening Dazhu.

Therefore, the people of Liangping built the tall Wenfeng Pagoda here, hoping it could prop open the mouth of that gluttonous fox.

This folk joke vividly reflects the majestic image of Wenfeng Pagoda, somewhat interesting.

双桂堂

Shuangguitang Temple
国家级 清 宗教建筑
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address梁平县金带镇双桂村
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 禅宗文化 雕刻 彩绘 佛寺组图

中文描述 Description

双桂堂由著名僧人破山创立于清顺治十年(1653年)，其名字起源于其内所植两株桂树。

相传这两株桂树为嫦娥亲手栽培，在一个中秋之夜被送往人间，落在宁波天童寺院内。

密云法师命弟子破山将这两株桂树带回蜀中，在桂树生根之处建寺传法。

破山遵命入蜀，一日行至万竹山，半夜正打坐之时，忽见桂树已落地生根，霎时霞光万丈，异象丛生。

于是破山便在这里建立禅院，取名双桂。

想象力丰富的传说自然不可全信，但它体现的双桂堂在民间百姓心中的神圣地位却颇符合实际。

破山禅师一生培育弟子一百余人，后来这些弟子分赴四川、云南、贵州、陕西乃至东南亚等地建寺传法，为西南地区汉传佛教的发展做出了重大贡献，双桂堂也因此有西南禅宗祖庭之称。

它不是简单的寺庙，而是培养了一大批佛法传播者的大学堂。

双桂堂规模颇大，建筑面积达1.1万平方米。

合院式布局。

沿着中轴线依次排列着关圣殿、放生池、弥勒殿、大雄宝殿、戒堂、破山塔、大悲殿、藏经楼等。

放生池上两座石拱桥，雕刻精美。

大雄宝殿建于清顺治十年(1653年)，气势恢宏，面阔五间、进深四间、三重檐歇山顶。

石柱间挂满吊着穗儿的红色祈愿符，里面有虔诚的信客们最美好的愿望，散发出浓厚暖意，为庄严的大雄宝殿平添了几分人情味。

离开轴线从侧门走出重重院落，在一片开阔地中这四方重檐、体量巨大的罗汉堂显得格外有震慑力。

我正在犹豫是否进去时天空突然洒下一阵大雨，逼得我慌忙往里躲。

刚进去便被惊了一跳——大大小小许多个彩绘罗汉列满了整个大厅，其中不乏瞠目怒视者，着实生动得吓人，我只得心惊肉跳地默求宽恕惊扰之罪了。

双桂堂内长廊厢房与殿堂相连，花圃水池与天井相辅，于威严肃穆中透露出人世情怀，兼有重要的历史渊源，也难怪其香火不断、游人不绝了。

英文翻译 English Translation

Shuangguitang (Double-Osmanthus) Temple was founded by the famous monk Poshan in the 10th year of Shunzhi (1653), Qing; its name originates from the two osmanthus trees planted inside.

Legend has it that these two osmanthus trees were personally cultivated by Chang'e (the Moon Goddess), and on one Mid-Autumn night were sent to the human world, landing in the courtyard of Tiantong Temple in Ningbo.

Master Miyun ordered his disciple Poshan to bring these two osmanthus trees back to Shu (Sichuan), and to build a temple and transmit the Dharma where the osmanthus trees took root.

Poshan obeyed the order and entered Shu; one day when he reached Wanzhu Mountain, in the middle of the night while sitting in meditation, he suddenly saw the osmanthus trees had landed and taken root, instantly with rays of auspicious light soaring to the sky and strange phenomena sprouting everywhere.

So Poshan built a Chan monastery here, named Shuanggui (Double Osmanthus).

The imaginative legend naturally cannot be fully believed, but the sacred status of Shuangguitang in the hearts of ordinary people that it reflects is quite in line with reality.

Chan Master Poshan cultivated over a hundred disciples in his lifetime; later these disciples went separately to Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, Shaanxi and even Southeast Asia to build temples and transmit the Dharma, making major contributions to the development of Han Chinese Buddhism in the Southwest region; hence Shuangguitang also has the title of Ancestral Hall of Chan Buddhism in the Southwest.

It is not a simple temple, but a great academy that cultivated a large number of Dharma disseminators.

Shuangguitang is quite large in scale, with a building area of 11,000 sq m.

It has a courtyard layout.

Along the central axis are sequentially arranged the Guansheng (Holy Lord Guan) Hall, Free Life Pond, Maitreya Hall, Mahavira Hall, Precept Hall, Poshan Pagoda, Great Compassion Hall, and Scripture Library.

On the Free Life Pond there are two stone arch bridges, exquisitely carved.

The Mahavira Hall was built in the 10th year of Shunzhi (1653), Qing, with imposing momentum, 5 bays wide, 4 bays deep, and triple-eave xieshan roof.

Between the stone columns hang red prayer charms with tassels, containing the best wishes of devout believers, exuding a strong warmth, adding a touch of human warmth to the solemn Mahavira Hall.

Leaving the central axis and walking out of the layers of courtyards through a side door, in an open area this four-sided double-eave, huge-volume Arhat Hall appears particularly imposing.

I was hesitating whether to go in when the sky suddenly poured down a heavy rain, forcing me to hurriedly take shelter inside.

Just as I entered I was startled — large and small many painted arhats filled the entire hall, among them there were no lack of those glaring with wide eyes, truly vivid and frightening; I had to, with a pounding heart, silently beg forgiveness for the sin of disturbing them.

In Shuangguitang, long corridors and wing rooms are connected with the halls; flower beds, ponds, and courtyards complement each other; amidst majesty and solemnity it reveals human feelings, and it also has important historical origins — no wonder its incense is constant and tourists are endless.

石宝寨

Shibaozhai Camp
国家级 清 城寨
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address忠县石宝镇西60米玉印山
类型 Type城寨
看点 Highlights: 倚山楼阁 穿斗式结构 山水景致

中文描述 Description

传说女娲补天时遗留下一块五彩石，落到了忠县境内。

不过这石头并未幻化成公子哥，而是在距县城45公里处的长江北岸生了根，成为一座孤零零的山崖，人称石宝。

明朝末年谭宏在此地结寨起义，自称武陵王，石宝因而成寨。

石宝寨最初的建筑天子殿始建于明万历年间。

自此以后，石宝寨几经改造扩建。

清嘉庆二十四年(1819年)依傍崖壁建造了9层飞檐楼阁与山崖同高。

咸丰四年(1854年)对最初的天子殿进行了扩建。

20世纪50年代初，在清代9层楼阁的基础上于山巅加建3层，共合为12层，始成今日的模样。

加建部分名为魁星阁，四角攒尖顶。

寨中现存的建筑多为清代所建。

12层楼阁是石宝寨最重要的建筑。

它坐北朝南，靠山面水，通高56米，全木结构，形如楼阁式塔，是我国现存体积最大、层数最多的穿斗式木结构建筑。

下九层楼阁高33.46米，有九重天的象征意义。

阁内每层石壁上均有题刻，并有木楼梯盘旋而上。

楼窗前有高6米多高的砖石结构山门，正面用陶瓷镶嵌有小蓬莱梯云直上等字样，辅以五龙捧圣哪吒闹海等浮雕故事，生动有趣。

石宝山顶有一块平地，是天子殿(又名绀宇宫)的所在，为石宝寨的制高点。

在此凭栏远眺，滔滔江流，孤帆远影，尽收眼底。

受三峡工程蓄水影响，长江水面上升到寨门口，石宝寨从半岛变成了江中的一个孤岛，仅通过一架悬索桥与岸相接。

寨下修建有一圈白色软堤。

如今的石宝寨仿佛一个放大的盆景置于江中，十分奇特。

英文翻译 English Translation

Legend has it that when Nüwa mended the sky, she left behind a five-colored stone, which fell into the territory of Zhongxian County.

However, this stone did not transform into a playboy; instead, it took root on the north bank of the Yangtze River 45 km from the county seat, becoming a lonely cliff, called Shibao (Stone Treasure).

At the end of Ming, Tan Hong built a fortress and rose in rebellion here, proclaiming himself King of Wuling; hence Shibao became a fortress (zhai).

The earliest building of Shibaozhai, the Tianzi (Son-of-Heaven) Hall, was first built during the Ming Wanli era.

Since then, Shibaozhai has undergone several renovations and expansions.

In the 24th year of Jiaqing (1819), Qing, a 9-story flying-eave pavilion was built against the cliff, equal in height to the cliff.

In the 4th year of Xianfeng (1854), the original Tianzi Hall was expanded.

In the early 1950s, on the basis of the Qing 9-story pavilion, 3 more stories were added on the mountain top, totaling 12 stories, becoming today's appearance.

The added part is named Kuixing (Star of Literature) Pavilion, with a four-corner pyramidal roof.

Most of the existing buildings in the fortress were built in Qing.

The 12-story pavilion is the most important building of Shibaozhai.

It faces south, backed by the mountain and facing the water, with a total height of 56m, all-timber structure, shaped like a pavilion-style pagoda; it is the largest-volume and most-story穿斗式 (column-and-tie) timber structure building existing in China.

The lower nine stories of the pavilion are 33.46m high, with the symbolic meaning of Nine Heavens.

On the stone wall of each story inside the pavilion there are inscriptions, and a wooden staircase spirals upward.

In front of the pavilion window there is an over-6m-high brick-stone structure mountain gate; on the front are inlaid with ceramics the characters Small Penglai, Ladder Clouds Straight Up, etc., supplemented by relief stories such as Five Dragons Holding the Sage and Nezha Stirs the Sea, vivid and interesting.

On the top of Shibao Mountain there is a flat ground, where the Tianzi Hall (also called Ganyu Palace) is located, being the highest point of Shibaozhai.

Leaning on the railing and looking into the distance here, the surging river flow and lonely sail shadows are all in sight.

Affected by the water storage of the Three Gorges Project, the Yangtze River water level rose to the fortress gate; Shibaozhai changed from a peninsula to an isolated island in the river, only connected to the shore through a suspension bridge.

A circle of white soft embankment was built under the fortress.

Today's Shibaozhai is like an enlarged bonsai placed in the river, very peculiar.

丁房阙和无铭阙

Dingfang Que and Wuming Que
国家级 东汉 石阙
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty东汉
地址 Address忠县忠州镇白公路24号白公祠内
类型 Type石阙
看点 Highlights: 汉阙 浮雕

中文描述 Description

汉阙是汉代的一种表示威仪等级的纪念性建筑，有石质汉书之称。

巴蜀一带的汉阙数量超过我国现存汉阙总数的二分之一，仅忠县一个县城就有乌杨阙、丁房阙、无铭阙等共五座汉阙。

随着三峡水库的兴建，忠县老县城有将近三分之二被淹没，因此这些国宝也被迫迁移原址，其中丁房阙和无铭阙都迁进了白公祠内，并安置在同一处。

丁房阙原本位于忠州镇人民路二巷，为双阙，高约7米。

建于东汉，宋、明两代都曾有过修葺。

关于其身份有不同的猜测，一说是墓阙，一说是巴王庙阙。

东阙为母子阙(即紧邻的一大一小两阙)。

每阙从下至上可划分为11层不同的结构，依次是阙基、阙身、刻画层、枋子层、介石层、斗拱层、腰檐、上枋子层、上介石层、上斗拱层、阙顶。

阙身收分明显，显得瘦长而挺拔。

阙正面刻有《巴国忠贞祠铭》，内侧刻《重修巴国忠贞祠铭》，背面刻清乾隆三十六年(1771年)题铭，内容均已难以辨认。

刻画层正面有二只小兽口衔缠带的图案，其中一只已严重风化，形状已磨灭了；

右侧浮雕有一乘鹿、一抱物的两个人。

枋子层刻锯齿状枋头、角神、饕餮等。

介石层与斗拱层由一块石头刻成，形制朴素。

上斗拱层的正、背面刻有浮雕斗拱各二朵，一斗二升，两斗拱间刻着一个半开的小门，一个妇人探身而出，极富生活气息；

侧面刻鸳鸯交手拱。

阙顶盖是庑殿顶的形式，出檐较远。

英文翻译 English Translation

Han Que (Han dynasty gate towers) are a type of commemorative building of the Han dynasty indicating majesty and rank, known as the Stone Han Book.

The number of Han Que in the Bashu (Sichuan) region exceeds half of the total existing Han Que in China; in Zhongxian County alone there are five Han Que including Wuyang Que, Dingfang Que, and Wuming Que.

With the construction of the Three Gorges Reservoir, nearly two-thirds of the old county town of Zhongxian was submerged, so these national treasures were also forced to relocate from their original sites; among them, Dingfang Que and Wuming Que were both moved into the Bai Gong Shrine and placed at the same location.

Dingfang Que was originally located in Lane 2, Renmin Road, Zhongzhou Town, as a pair of que, about 7m high.

Built in Eastern Han, it was renovated in both Song and Ming dynasties.

There are different speculations about its identity; one says it is a tomb que, another says it is the que of the Ba King Temple.

The east que is a mother-son que (i.e., a large and a small que adjacent to each other).

Each que can be divided from bottom to top into 11 different structural layers, sequentially: que base, que body, carving layer, lintel layer, stone-interlayer layer, bracket-set layer, waist eave, upper lintel layer, upper stone-interlayer layer, upper bracket-set layer, and que top.

The que body has obvious tapering, appearing slender and upright.

On the front of the que is engraved the Inscription of the Loyal and Chaste Shrine of the Ba State; on the inner side is engraved the Inscription of Rebuilding the Loyal and Chaste Shrine of the Ba State; on the back is engraved an inscription of the 36th year of Qianlong (1771), Qing, all contents already difficult to辨认.

On the front of the carving layer there is a pattern of two small beasts with wrapped bands in their mouths; one of them has been severely weathered, its shape already worn away; on the right side are reliefs of two people, one riding a deer and one holding an object.

The lintel layer is carved with serrated lintel heads, corner deities, taotie (gluttonous beast), etc.

The stone-interlayer layer and bracket-set layer are carved from a single stone, with a simple shape.

On the front and back of the upper bracket-set layer are carved two relief bracket sets each, one bucket with two capitals; between the two bracket sets is carved a half-open small door, with a woman leaning out, extremely rich in life atmosphere; on the side is carved a mandarin-duck hand-in-hand bracket set.

The que top cover is in the form of a hip-and-gable (wudian) roof, with far-reaching eaves.

潼南大佛寺摩崖造像

Cliffside Statues of Dafo Temple in Tongnan
国家级 隋—清 宗教建筑、摩崖造像
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty隋—清
地址 Address潼南县梓潼镇石碾村
类型 Type宗教建筑、摩崖造像
看点 Highlights: 历代造像 龛窟 题刻 大佛阁

中文描述 Description

大佛寺位于潼南县梓潼镇石碾村定明山下。

始建于唐，称为南禅寺，宋代叫作定明院。

后因在寺内依山凿成一座大佛，又改名为大佛寺。

寺内有大佛阁、观音殿、玉皇殿、鉴亭等木构建筑，大多为清代所建。

寺内的摩崖造像是隋唐至清代雕刻遗留下来的文物，内容与佛道两教有关，具有极高的历史研究价值。

现存的128个龛窟和932尊造像分布在以大佛阁两旁长达一里左右的山崖峭壁上。

其中最重要的是位于大佛阁内的金身坐佛像。

寺内的山崖上刻有一则《皇宋创造石佛记》，从中我们得知该像是由佛道两教前后历时近300年共同凿刻而成的。

唐咸通年间(843—860年)开凿了佛头，而后宋代道家按照佛首的比例续刻佛身，用了26年。

大佛形体凿好后又浑身贴金，直到公元1152年才全部完成。

佛像高18.43米，体型匀称，双目有神，为我国第一大金佛。

后来在大佛外部倚靠山势修建了高七重的大佛阁，各层顶上均满铺琉璃瓦，檐角起翘，巍峨壮观。

大佛阁是我国迄今为止保留不多的佛阁例证之一。

大佛寺的东岩有隋代凿刻的道教造像，是重庆现存年代最久远的纪年造像。

除了造像，岩壁上一个高8.85米的佛字也十分壮观。

这个佛字书于清同治年间(1870年)，用笔刚劲有力。

岩石经年累月因风雨冲刷形成的自然纹理，为其平添了几分沧桑之感。

在大佛寺左侧的山崖上还有一处十分有趣的印记——从明代到民国七个不同年代的洪水标记线，由此可以清楚地看出历次涪江洪水的大小，也算是一份别样的史料贡献。

英文翻译 English Translation

Dafo (Great Buddha) Temple is located at the foot of Dingming Mountain, Shinian Village, Zitong Town, Tongnan County.

It was first built in Tang, called Nanchan (Southern Chan) Temple, and in Song it was called Dingming Courtyard.

Later, because a great Buddha was chiseled against the mountain inside the temple, it was renamed Dafo Temple.

Inside the temple there are timber buildings such as the Great Buddha Pavilion, Guanyin Hall, Jade Emperor Hall, and Jian Pavilion, most of which were built in Qing.

The cliffside statues inside the temple are cultural relics left by carving from Sui-Tang to Qing, with content related to both Buddhism and Daoism, having extremely high historical research value.

The existing 128 niches and 932 statues are distributed on the cliff walls about one li long on both sides of the Great Buddha Pavilion.

Among them, the most important is the gilded seated Buddha statue inside the Great Buddha Pavilion.

On the mountain cliff inside the temple there is engraved a Record of the Great Song Creating the Stone Buddha, from which we learn that this statue was jointly chiseled by Buddhism and Daoism over a period of nearly 300 years.

During the Tang Xiantong era (843-860), the Buddha head was chiseled; then Song Daoists continued to carve the Buddha body according to the proportion of the Buddha head, taking 26 years.

After the Buddha form was chiseled, it was gilded all over, and it was not fully completed until 1152 AD.

The Buddha statue is 18.43m high, with a well-proportioned body and spirited eyes, being the No.1 Great Gold Buddha in China.

Later, outside the Great Buddha, a seven-story-high Great Buddha Pavilion was built against the mountain terrain; the tops of each layer are fully covered with glazed tiles, with upturned eave corners, towering and spectacular.

The Great Buddha Pavilion is one of the few preserved examples of Buddha pavilions in China to date.

On the east rock of Dafo Temple there are Daoist statues chiseled in Sui, being the oldest dated statues existing in Chongqing.

Besides the statues, an 8.85m-high character Fo (Buddha) on the rock wall is also very spectacular.

This Buddha character was written during the Qing Tongzhi era (1870), with vigorous and powerful brushwork.

The natural texture formed by the rock over years of wind and rain erosion adds a touch of vicissitudes to it.

On the cliff on the left side of Dafo Temple there is also a very interesting mark — flood marker lines from seven different eras from Ming to Republic, from which one can clearly see the magnitude of each Fujiang River flood, which can be regarded as a unique historical contribution.

独柏寺正殿

Main Hall of Dubai Temple
国家级 元 宗教建筑
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty元
地址 Address潼南县上和镇后沟村四社独柏小学内
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 元代木构 斗拱细作

中文描述 Description

在潼南县东20公里的上和镇后沟村四社独柏小学内，保留着两座古老的木构建筑，它们就是独柏寺正殿和后殿。

关于独柏寺的史料记载极少，仅在《潼南县志》上有一句话独柏寺始建于唐咸通三年(862年)，而民间的老百姓自有流传的说法。

当地人认为这座寺庙与一尊叫作柏树菩萨的雕像有密切的关系。

这尊雕像用一整根柏木雕刻而成，后人为了供奉它而修建了这座寺庙，也就顺理成章地给它取名独柏寺。

独柏寺经唐、宋、元等各代维修改建，现在只剩下元代正殿与清代后殿(观音殿)。

独柏寺正殿坐东北向西南，建在高0.55米的素面台基上，单檐歇山顶，抬梁式木结构。

面阔三间，进深三间。

正殿四周的檐面铺有二重椽，这一举措保证了屋面的出檐宽度。

屋檐自中心向两边缓慢起翘，举折之比(比例：7.1:12.4)较小，坡度平缓。

建筑用材较大，最大柱径为0.38米，高5米，给人坚实之感。

斗拱的设置是整个建筑最值得称道之处。

前檐下斗拱数量达10朵之多，朵朵构造精巧，造型美观，具有元代建筑的典型特征。

据专家考证，独柏寺正殿是重庆境内年代最为久远的木构建筑。

整座建筑古朴大方，初见觉得其貌不扬，但细观其阑额、普柏枋、圆形蜀柱、覆盖式柱础、殿内横梁彩绘等，便知这座看似普通的建筑其实具有很高的科学研究价值。

独柏寺后殿建成于清代，面阔五间，硬山顶，同为抬梁式构架。

梁上题有清康熙五十四年(1715年)修造记，昭示着它历经的悠久岁月。

英文翻译 English Translation

Inside Dubai Primary School, Group 4, Hougou Village, Shanghe Town, 20 km east of Tongnan County, there are preserved two ancient timber buildings — they are the main hall and rear hall of Dubai Temple.

There are very few historical records about Dubai Temple; only one sentence in the Tongnan County Annals says Dubai Temple was first built in the 3rd year of Xiantong (862), Tang, while the common people have their own circulating sayings.

Locals believe that this temple is closely related to a statue called the Cypress Tree Bodhisattva.

This statue was carved from an entire cypress log; later generations built this temple to enshrine it, and naturally named it Dubai (Single Cypress) Temple.

Dubai Temple underwent maintenance and reconstruction in Tang, Song, Yuan and other dynasties; now only the Yuan main hall and the Qing rear hall (Guanyin Hall) remain.

The main hall of Dubai Temple faces southwest from the northeast, built on a 0.55m-high plain platform base, with single-eave xieshan roof and beam-lifting timber structure.

It is 3 bays wide and 3 bays deep.

Around the main hall, the eave surface is laid with double rafters; this measure ensures the eave projection width of the roof.

The eaves slowly rise from the center to both sides, with a small举折 ratio (proportion: 7.1:12.4) and a gentle slope.

The building materials are large; the maximum column diameter is 0.38m, 5m high, giving a solid feeling.

The setting of bracket sets (dougong) is the most praiseworthy part of the entire building.

There are as many as 10 bracket sets under the front eave, each exquisitely constructed and beautifully shaped, with typical features of Yuan architecture.

According to expert research, the main hall of Dubai Temple is the oldest timber building within Chongqing.

The entire building is simple and generous; at first glance it seems unremarkable, but a close look at its lan'e (architrave), pubai fang (plate), round shu zhu (short columns), covered-style column bases, and painted beams inside the hall reveals that this seemingly ordinary building actually has high scientific research value.

The rear hall of Dubai Temple was built in Qing, 5 bays wide, with flush gable roof, also of beam-lifting frame.

On the beam there is an inscription of repair and construction in the 54th year of Kangxi (1715), Qing, indicating its long history.

龙兴寺正殿

Main Hall of Longxing Temple
市级 明 宗教建筑
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty明
地址 Address潼南县小渡镇代场村六社
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 明代木构 题记

中文描述 Description

若不是特地前来寻访，大概第一眼看见这个被荒山荒草包围的小房子的人，都会觉得它不过是个因被弃而荒废多年的乡间草庐。

但对稍有点儿中国古建筑常识的人来说，那比普通民居高出一个等级的歇山顶却也露出一些端倪。

这是明代的遗物。

虽经历代改造修缮，但总体依然保留了明代特征。

龙兴寺正殿始建于明天顺四年(1460年)，脊檩上题有大明天顺四年寅辰字样。

坐北朝南，面阔三间19.1米，进深三间12.09米，高8.2米。

1米高的台基将正殿从杂草中抬起。

柱子和梁直接结合，没有斗拱。

柱顶也没有卷杀和侧脚等做法。

梁架中的联系构件以横向为主，纵向较少。

檩、垫板和枋子为一个整体。

檐下的飞椽保证了可观的出檐宽度。

殿身周围有四根擎檐柱，用于支撑大角梁，形成了0.85米宽的副阶周匝。

殿内壁原有明代壁画4幅，可惜惨遭灰浆涂抹，已不可见。

关于正殿的屋顶，据考察有被改造的痕迹。

现有歇山顶的构件颜色、材质等与殿内梁架不同，并且在殿内屋架还可看到庑殿顶的构件由戗，由此判断原来的屋顶形式为单檐庑殿顶，不知为何被改为了歇山顶。

而如今灰瓦歇山顶的正脊也被损毁，瓦间尽是枯黄的野草。

龙兴寺正殿曾作为隆兴村小学的教室，内墙上仍保留着好好学习天天向上的标语。

而在山墙的外面，愚公移山改造中国等豪言壮语也还清晰可见，这大概是最简单明了的历史印记了吧。

英文翻译 English Translation

If not specifically coming to visit, probably people who at first glance see this small house surrounded by barren mountains and weeds would all think it is nothing more than a countryside thatched hut abandoned and wasted for many years.

But for those with a little knowledge of Chinese ancient architecture, the xieshan (overhanging gable) roof, one grade higher than ordinary folk houses, also reveals some clues.

This is a relic of Ming.

Although it has undergone reconstruction and repair through dynasties, overall it still retains Ming features.

The main hall of Longxing Temple was first built in the 4th year of Tianshun (1460), Ming; on the ridge purlin is inscribed the characters Yinshen, 4th Year of Tianshun of the Great Ming.

It faces south, 3 bays wide (19.1m), 3 bays deep (12.09m), 8.2m high.

The 1m-high platform base lifts the main hall from the weeds.

Columns and beams are directly combined, without bracket sets.

There is also no entasis (juansha) or incline (cejiao) at the column tops.

The connecting members in the beam frame are mainly horizontal, with fewer vertical ones.

The purlin, backing board, and lintel are one whole.

The flying rafters under the eave ensure a considerable eave projection width.

Around the hall body there are four eave-supporting columns, used to support the large corner beams, forming a 0.85m-wide surrounding auxiliary eave (fujie zhouza).

The inner walls of the hall originally had 4 Ming murals; unfortunately they were cruelly smeared with mortar and are no longer visible.

Regarding the roof of the main hall, according to investigation there are traces of modification.

The color and material of the existing xieshan roof components differ from the beam frame inside the hall, and in the interior roof frame one can still see the youqiang (diagonal beam) component of a wudian (hip) roof; from this it is judged that the original roof form was a single-eave wudian roof, which for unknown reason was changed to a xieshan roof.

And now the main ridge of the grey-tile xieshan roof has also been damaged, with withered yellow weeds between the tiles.

The main hall of Longxing Temple once served as the classroom of Longxing Village Primary School; on the inner walls there still remain the slogans Study Hard and Make Progress Every Day.

And on the outside of the gable walls, heroic words such as The Foolish Old Man Removes the Mountains, Transforming China are still clearly visible — this is probably the simplest and clearest historical imprint.

涞滩二佛寺摩崖造像

Cliffside Statues of Erfo Temple in Laitan
国家级 南宋 摩崖造像
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty南宋
地址 Address合川区涞滩镇二佛寺下殿
类型 Type摩崖造像
看点 Highlights: 古镇 造像

中文描述 Description

涞滩古镇位于合川区东北部，宋代时已初具规模，现保留着清代瓮城等大量明清时代遗迹。

古镇傍着流经合川的三江之一渠江，曾是个繁忙的码头。

高低错落的小青瓦房，古朴典雅的青石小巷，别具风韵。

涞滩二佛寺原名鹫峰禅寺，分为上下两寺，上寺居于鹫峰山顶，规模庞大，气势雄伟；

下寺在山间，依山而建一重檐歇山式三层殿堂，名曰二佛殿。

该寺在晚唐时期香火极盛。

但自从南宋淳熙、嘉泰年间在下寺开凿了大批摩崖造像后，造像的名声渐渐盛于寺庙本身。

据说后因寺内石佛曾居四川省第二，连名字都改为了二佛寺。

摩崖造像分布在二佛殿内北、西、南三面崖壁上。

有浮雕造像218龛，共计1676尊，规模可观。

整个造像的核心部分——大型群雕释迦牟尼说法图位于北崖，体现的是禅宗不立文字，教外别传，直指人心，见性成佛的宗旨。

主像是正中央的圆雕弥勒佛金身坐像。

坐像高12.5米，头饰螺髻，双耳垂肩，双眼半睁，面部丰腴；

着褒衣博带式袈裟，左手抚膝，作说法状。

这就是当年仅次于乐山大佛的二佛。

大佛旁侧侍阿难、迦叶、十菩萨等。

后壁还有千佛、飞天等像。

西崖禅宗六祖像壁刻有造像记一则，落款为皇宋淳熙丙午(1186年)季春。

南崖也有两则淳熙年间的造像记。

此外还有目连尊者、十六尊者、泗州大圣、达摩、须菩提和弥勒大士等像，各有特色。

其中的达摩像最是与别处不同。

达摩一贯以浓眉大眼、威猛异常的形象出现，而这里的达摩像却表情娴静，慈祥非凡，让人觉得可亲可近。

无论是否有佛教的信仰，看完这些前人虔心雕刻的作品，心中多少怀有一丝敬畏和感念。

若能因此种下些善的种子，那便是前人的大功德一件了。

英文翻译 English Translation

Laitan Ancient Town is located in the northeast of Hechuan District; it had already begun to take shape in Song, and now preserves a large number of Ming-Qing era relics such as the Qing barbican.

The ancient town borders the Qujiang River, one of the three rivers flowing through Hechuan, and was once a busy wharf.

The高低错落 small grey-tile houses and the simple and elegant bluestone alleys have a unique charm.

Erfo (Second Buddha) Temple in Laitan was originally named Jiufeng Chan Temple, divided into upper and lower temples; the upper temple sits on the top of Jiufeng Mountain, with a large scale and imposing momentum; the lower temple is in the mountains, built against the mountain as a double-eave xieshan-style three-story hall, named the Second Buddha Hall.

This temple had extremely flourishing incense in the late Tang period.

But since large numbers of cliffside statues were chiseled in the lower temple during the Southern Song Chunxi and Jiatai eras, the reputation of the statues gradually surpassed that of the temple itself.

It is said that later because the stone Buddha inside the temple once ranked second in Sichuan Province, even the name was changed to Erfo (Second Buddha) Temple.

The cliffside statues are distributed on the north, west, and south cliff walls inside the Second Buddha Hall.

There are 218 niches of relief statues, totaling 1,676 statues, with considerable scale.

The core part of the entire statues — the large group carving of Sakyamuni Preaching the Dharma — is located on the north cliff, reflecting the Chan (Zen) sect's宗旨 of Not establishing written words, transmitting outside the teachings, pointing directly to the human heart, and seeing one's nature and becoming Buddha.

The main statue is the round-carved Maitreya Buddha gilded seated statue in the exact center.

The seated statue is 12.5m high, with spiral hair ornaments, long earlobes reaching the shoulders, half-open eyes, and a plump face; wearing a loose-robe and broad-sash style kasaya, with the left hand stroking the knee, in a preaching pose.

This was the Second Buddha, second only to the Leshan Giant Buddha in those days.

Beside the Great Buddha stand Ananda, Kasyapa, Ten Bodhisattvas, etc.

On the back wall there are also images of Thousand Buddhas, flying apsaras, etc.

On the west cliff, the wall carving of the Six Patriarchs of Chan has one statue inscription, dated to the late spring of the Bingwu year of Chunxi of the Great Song (1186).

On the south cliff there are also two statue inscriptions from the Chunxi era.

In addition there are images of Venerable Mulian, Sixteen Arhats, the Great Sage of Sizhou, Bodhidharma, Subhuti, and Maitreya, etc., each with its own characteristics.

Among them, the Bodhidharma statue is most different from elsewhere.

Bodhidharma has consistently appeared with thick eyebrows, big eyes, and an extraordinarily fierce image, but the Bodhidharma statue here has a serene expression, extraordinarily kind, making people feel approachable.

Whether or not one has Buddhist faith, after seeing these works devoutly carved by predecessors, one's heart more or less harbors a trace of reverence and gratitude.

If some seeds of goodness can thereby be planted, that would be a great merit of the predecessors.

净果寺

Jingguo Temple
市级 明 宗教建筑
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty明
地址 Address合川区古楼镇净果村
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 明代木构 题记 轴柱

中文描述 Description

古楼镇位于合川区西北部，嘉陵江穿境而过。

以盛产枇杷而闻名。

每年除了摘枇杷的时节会吸引大批嘴馋的游客外，其余时候并无太多喧嚣。

而镇上最为安静的地方，应属古刹净果寺了。

净果寺始建于北宋雍熙二年(985年)，明代时重修，清代维修，现存建筑均为明清时期所建。

不知在这些建筑中间是否还能找到一些宋代的遗物。

寺庙遵循传统的坐北朝南的四合院布局，占地3400平方米。

中轴线上依次排列着天王殿、大雄宝殿和后殿，两侧有转轮经藏殿和观音殿。

转轮经藏殿为歇山顶，脊檩上墨书大明正统捌年(1443年)……重立敬题。

殿内原本有木质转轮藏一具，不幸毁于文革时期，只剩下铁轴座，座上铸大宋已丑乾道五年(1169年)十月二日甲申建立等字，现保存在区文管所内。

大雄宝殿面阔三间、进深14.5米。

重檐歇山顶，抬梁式梁架。

檐下斗拱极多，足有21朵。

正檩上有明永乐二年(1404年)年重修时追题的维宋朝雍熙贰年等字样。

与明代重修时写下的小字相比，墙上歪歪扭扭的毛主席语录要抢镜得多。

不过说不定正是这些语录让古老的寺庙在当时有了先进的标志而免于被摧毁呢。

还有熟悉的团结、紧张、严肃、活泼几个大字，表明这地方曾经被征用做过学校。

佛像背后的《纪念白求恩》文章还清晰可见。

这些20世纪的纪念物早已与寺庙融为一体，不可分割了。

净果寺因香火不盛而异常清静安宁，多亏寺里挂了不少鲜红的大灯笼，不然就该过于冷清了。

英文翻译 English Translation

Gulou Town is located in the northwest of Hechuan District, with the Jialing River passing through its territory.

It is famous for producing loquats.

Every year, except for the loquat-picking season which attracts large numbers of greedy tourists, there is not much noise at other times.

And the quietest place in the town should be the ancient temple Jingguo Temple.

Jingguo Temple was first built in the 2nd year of Yongxi (985), Northern Song; it was rebuilt in Ming and repaired in Qing; the existing buildings were all built in the Ming-Qing period.

It is unknown whether some Song relics can still be found among these buildings.

The temple follows the traditional north-facing-south siheyuan layout, covering 3,400 sq m.

On the central axis are sequentially arranged the Heavenly Kings Hall, Mahavira Hall, and rear hall; on both sides are the Revolving Scripture Repository Hall and Guanyin Hall.

The Revolving Scripture Repository Hall has a xieshan roof; on the ridge purlin is written in ink: The 8th Year of Zhengtong of the Great Ming (1443)...

Re-erected and respectfully inscribed.

Inside the hall there was originally one wooden revolving scripture repository, unfortunately destroyed during the Cultural Revolution, leaving only the iron axle base; on the base are cast characters such as Established on the甲申 day, the 2nd day of the 10th month, the 5th year of Qiandao of the Great Song (1169), now preserved in the district cultural relics management office.

The Mahavira Hall is 3 bays wide and 14.5m deep.

It has a double-eave xieshan roof and beam-lifting frame.

There are extremely many bracket sets under the eave, as many as 21.

On the main purlin there are characters such as In the 2nd year of Yongle (1404), Ming, when rebuilt, retrospectively inscribed: The 2nd year of Yongxi of the Great Song, etc.

Compared with the small characters written during the Ming reconstruction, the crooked Chairman Mao quotations on the walls are much more eye-catching.

But perhaps it was precisely these quotations that gave the ancient temple an advanced mark at that time and saved it from destruction.

There are also the familiar large characters Unity, Tension, Seriousness, Liveliness, indicating that this place was once requisitioned as a school.

The article In Memory of Norman Bethune behind the Buddha statue is still clearly visible.

These 20th-century memorials have long since merged with the temple into one, inseparable.

Jingguo Temple is exceptionally quiet and peaceful because its incense is not flourishing; thanks to the many bright red large lanterns hung in the temple, otherwise it would be too desolate.

钓鱼城

Diaoyu Fortress
国家级 南宋 古战场遗址、城墙
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty南宋
地址 Address合川区合阳镇嘉陵江南岸钓鱼山上
类型 Type古战场遗址、城墙
看点 Highlights: 战场遗址 摩崖造像 题刻

中文描述 Description

在合川区合阳镇有一座钓鱼山，雄踞着嘉陵江、涪江、渠江三江交汇处，三面环水，乃兵家易守难攻之地。

800年前的南宋朝廷显然也看到了这一点，于是才有了今天的钓鱼城。

南宋淳祐二年(1242年)，为抵抗不断南侵的蒙古军队，时任四川制置使兼重庆府事余玠开始依山势建筑钓鱼城。

此后直到祥兴二年(1279年)，在将近40年的时间里，钓鱼城历经大小战役200多次，是宋军的坚实堡垒，就连蒙古军队所向披靡的蒙哥大汗也丧命于此。

钓鱼城因此有了上帝折鞭处的美誉。

钓鱼城有内外城之分，均依山势地形而建。

外城用条石垒砌，绵延近万米。

内城约2500米，现存城墙的墙基都是宋代遗迹。

在南北两侧各有一道一字墙，长度分别为1200米和2500米。

城外嘉陵江边有水师码头遗址。

从山下往上走，一处处遗迹依次出现在眼前，仿佛一幅巨大的抗战生活画卷在眼前缓缓展开。

首先是城门，原本有九个，现尚存八个，均为石券门。

始关门是进城经过的第一道关卡。

规模最大的城门是位于城南第二道防线上的护国门，门洞上镌刻全蜀关键四字。

城台上筑有重檐歇山顶城楼。

当年钓鱼城军民在此出入都要借助栈道，今天还能看出遗留的栈道石穴。

站在护国门上往下望，可见原一字墙遗址。

不远处还有安置巨炮的炮台遗迹。

继续往上，来到一处较为平坦的高地，只见地上有许多规则的圆形坑洞，这里便是九口锅遗迹。

这是中国最早的兵工厂遗址。

那些锅状的坑是当年守军碾磨硝、磺、木炭等配制火药的原料的碾盘。

九口锅旁边是传说中神仙济世的远古遗迹钓鱼台和粮食加工场遗址。

登上山顶，就是当年守军操练的校场和军营遗址了。

校场为直径36米的圆形，七幢营房排列在正南边。

这里的道路四通八达，便于军队在紧急时刻迅速出击。

800年前的硝烟早已散去，钓鱼城也绝不仅仅是战场遗迹那么简单。

而后的元、明、清及至民国，各个时期都在此留下了自己的印记。

山崖上有历代摩崖造像和题刻数十处，其中包括晚唐时期的悬空卧佛；

还有遍及整座山的宋代水井、清代建筑护国寺、忠义祠等。

如今的钓鱼城更像是一个宋以来的文物宝库，只不过它本身肩负着更深的历史意义。

痛苦的呻吟和胜利的欢呼都隐藏进大山里，也许化为一道辙痕、一个炮坑，等待着后人去发现。

英文翻译 English Translation

In Heyang Town, Hechuan District, there is a Diaoyu (Fishing) Mountain, towering at the confluence of the Jialing, Fu, and Qu three rivers, surrounded by water on three sides — a place easy to defend and difficult to attack for military strategists.

The Southern Song court 800 years ago obviously also saw this point, hence today's Diaoyu Fortress.

In the 2nd year of Chunyou (1242), Southern Song, to resist the constantly south-invading Mongol army, Yu Jie, then Sichuan Military Governor and concurrently Chongqing Prefect, began building Diaoyu Fortress according to the mountain terrain.

Thereafter until the 2nd year of Xiangxing (1279), in nearly 40 years, Diaoyu Fortress experienced over 200 battles large and small, being a solid stronghold of the Song army; even the Great Khan Möngke, whom the Mongol army was invincible, lost his life here.

Hence Diaoyu Fortress has the reputation of the Place Where God's Whip Was Broken.

Diaoyu Fortress is divided into inner and outer cities, both built according to the mountain terrain.

The outer city is built of dressed stones, stretching nearly 10,000m.

The inner city is about 2,500m; the existing wall bases of the city wall are all Song relics.

On the north and south sides there is each a one-character wall, with lengths of 1,200m and 2,500m respectively.

Outside the city by the Jialing River there is a navy wharf ruin.

Walking up from the foot of the mountain, ruins appear one after another before the eyes, as if a huge picture scroll of anti-war life slowly unfolds before the eyes.

First are the city gates; originally there were nine, now eight still survive, all stone-vaulted gates.

The Shiguan (Beginning-to-Close) Gate is the first checkpoint passed when entering the city.

The largest city gate is the Huguo (Protecting the Nation) Gate located on the second defense line south of the city; on the gate opening are engraved the four characters Key to All of Shu.

On the city gate platform is built a double-eave xieshan-roof gate tower.

In those days, the military and civilians of Diaoyu Fortress had to use plank roads to enter and exit here; today one can still see the remaining plank-road stone holes.

Standing on the Huguo Gate and looking down, one can see the original one-character wall ruin.

Not far away there is also the artillery platform ruin for placing giant cannons.

Continuing upward, one comes to a relatively flat highland, only to see many regular circular pits on the ground — this is the Nine Pots ruin.

This is the earliest arsenal ruin in China.

Those pot-shaped pits were the grinding discs for the garrison to grind raw materials for making gunpowder such as saltpeter, sulfur, and charcoal in those days.

Beside the Nine Pots is the ancient ruin Diaoyu (Fishing) Terrace of legendary immortal salvation and the grain processing site ruin.

Climbing to the mountaintop is the drill ground and military camp ruin where the garrison practiced in those days.

The drill ground is circular with a diameter of 36m, with seven barracks arranged on the due south side.

The roads here extend in all directions, facilitating the army to attack quickly in emergencies.

The smoke of gunpowder 800 years ago has long dispersed, and Diaoyu Fortress is by no means simply a battlefield ruin.

Later, Yuan, Ming, Qing and even Republic, each period left its own mark here.

On the mountain cliffs there are dozens of cliffside statues and inscriptions of various dynasties, including the suspended reclining Buddha of the late Tang; there are also Song dynasty wells throughout the mountain, the Qing building Huguo Temple, Zhongyi (Loyalty and Righteousness) Shrine, etc.

Today's Diaoyu Fortress is more like a treasure house of cultural relics since Song, except that it itself bears a deeper historical significance.

Painful groans and victory cheers have all hidden into the great mountain, perhaps turning into a rut mark or a cannon pit, waiting for later generations to discover.

岩溪桥

Yanxi Bridge
市级 南宋 桥梁
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty南宋
地址 Address合川区北郊嘉陵江西岸岩沟·地中海广场内
类型 Type桥梁
看点 Highlights: 石拱券

中文描述 Description

岩溪桥位于合川区北郊嘉陵江西岸的岩溪河口上，原桥东3米外有一个摩崖《张氏建岩溪桥记》碑记。

据碑记记载，该桥捐兴于庆元乙卯孟春。

由此可知这座石桥建造于南宋庆元元年(1195年)，距今已有800多年历史。

这座长21.5米、宽2.18米的单孔石拱桥连接着南北两岸。

中央拱券形似半圆，矢高(拱顶到拱脚的高差)4.66米，净跨度5.6米，看上去比较丰满。

拱石采用干式叠砌法。

桥面上平铺石板，桥两侧无栏杆。

桥身两端与河床上自然的石壁连成一个整体。

西侧拱券中部有一个圆雕的鳞甲吸水兽。

清道光年间(1827年)，曾经在老桥近旁修过一座新桥，因两桥高度一致，看起来似一个整体，所以一度有古今桥的说法。

2011年，合川草街航电枢纽蓄水工程将要投入使用，岩溪桥所在的位置将被完全淹没，因此，不得不把这座在原地待了8个多世纪的古桥整体往上游方向移动了40米。

同时，加固了桥基，桥身增加了石栏杆。

但遗憾的是，原摩崖碑记已不见踪影，桥两端与自然石壁相连的结构也不复存在了。

今天岩溪桥所在的地方已变成了一个地中海风格的婚纱拍摄基地和高档住宅区。

包围在西餐厅、咖啡馆、现代雕塑和极具异国风情的植物之间，被拔了根的岩溪桥显得格外的落寞和虚弱。

英文翻译 English Translation

Yanxi Bridge is located at the mouth of Yanxi River on the west bank of the Jialing River in the northern suburb of Hechuan District; 3m east of the original bridge there was a cliffside stele inscription Record of the Zhang Family Building Yanxi Bridge.

According to the stele inscription, this bridge was donated and initiated in the early spring of the Yimao year of Qingyuan.

From this we know that this stone bridge was built in the 1st year of Qingyuan (1195), Southern Song, with a history of over 800 years to date.

This single-arch stone bridge, 21.5m long and 2.18m wide, connects the north and south banks.

The central arch券 resembles a semicircle, with a rise (height difference from arch top to arch springing) of 4.66m and a clear span of 5.6m, looking relatively plump.

The arch stones use the dry stacking method.

The bridge deck is paved with stone slabs, with no railings on both sides.

Both ends of the bridge body are connected with the natural stone walls on the riverbed into one whole.

In the middle of the west arch券 there is a round-carved scale-armored water-absorbing beast.

During the Qing Daoguang era (1827), a new bridge was once built near the old bridge; because the two bridges had the same height and looked like one whole, there was for a time the saying of the Ancient-and-Modern Bridge.

In 2011, the water storage project of the Caojie Navigation and Power Hub in Hechuan was about to be put into use, and the location of Yanxi Bridge would be completely submerged; therefore, this ancient bridge, which had stayed in place for over 8 centuries, had to be moved 40m upstream as a whole.

At the same time, the bridge foundation was reinforced, and stone railings were added to the bridge body.

But regrettably, the original cliffside stele inscription has disappeared, and the structure connecting both ends of the bridge with the natural stone walls no longer exists.

Today, the place where Yanxi Bridge is located has become a Mediterranean-style wedding photography base and high-end residential area.

Surrounded by Western restaurants, cafes, modern sculptures, and extremely exotic plants, the uprooted Yanxi Bridge appears particularly lonely and weak.

合川文峰塔

Wenfeng Pagoda in Hechuan
市级 清 砖石塔
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address合川区合阳镇文峰古街
类型 Type砖石塔
看点 Highlights: 塔门浮雕 夜景 江景

中文描述 Description

城市发展与历史旧建筑保护之间似乎总是存在矛盾的，我们不止一次遗憾地看到许多珍贵的历史文物遗址在急功近利的城市建设中变成了建设用地，令人痛心。

但是，合川应该算一个例外。

作为重庆六大卫星城之一，合川近年来在新城建设的同时，对境内一大批历史文物也进行了建设性修缮，使文物在得以保存的基础上具有了更大的价值。

文峰古街的建设就是一个比较成功的例子。

文峰塔位于嘉陵江和涪江交汇处的河口，利用这良好的景观区位，围绕文峰塔顺势建起一条古色古香的文峰街，不仅使文峰塔免于陷在逼仄的高楼间的窘境，也为市民休闲观景打造了一个好去处，还吸引了大量游客，简直是一举三得，值得借鉴。

文峰塔始建于清嘉庆十五年(1810年)，时为9层。

道光十六年(1836年)，合州知州李宗沆又在原基础上加建4层，共13层，通高58米。

因为塔身呈灰白色，当地人俗称其为白塔。

石塔平面为八角形，密檐式，坐西南朝东北。

底层塔门门额上浮雕有形态各异的八仙人物，上方悬挂书有文峰塔的石匾，下方为一石拱券。

塔身逐级收分，呈锥状。

各层门洞上均有门额，额上挂有更上一层欲罢不能俯瞰嘉涪等匾，这些字均是用青花碎瓷拼合而成的。

黑色的塔檐采取叠涩出挑，塔刹为宝瓶顶。

底层至11层的塔心是一个锥形实体，有石梯盘旋可至11层。

每层塔心正面原来均有圆雕佛像，今已俱毁。

登塔远眺，山光水色尽收眼底。

文峰街的夜色极美。

灯光将文峰塔通体照得晶莹剔透一般，周围仿古建筑的翘角飞檐也被灯光勾勒出漂亮的弧线。

走到街边平台上，江风习习，可见江水荡漾，远山依稀，江上偶有一两星灯火摇晃，唤起人绵绵的情思，疑心是否闯进了谁的梦乡。

英文翻译 English Translation

There always seems to be a contradiction between urban development and the protection of historical old buildings; we have more than once regretfully seen many precious historical relic sites turned into construction land in quick-profit urban construction, heartbreaking.

But Hechuan should be considered an exception.

As one of the six satellite cities of Chongqing, in recent years Hechuan, while building new cities, has also carried out constructive repairs on a large number of historical relics within its territory, giving the relics greater value on the basis of being preserved.

The construction of Wenfeng Ancient Street is a relatively successful example.

Wenfeng Pagoda is located at the estuary where the Jialing and Fu rivers meet; utilizing this good landscape location, an antique Wenfeng Street was built顺势 around Wenfeng Pagoda, not only saving Wenfeng Pagoda from the dilemma of being trapped among cramped high-rise buildings, but also creating a good place for citizens to relax and view scenery, and attracting a large number of tourists — simply achieving three things at one stroke, worth learning from.

Wenfeng Pagoda was first built in the 15th year of Jiaqing (1810), Qing, then with 9 stories.

In the 16th year of Daoguang (1836), Li Zonghuang, the prefect of Hezhou, added 4 more stories on the original basis, totaling 13 stories, with a total height of 58m.

Because the pagoda body is grayish-white, locals commonly call it the White Pagoda.

The stone pagoda has an octagonal plane, of dense-eave style, facing northeast from the southwest.

On the lintel of the bottom-layer pagoda gate are reliefs of the Eight Immortals with different forms; above hangs a stone plaque inscribed with Wenfeng Pagoda, and below is a stone arch券.

The pagoda body tapers layer by layer, in a conical shape.

Above the door openings of each layer there are door lintels, on which hang plaques such as One More Layer, Unable to Stop, Overlooking Jia and Fu, etc.; these characters are all assembled from broken blue-and-white porcelain pieces.

The black pagoda eaves use corbelled projection, and the pagoda finial is a precious-vase top.

The pagoda core from the bottom to the 11th layer is a conical solid mass, with stone steps spiraling up to the 11th layer.

On the front of the pagoda core of each layer there were originally round-carved Buddha statues, now all destroyed.

Climbing the pagoda and looking into the distance, mountain scenery and water views are all in sight.

The night view of Wenfeng Street is extremely beautiful.

Lights illuminate the entire Wenfeng Pagoda so that it appears crystal clear; the upturned corners and flying eaves of the surrounding antique buildings are also outlined by lights into beautiful arcs.

Walking to the platform by the street, with the river breeze blowing gently, one can see the river water rippling, distant mountains faintly visible, and occasionally one or two star-like lights swaying on the river, evoking continuous tender feelings, and one suspects whether one has broken into someone's dreamland.

铜梁武庙

Emperor Guan's Temple in Tongliang
市级 明 宗教建筑、木结构
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty明
地址 Address铜梁县巴川街道民主路2号·少云公园内
类型 Type宗教建筑、木结构
看点 Highlights: 合院 琉璃顶 石雕

中文描述 Description

来到铜梁，意外发现这里有很多邱少云的痕迹，才知道原来他是铜梁人。

这让人多少有些欣喜，仿佛在一个陌生的地方找到了熟悉的东西。

而我们要寻访的铜梁武庙正位于少云公园内的凤山上，山顶是邱少云烈士纪念馆。

我们在当地人的指引下沿着石阶一路上山。

没走多远，便在绿树掩映中发现一个显眼的金色琉璃顶，是它无疑了。

武庙始建于明代，清同治六年(1867年)及20世纪80年代都有过修葺，庙内存同治年间重修碑记一则。

传统合院式布局。

现有天王殿、大雄宝殿、观音殿、厢房等。

大门进去第一个是天王殿。

天王殿位于0.8米高的台基上，东西垂带台阶各9级。

面阔三间、进深五间，高7米。

悬山顶，上铺灰瓦。

穿斗式梁架结构。

天王殿后面是大雄宝殿。

面阔三间，进深四间，高13.5米。

抬梁式梁架，共有七架梁。

上为歇山琉璃顶，下有2米高的台基。

80年代修缮时在台基正面加刻浮雕，分别以九龙壁姑苏城渔樵耕读天仙配等为主题，倒是令其生动不少。

厢房面阔七间，进深三间，与天王殿一样为穿斗式梁架和悬山顶。

最后面是观音阁，重檐歇山顶，虽也覆琉璃瓦，但明显要比大雄宝殿的琉璃顶粗劣得多，疑是后来加建的一座建筑。

大雄宝殿右侧有一覆坡屋顶的二层小楼，走廊上悬挂着洗过的衣服，很明显有人在此居住。

楼前有一块石照壁，刻二龙戏珠图案。

上有几道明显的裂痕，似乎是碎后重新拼接上的，但总体十分完整。

绕过石照壁，从侧门出了武庙，沿另一条路下山。

回头望了一眼，发现那金色的琉璃顶在夕阳下熠熠生辉。

英文翻译 English Translation

Coming to Tongliang, we unexpectedly discovered many traces of Qiu Shaoyun here, only then learning that he was originally from Tongliang.

This makes people somewhat delighted, as if finding something familiar in a strange place.

And the Tongliang Wumiao (Emperor Guan's Temple) we want to visit is located on Fengshan Mountain inside Shaoyun Park; on the mountaintop is the Qiu Shaoyun Martyr Memorial Hall.

Under the guidance of locals, we climbed up the mountain along the stone steps.

Not far after walking, we spotted a conspicuous golden glazed roof among the green trees — it was undoubtedly it.

Wumiao was first built in Ming; it was repaired in the 6th year of Tongzhi (1867), Qing, and in the 1980s; inside the temple there is one stele inscription of reconstruction during the Tongzhi era.

It has a traditional courtyard layout.

The existing buildings include the Heavenly Kings Hall, Mahavira Hall, Guanyin Hall, and wing rooms.

The first one after entering the main gate is the Heavenly Kings Hall.

The Heavenly Kings Hall is located on a 0.8m-high platform base, with 9垂带-style steps on the east and west each.

It is 3 bays wide, 5 bays deep, 7m high.

It has an overhanging gable roof, covered with grey tiles.

It has a穿斗式 (column-and-tie) beam frame structure.

Behind the Heavenly Kings Hall is the Mahavira Hall.

It is 3 bays wide, 4 bays deep, 13.5m high.

It has a beam-lifting frame, with a total of seven rafter beams.

Above is a xieshan glazed roof, below is a 2m-high platform base.

During the 1980s repair, reliefs were added on the front of the platform base, with themes such as Nine-Dragon Wall, Gusu City, Fisherman-Woodcutter-Farmer-Scholar, and Heavenly Match, which indeed make it much more vivid.

The wing rooms are 7 bays wide and 3 bays deep, like the Heavenly Kings Hall with column-and-tie beam frame and overhanging gable roof.

At the very back is the Guanyin Pavilion, with double-eave xieshan roof; although also covered with glazed tiles, it is obviously much cruder than the glazed roof of the Mahavira Hall, suspected to be a later-added building.

On the right side of the Mahavira Hall there is a two-story small building with a sloped roof; washed clothes are hung on the corridor, obviously someone lives here.

In front of the building there is a stone screen wall, carved with a Two Dragons Playing with a Pearl pattern.

There are several obvious cracks on it, seemingly reassembled after being broken, but overall very complete.

Bypassing the stone screen wall, we exited Wumiao through the side gate and went down the mountain along another road.

Looking back, we found that golden glazed roof shining brilliantly in the setting sun.

铁佛寺

Tiefo Temple
市级 明—清 宗教建筑、木结构
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address铜梁县巴川镇铁佛村
类型 Type宗教建筑、木结构
看点 Highlights: 明代木构 题记

中文描述 Description

在一条人车稀少的宽阔的大马路旁，是一个巨大的石砌高台，高台之上不是别的，正是铁佛寺的遗迹。

铁佛寺始建于元至正年间(1341—1368年)，从明至清均有过不同程度的维修。

四合院布局，坐北朝南，原建筑有山门、古塔、主殿、正殿、玉皇殿和东西厢房等。

抗日战争时期，铜梁正谊中学曾迁来寺内多年。

新中国成立后，这里又被改造成村小学，两侧的厢房分给百姓居住。

这时寺内的佛像显得碍眼而多余，因此大部分被毁。

文革时期，铁佛寺遭到更大破坏。

玉皇殿连同殿内玉皇像、铁佛像遭火灾烧毁，主殿和古塔被毁，山门被改建成住房。

经历多场浩劫后，现寺内仅存正殿和部分厢房，系典型的明代风格。

正殿保存较为完整，高8.5米，面阔三间、进深三间，抬梁式梁架，歇山顶石件搭到厢房屋顶上。

檐下共有斗拱28朵。

前梁和次梁上分别题有皇清乾隆五年岁次庚申仲冬月和大清同治八年岁次己巳仲冬月维修记。

殿内原先供奉西方三圣、文殊、普贤、十八罗汉等佛像，盘龙柱，顶上绘有西游记图集，均已被毁，令人惋惜。

左厢房保存较好，右厢房仅剩下北山墙面的抬梁式构架和屋顶，其余部分为后来改建砖砌。

正殿后面也有砖砌平房一座，可能是曾经的教室。

就这么几座建筑，孤寂、冷清，却又高调地立在高台上。

它们似乎想要说些什么，却欲言又止。

语言和现实一样苍白。

英文翻译 English Translation

Beside a wide main road with few people and vehicles, there is a huge stone-built high platform; on top of the platform is none other than the ruins of Tiefo (Iron Buddha) Temple.

Tiefo Temple was first built during the Yuan Zhizheng era (1341-1368), and underwent repairs of varying degrees from Ming to Qing.

It has a siheyuan layout, facing south; the original buildings included the mountain gate, ancient pagoda, main hall, principal hall, Jade Emperor Hall, and east and west wing rooms, etc.

During the War of Resistance against Japan, Tongliang Zhengyi Middle School once moved into the temple for many years.

After the founding of New China, this place was converted into a village primary school, and the wing rooms on both sides were distributed to common people to live in.

At this time, the Buddha statues inside the temple appeared obtrusive and redundant, so most were destroyed.

During the Cultural Revolution, Tiefo Temple suffered even greater damage.

The Jade Emperor Hall, together with the Jade Emperor statue and iron Buddha statue inside the hall, was destroyed by fire; the main hall and ancient pagoda were destroyed; the mountain gate was converted into housing.

After multiple catastrophes, now only the principal hall and part of the wing rooms remain in the temple, of typical Ming style.

The principal hall is relatively well preserved, 8.5m high, 3 bays wide, 3 bays deep, with beam-lifting frame; the xieshan-roof stone components rest on the wing room roofs.

Under the eave there are a total of 28 bracket sets.

On the front beam and secondary beam are respectively inscribed repair records of The Gengshen Year, the 5th Year of Qianlong of the Great Qing, Mid-Winter Month and The Jisi Year, the 8th Year of Tongzhi of the Great Qing, Mid-Winter Month.

Inside the hall were originally enshrined Buddha statues such as the Three Sages of the West, Manjushri, Samantabhadra, and Eighteen Arhats, with coiled-dragon columns, and Journey to the West picture collections painted on the top, all have been destroyed, regrettable.

The left wing room is relatively well preserved; the right wing room only has the beam-lifting frame and roof of the north mountain wall remaining, the rest was later rebuilt with bricks.

Behind the principal hall there is also a brick one-story house, possibly a former classroom.

Just these few buildings, lonely and desolate, yet standing high-profile on the high platform.

They seem to want to say something, but hesitate to speak.

Language is as pale as reality.

碑记桥

Beiji Bridge
市级 南宋 桥梁
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty南宋
地址 Address涪陵区马武镇蒲江办事处碑记村
类型 Type桥梁
看点 Highlights: 宋代石桥 石作

中文描述 Description

碑记桥为单孔石拱桥，始建于南宋绍熙五年(1194年)，清道光十年(1835年)补修，迄今已有约800年历史，过去是人们过往涪陵和南川的必经之地，是重庆现存最古老的、最大的一座石拱桥。

原本无名，后因石碑记述修桥相关事宜而得名，但题有绍熙甲寅(1194)的碑记现已不存，只存有1996年乡民修桥身时立下的石碑。

桥身南北走向，横跨东流溪河。

桥长31.5米，宽5.32米，高7.7米。

其石料普遍采用青石，表面呈人字形凿痕，利用原溪床基岩作桥基护底石，拱券条石为纵联砌置，箍以外圈。

矢高6.6米，净跨9.9米，具有典型的宋代民间建桥工艺和风格。

桥面以不规则的石板铺成，桥栏高0.35米，宽0.3米。

碑记桥表现了古代劳动人民的智慧和才干，为探讨宋代桥梁建筑提供了极为珍贵的实物资料。

曾经浩浩荡荡的蒲江只剩涓涓细流，800年的古桥被藤蔓缠绕若隐若现，但坚固牢实的桥墩、桥面、桥拱、桥栏，久经风吹雨打浪卷水冲，依然坚定地横卧在历史的长河上。

英文翻译 English Translation

Beiji (Stele-Inscription) Bridge is a single-arch stone bridge, first built in the 5th year of Shaoxi (1194), Southern Song, and repaired in the 10th year of Daoguang (1835), Qing; it has a history of about 800 years to date.

In the past it was the only way for people to travel between Fuling and Nanchuan, and is the oldest and largest existing stone arch bridge in Chongqing.

Originally nameless, it later got its name because a stone stele recorded matters related to building the bridge; but the stele inscription inscribed with Shaoxi Jiayin (1194) no longer exists now, only a stone stele erected by villagers when repairing the bridge body in 1996 remains.

The bridge body runs north-south, spanning the Dongliuxi River.

The bridge is 31.5m long, 5.32m wide, and 7.7m high.

Its stone materials generally use bluestone, with herringbone chisel marks on the surface; the original stream bed bedrock is used as the bridge foundation bottom-protection stone; the arch券 dressed stones are laid in longitudinal connection, hooped with an outer ring.

The rise is 6.6m, and the clear span is 9.9m, with typical Song folk bridge-building craftsmanship and style.

The bridge deck is paved with irregular stone slabs; the bridge railing is 0.35m high and 0.3m wide.

Beiji Bridge demonstrates the wisdom and talent of ancient working people, providing extremely precious physical material for discussing Song dynasty bridge architecture.

The once mighty Pujiang River now only has a trickle; the 800-year-old ancient bridge is faintly visible wrapped in vines, but its solid and firm bridge piers, deck, arch, and railings, after long exposure to wind, rain, waves, and water, still firmly lie across the long river of history.

宝顶山摩崖造像

Cliffside Statues at Baoding Mountain
国家级 南宋 宗教建筑、石刻
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty南宋
地址 Address大足县宝顶镇
类型 Type宗教建筑、石刻
看点 Highlights: 佛像 雕刻 色彩

中文描述 Description

与北山摩崖造像齐名的另一处大足石刻是位于大足县宝顶镇的宝顶山摩崖造像。

不同于北山造像历经多个时代的凿刻，宝顶山的造像集中反映的是南宋时期的雕刻特点。

宝顶山造像开凿于南宋淳熙六年(1179年)至淳祐九年(1249年)，由高僧赵智凤主持统一规划凿刻，是著名的密宗佛教道场。

各造像之间衔接紧凑，排布合理，数以万计却毫不零乱，相反，组成一个有序的整体。

在这整体之中，又有突出和侧重，其中大佛湾的造像最具价值。

大佛湾山崖形似马蹄，长500多米，其上密集排布着30余幅巨型浮雕，雕刻工艺精湛，图文并茂，宛如一本有趣的连环画。

而其中内容竟毫无雷同之处，让人不得不佩服前人的智慧和想象力。

既是佛教道场，造像的题材必然要宣扬这一时期的佛教理念，各种反映佛经故事、教义精髓的群雕自然少不了。

华严三圣像、千手观音像、释迦涅槃圣迹图、孔雀明王经变、六道轮回图等，不一而足。

但与之前其他时期的佛教造像所不同的是，这里面还有不少反映民间生活、倡导忠孝仁义的雕塑，如父母恩重经变、养鸡女图等，造型生动，贴近生活，仿佛为我们展开了一幅丰富多彩的南宋社会生活画卷；

又如大佛湾南岩的宝顶圆觉洞，佛像周围十分细致地雕刻了楼阁亭台、人物鸟兽、花草树木，将佛像放入十分写实的场景之中，给人亲切真实之感。

宝顶山造像中有不少大型造像，均利用天然岩石镂空雕刻，因造型的需求会产生一些力学问题。

工匠们以子之矛攻子之盾，巧用造型中的法器、飘带、配饰等对佛像整体进行平衡；

又利用祥云、飞天华盖等对山顶排水问题进行了妥善处理。

排水方面构思和设计最为周密的还属宝顶圆觉洞。

山间的泉水经洞顶被引入洞中，顺着壁间的小沟流入雕塑的龙口，作喷水状吐出，再注入暗沟，流出洞外。

此设计简直浑然天成，以致观者察觉不出雕琢痕迹。

在大佛湾一旁，还有同样为名僧赵智凤南宋年间主持修建的密宗禅院圣寿寺，几经损毁，现有建筑为明清重建。

寺庙规模宏大，沿山势布局，主要建筑有天王殿、玉皇殿、大雄宝殿、经殿、燃灯殿、维摩殿等。

此外，始建于明的万岁楼重檐八角，屋角高跷，极为灵动。

1999年，宝顶山摩崖造像与北山摩崖造像一起被联合国教科文组织列入《世界文化遗产名录》，其价值得到了更大范围的认可。

近年来，国家组织对大佛湾千手观音像进行了全面修复，也得到社会各界广泛关注。

英文翻译 English Translation

Another Dazu Rock Carving as famous as the North Mountain cliffside statues is the Baoding Mountain cliffside statues located in Baoding Town, Dazu County.

Unlike the North Mountain statues which were chiseled through multiple eras, the Baoding Mountain statues centrally reflect the carving characteristics of the Southern Song period.

The Baoding Mountain statues were chiseled from the 6th year of Chunxi (1179) to the 9th year of Chunyou (1249), Southern Song, under the unified planning and chiseling presided over by the eminent monk Zhao Zhifeng; it is a famous Tantric Buddhist ashram.

The statues connect compactly and are reasonably arranged; numbering in the tens of thousands yet not at all messy, on the contrary, they form an orderly whole.

Within this whole, there are also highlights and emphases; among them, the statues of Dafo (Great Buddha) Bay are the most valuable.

The cliff of Dafo Bay is shaped like a horseshoe, over 500m long, on which over 30 giant reliefs are densely arranged, with exquisite carving craftsmanship, combining pictures and texts, just like an interesting comic strip.

And the contents among them are surprisingly without any duplication, making one have to admire the wisdom and imagination of predecessors.

Since it is a Buddhist ashram, the themes of the statues must propagate the Buddhist concepts of this period; various group carvings reflecting Buddhist scripture stories and the essence of doctrines are naturally indispensable.

The Three Sages of Huayan statue, Thousand-Armed Guanyin statue, Sakyamuni Nirvana Holy Trace picture, Peacock Ming King Sutra Illustration, Six Paths of Reincarnation picture, etc., are too numerous to list.
