But different from Buddhist statues of other previous periods, there are also many sculptures reflecting folk life and advocating loyalty, filial piety, benevolence, and righteousness, such as the Parents' Kindness Sutra Illustration and Chicken-Raising Woman picture, with vivid modeling, close to life, as if unfolding for us a rich and colorful picture scroll of Southern Song social life; another example is the Baoding Yuanjue (Perfect Enlightenment) Cave on the south rock of Dafo Bay, around the Buddha statues are very meticulously carved pavilions, towers, terraces, figures, birds, beasts, flowers, and trees, placing the Buddha statues in a very realistic scene, giving a亲切 and真实 feeling.

Among the Baoding Mountain statues there are many large statues, all using natural rock for openwork carving; due to modeling needs, some mechanical problems arise.

The craftsmen, using the spear to attack the shield, cleverly use the ritual implements, ribbons, and accessories in the modeling to balance the whole Buddha statue; they also use auspicious clouds, flying apsaras, and canopies to properly handle the mountaintop drainage problem.

The most thoughtful in drainage conception and design is still the Baoding Yuanjue Cave.

The mountain spring water is introduced into the cave through the cave top, flows along the small grooves on the wall into the dragon mouth of the sculpture, spurts out in a water-spraying shape, then is injected into a hidden ditch and flows out of the cave.

This design is simply浑然天成, so that viewers cannot detect carving traces.

Beside Dafo Bay, there is also the Tantric Chan monastery Shengshou (Holy Longevity) Temple, likewise presided over and built by the famous monk Zhao Zhifeng during the Southern Song era; after several destructions, the existing buildings were rebuilt in Ming-Qing.

The temple is large in scale, laid out along the mountain terrain; the main buildings include the Heavenly Kings Hall, Jade Emperor Hall, Mahavira Hall, Scripture Hall, Burning-Lamp Hall, and Vimalakirti Hall, etc.

In addition, the Wansui (Long-Live) Tower, first built in Ming, has double eaves and eight corners, with high-raised eave corners, extremely agile.

In 1999, the Baoding Mountain cliffside statues, together with the North Mountain cliffside statues, were inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List by UNESCO, and their value has been recognized on a larger scale.

In recent years, the state organized a comprehensive restoration of the Thousand-Armed Guanyin statue in Dafo Bay, which has also received widespread attention from all sectors of society.

北山摩崖造像

Cliffside Statues at North Mountain
国家级 唐至宋 摩崖造像、宗教建筑
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty唐至宋
地址 Address大足县龙岗镇龙岗山
类型 Type摩崖造像、宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 历代造像风格 雕刻技艺 转世塔

中文描述 Description

提到北山摩崖造像大家可能感到十分陌生，但若说出大足石刻的名字，恐怕是无人不知，无人不晓。

其实，北山摩崖造像就是大名鼎鼎的重庆大足石刻的重要部分，位于大足县城西北2公里的龙岗镇龙岗山上。

造像始创于唐景福元年(892年)，创凿者为昌、普、渝、合四州都指挥使韦君靖，历经五代、北宋，直到南宋绍兴年间，共计250年才全部完成。

各朝代雕刻风格明显，保存完好，完美地展现了这一时期我国石窟艺术风格的发展变化。

造像分布在佛湾、营盘坡、观音坡、佛耳岩等处，其中以佛湾规模最为宏大。

佛湾形似一牙新月，长达300米的崖面分为南北两段，龛窟密集，通编290号，共计4360余躯造像。

南段多为晚唐、五代作品，北段多为两宋时期的作品。

晚唐造像以观音、地藏、观音地藏合龛等居多，颇具盛唐风格——人物体态丰满端庄，气质浑厚，衣纹细腻，线条流畅；

五代的造像则更小巧活泼一些，体态富于变化，呈现出由唐代向宋代过渡的特征。

两宋时期的作品题材更为丰富多样，人物形象鲜明，比例匀称，体态优美，衣着华丽，极具生活气息。

这一时期的佛教造像已具有明显的民族特征。

最具代表性的是凿于公元1142年至1146年的第136号转轮经藏窟，被誉为中国石窟艺术皇冠上的一颗明珠。

该窟中央是一个镂空的八角形转轮经藏，三面壁上对称分布着二十余尊造像。

各造像神情体态生动无比，反映出鲜明的性格，如普贤菩萨的典雅，玉印观音的庄重，数珠手观音的文静……尊尊雕像神性掺杂着人性，令人感受到神佛的可爱之处，又心生敬意，真是奇妙无比。

此外，佛湾的韦君靖碑蔡京碑古文孝经碑等碑文在给人以书法之美感的同时兼具重要的史料参考价值，十分珍贵。

在宋代释迦多宝龛之上不远处有一座砖砌的多宝塔，为空心密檐式塔，平面呈八角形，建于南宋绍兴年间。

塔的内外壁上镶嵌有一百多幅宋代雕刻。

从塔心的通道拾级而上，登临塔顶，向下俯瞰，周围景色尽收眼底，这是与在各个窟间仰视佛像时的应接不暇完全不同的感受。

英文翻译 English Translation

Mentioning the North Mountain cliffside statues, everyone may feel quite unfamiliar; but if the name Dazu Rock Carvings is spoken, I am afraid no one does not know it.

In fact, the North Mountain cliffside statues are an important part of the famous Dazu Rock Carvings in Chongqing, located on Longgang Mountain, Longgang Town, 2 km northwest of Dazu county town.

The statues were first created in the 1st year of Jingfu (892), Tang; the founder was Wei Junjing, the Commander-in-Chief of the four prefectures of Chang, Pu, Yu, and He; through Five Dynasties and Northern Song, until the Southern Song Shaoxing era, it took a total of 250 years to fully complete.

The carving styles of each dynasty are distinct and well preserved, perfectly showing the development and changes of Chinese grotto art style during this period.

The statues are distributed in Fo Bay, Yingpan Slope, Guanyin Slope, Fo'er Rock, etc., among which Fo Bay is the largest in scale.

Fo Bay is shaped like a crescent moon; the 300m-long cliff face is divided into north and south sections, with dense niches and caves, consecutively numbered 290, totaling over 4,360 statues.

The south section is mostly works of late Tang and Five Dynasties, and the north section is mostly works of the Two Song periods.

Late Tang statues are mostly Guanyin, Ksitigarbha, and combined Guanyin-Ksitigarbha niches, quite with the High Tang style — figures with plump and dignified postures, solid temperament, delicate garment patterns, and fluent lines; Five Dynasties statues are smaller and more lively, with postures full of variation, showing the transitional features from Tang to Song.

Works of the Two Song period have richer and more diverse themes, with vivid figure images, well-proportioned ratios, graceful postures, and gorgeous clothing, extremely full of life atmosphere.

Buddhist statues of this period already have obvious ethnic characteristics.

The most representative is Cave No.

136, the Revolving Scripture Repository Cave, chiseled from 1142 to 1146 AD, known as a pearl on the crown of Chinese grotto art.

In the center of this cave is an openwork octagonal revolving scripture repository; on the three walls are symmetrically distributed over twenty statues.

Each statue has vivid expressions and postures, reflecting distinct personalities, such as the elegance of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, the dignity of the Jade-Seal Guanyin, the quietness of the Prayer-Beads-Hand Guanyin...

each statue has divinity mixed with humanity, making people feel the loveliness of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and also心生 respect — truly奇妙无比.

In addition, the inscriptions such as the Wei Junjing Stele, Cai Jing Stele, and Ancient Text Classic of Filial Piety Stele in Fo Bay, while giving people the beauty of calligraphy, also have important historical reference value, very precious.

Not far above the Song Sakyamuni-Prabhutaratna niche there is a brick Duobao (Many Treasures) Pagoda, a hollow dense-eave style pagoda with an octagonal plane, built during the Southern Song Shaoxing era.

On the inner and outer walls of the pagoda are inlaid over a hundred Song carvings.

Climbing up step by step from the passage in the pagoda center, reaching the top of the pagoda and looking down, the surrounding scenery is all in sight — this is a completely different feeling from the overwhelming experience of looking up at Buddha statues between the various caves.

璧山文庙大成殿

Dacheng Hall of Temple of Confucius in Bishan
市级 清 礼制建筑
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address璧山县璧城街道中山北路
类型 Type礼制建筑
看点 Highlights: 如意斗拱 琉璃顶

中文描述 Description

璧山文庙又名孔庙，南宋绍熙年间始建。

据乾隆《璧山县志》记载，文庙曾经几易其址。

最初文庙建在县城南门；

明万历年间改建西门内，坐西朝东，毁于明朝末年；

清康熙二十五年(1686年)在城南旧址重建，毁于雍正七年(1729年)；

雍正十一年(1733年)又于西门内复建，也就是今天所在的地方。

清咸丰四年(1854年)重建，经同治、光绪补修。

如此反复之重建，倒是证明了儒家学派在历朝历代难以撼动的较高地位。

大成殿是文庙的主体建筑，明代时为祭奠孔子所建，现存建筑为清代遗构。

正殿高14米，位于双层素面石台基(高分别为1.2米和1.4米)之上，两侧分设台阶4级、7级。

面阔五间16米，进深三间11米。

明间设置6道六合门，次间3道，稍间有障水板，门窗上皆有雕花窗棂。

大殿为抬梁式梁架，中檩上墨书咸丰四年甲寅四月二十九日谷旦。

檐下斗拱密集，造型独特。

屋顶为重檐歇山琉璃顶，顶上装饰用的戗脊、正脊、翼角及鸱吻等均用镂空的黄、绿色琉璃件砌筑，整体造型庄严大方。

20世纪50年代起，璧山文庙一度作为璧山区公安局的办公场所使用，因此建筑得以躲过一些灾难，较完整地保存了形制。

如今，大成殿内每周日下午都有川剧演出，殿前设几张竹木桌椅，常有人在此品茶论道，读书看报，文化气息十分浓厚，也算是不负历史上因庙设学之庙学传统了。

英文翻译 English Translation

Bishan Temple of Confucius, also called the Confucian Temple, was first built during the Southern Song Shaoxi era.

According to the Qianlong-era Bishan County Annals, the Temple of Confucius changed its location several times.

Originally the Temple of Confucius was built at the south gate of the county town; during the Ming Wanli era it was rebuilt inside the west gate, facing east, and was destroyed at the end of Ming; in the 25th year of Kangxi (1686), Qing, it was rebuilt at the old site south of the city, and was destroyed in the 7th year of Yongzheng (1729); in the 11th year of Yongzheng (1733) it was rebuilt again inside the west gate, which is where it is today.

It was rebuilt in the 4th year of Xianfeng (1854), Qing, and repaired in Tongzhi and Guangxu.

Such repeated reconstructions actually prove the high and unshakable status of the Confucian school in all dynasties.

The Dacheng (Great Achievement) Hall is the main building of the Temple of Confucius; in Ming it was built to sacrifice to Confucius, and the existing building is a Qing surviving structure.

The main hall is 14m high, located on a double-layer plain stone platform base (1.2m and 1.4m high respectively), with 4 and 7 steps on both sides respectively.

It is 5 bays wide (16m) and 3 bays deep (11m).

The central bay has 6 six-panel doors, the secondary bays have 3 each, and the side bays have water-blocking boards; the doors and windows all have carved window lattice.

The main hall has a beam-lifting frame; on the middle purlin is written in ink: Auspicious Day, the 29th Day of the 4th Month, the Jiayin Year, the 4th Year of Xianfeng.

The bracket sets under the eave are dense and uniquely shaped.

The roof is a double-eave xieshan glazed roof; the decorative qiang ridges, main ridge, wing corners, and chiwen (owl-tail ornaments) on the roof are all built with openwork yellow and green glazed components, with an overall shape solemn and generous.

From the 1950s, Bishan Temple of Confucius once served as the office space of the Bishan District Public Security Bureau, so the building managed to avoid some disasters and preserved its form relatively completely.

Today, every Sunday afternoon there are Sichuan opera performances inside the Dacheng Hall; in front of the hall there are several bamboo-wood tables and chairs, and people often come here to taste tea and discuss the Way, read books and newspapers — the cultural atmosphere is very strong, which can be regarded as living up to the temple-school tradition of establishing schools because of temples in history.

朝元寺牌坊

Memorial Archway of Chaoyuan Temple
市级 明—清 石坊
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address璧山县梅江大兴镇朝元村
类型 Type石坊
看点 Highlights: 石仿木结构 石刻装饰 故事表现

中文描述 Description

在大兴镇山间曾隐藏着一座建于明万历癸巳年(1593年)的古刹——朝元寺。

据村里耄耋之年的老人回忆，他们小时候常在寺里玩耍流连，度过了许多快乐的时光。

令人痛心惋惜的是，朝元寺的殿宇均毁于文革时期，如今只剩下两道牌坊承载着所有的过去。

头道牌坊位于山门处，坐西北向东南，与朝元寺同年建成，为明代遗迹。

牌坊共有四柱三间，高宽均为6米，重檐歇山顶，明间檐下刻有交错菱形纹饰。

此牌坊最大的特点是它的斗拱，虽为石质，却是仿木结构。

其中明间一共有6攒斗拱，左右次间各2攒，均为一斗三升形式。

牌坊上还有莲花瓣、鱼肠绣球、二龙戏珠、双狮、云凤等精美雕刻。

牌坊当中立一匾额，上书欣国太平四个大字，落款为万历癸巳年孟冬吉旦立。

经过头道牌坊往里走十余米，矗立着另一座清代牌坊。

同为四柱三间，歇山顶，但比明代牌坊略大些，通高7米，宽6.8米。

柱子两侧有抱鼓夹杆石。

牌坊上依稀可见嘉庆四年(1799年)等字样，风化较为严重。

坊面上的雕刻涉及多种题材，有戏曲人物、神话传说，民间生活，也有花卉鸟兽，诸如二龙戏珠、双狮戏球等，大大小小共计50余幅，丰富有趣。

朝元寺虽毁，但周围的田间地头尚散落着许多破损的构件、雕像等。

希望今后它们和这两座牌坊都能得到尊重，免于被再次伤害，甚至成为文献上的传说。

英文翻译 English Translation

In the mountains of Daxing Town there once hid an ancient temple built in the Ming Wanli Guisi year (1593) — Chaoyuan Temple.

According to recollections of octogenarian elders in the village, when they were children they often played and lingered in the temple, spending many happy times.

It is heartbreaking and regrettable that the halls of Chaoyuan Temple were all destroyed during the Cultural Revolution; today only two memorial archways carry all of the past.

The first archway is located at the mountain gate, facing southeast from the northwest, built in the same year as Chaoyuan Temple, and is a Ming relic.

The archway has a total of four columns and three bays, both height and width are 6m, with double-eave xieshan roof; under the eave of the central bay are carved interlaced diamond patterns.

The biggest feature of this archway is its bracket sets; although of stone, they imitate timber structure.

Among them, the central bay has a total of 6 clusters of bracket sets, and the left and right secondary bays have 2 clusters each, all in the one-bucket-three-capital form.

On the archway there are also exquisite carvings such as lotus petals, fish-intestine silk balls, two dragons playing with a pearl, double lions, and cloud-phoenix.

In the middle of the archway stands a horizontal plaque, inscribed with the four large characters Happy Country and Peaceful World, with the signature: Erected on an Auspicious Day in the Early Winter of the Wanli Guisi Year.

Walking more than ten meters inward past the first archway, another Qing archway stands.

Also with four columns and three bays and xieshan roof, but slightly larger than the Ming archway, with a total height of 7m and width of 6.8m.

On both sides of the columns there are drum-shaped clamping stones.

On the archway one can faintly see characters such as the 4th year of Jiaqing (1799), with relatively severe weathering.

The carvings on the arch surface involve various themes, including opera figures, myths and legends, folk life, as well as flowers, birds, and beasts, such as two dragons playing with a pearl and double lions playing with a ball, totaling over 50 large and small, rich and interesting.

Although Chaoyuan Temple was destroyed, many damaged components, statues, etc.

are still scattered in the surrounding fields.

It is hoped that in the future they and these two archways can all be respected,免于 being harmed again, or even becoming legends in literature.

何氏百岁坊

Memorial Archway Marking He's 100th Birthday
国家级 清 石坊
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address璧山县青杠街道石安村1组
类型 Type石坊
看点 Highlights: 石仿木结构 石刻装饰 故事表现

中文描述 Description

清道光年间，璧山来凤有个周继盛，素爱行善。

他的祖母何氏，即奉直大夫周绍熙之妻，在周家一生严守妇道，也常行善积德，备受人们尊重。

于是周继盛在何氏年满百岁之时，即道光二十五年(1845年)，奏明朝廷，得圣旨恩准为祖母修建这座石牌坊，故称何氏百岁坊。

何氏百岁坊本是来凤古驿道上三座牌坊中的第二座，因此当地人也称其为二道牌坊。

可惜第一座和第三座牌坊均毁于文革时期，百岁坊能这么完整地保存下来实为幸事。

何氏百岁坊为仿木结构的石牌坊，重檐庑殿式顶，四柱三间五楼。

通高11米，宽7.88米。

最上方有寿字火焰宝珠顶，檐脊上饰有鱼龙飞吻。

牌坊上刻有狮子、白象、麒麟、蝙蝠等众多动物形象，明间正、背面的小额坊上题有旌表例赠奉直大夫周绍熙之妻何氏百岁坊，表明了此坊得圣上恩准的荣耀。

小额坊上的匾额刻有周绍熙的历任官职和何氏百岁坊序。

大额坊上浮雕有神话故事，故事里的人物姿态各异，栩栩如生。

其两端立柱上本来凿有八尊戏装人物造像，如今只剩六尊。

最上方的匾额正面刻升平人瑞，背面刻贞寿之门。

整个石坊雕饰丰富多彩，又不失庄严的气质。

石坊在此经历百余年月，周边光景早已改换，但它体现的孝义思想等作为传统美德的一部分却流传至今，仍然滋养着这一方土地。

英文翻译 English Translation

During the Qing Daoguang era, there was a Zhou Jisheng in Laifeng, Bishan, who always loved doing good deeds.

His grandmother, née He, the wife of Fengzhi Dafu (a rank) Zhou Shaoxi, strictly observed wifely duties throughout her life in the Zhou family, and also often did good deeds to accumulate virtue, highly respected by people.

So when He reached the age of 100, i.e., the 25th year of Daoguang (1845), Zhou Jisheng petitioned the court and obtained the imperial decree's approval to build this stone archway for his grandmother, hence called He's Centenarian Archway.

He's Centenarian Archway was originally the second of three archways on the ancient post road of Laifeng, so locals also called it the Second Archway.

Unfortunately, the first and third archways were both destroyed during the Cultural Revolution; it is truly fortunate that the Centenarian Archway has been preserved so completely.

He's Centenarian Archway is a timber-imitating stone archway, with double-eave hip-and-gable (wudian) style roof, four columns, three bays, and five stories.

It has a total height of 11m and width of 7.88m.

At the very top there is a寿-character flame precious-pearl top, and on the eaves and ridges are decorated fish-dragon kissing ornaments.

On the archway are carved many animal images such as lions, white elephants, qilin, and bats.

On the small lintel of the front and back of the central bay is inscribed: This archway marks the centenarian He, wife of the posthumously granted Fengzhi Dafu Zhou Shaoxi, in recognition of her virtues — indicating the glory of this archway being approved by the emperor.

On the plaque above the small lintel are carved Zhou Shaoxi's successive official positions and the preface to He's Centenarian Archway.

On the large lintel are reliefs of mythological stories, with figures in various postures, lifelike.

On the columns at both ends there were originally eight opera-costumed figure statues chiseled, now only six remain.

On the front of the topmost plaque is carved Peaceful Times and Human Sage, and on the back is carved Gate of Chastity and Longevity.

The entire stone archway has rich and colorful carvings and decorations, yet without losing its solemn temperament.

The stone archway has experienced over a hundred years here; the surrounding scenery has long changed, but the concepts of filial piety and righteousness it embodies, as part of traditional virtues, have been passed down to this day, still nourishing this land.

河包报恩寺塔

Pagoda of Bao'en Temple in Hebao
市级 南宋 砖石塔
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty南宋
地址 Address荣昌县河包镇白塔社区
类型 Type砖石塔
看点 Highlights: 盘龙柱 石斗拱 龙凤雀替

中文描述 Description

报恩寺塔位于荣昌县河包镇白塔社区内一个小山坡上，当地人称之为白塔。

行车至山坡下，离了公路，沿着一条石阶小路蜿蜒而上，来到坡顶一片石砌的平地上，便是塔的所在了。

报恩寺塔建于南宋绍兴二年(1132年)，其所在地原为报恩寺。

明末清初，报恩寺毁于大火，仅这一石塔幸免于难。

塔为八层方形空心楼阁式，正面朝北，通高16米。

塔基为素面双层正方形，边长5.2米，高1米，已被茂密的杂草湮没。

塔身由下往上逐层内收，每层四面或开窗，或设有椭圆形佛龛，少数龛内残存佛像，但面容早已风化不清。

底层四角有盘龙柱浮雕，鳞甲须鬣尚可辨认。

各层檐下均施一斗三升斗拱若干，并浮雕龙凤雀替，造型别致，虽有局部风化，但神韵犹存。

柱枋间依稀可见榫卯结构。

塔身各层刻有经文。

据记载，塔内有方形空心柱直贯顶层，石阶绕之盘旋，人可沿着石阶登至七层。

然而如今一层正面的门已被石板砌封上，无法一尽登临之兴了。

虽然整个塔身檐部缺损较多(越往上损毁越重，塔刹已全毁)，但它用石质构造向后世呈现了一斗三升、龙凤雀替等南宋独特的木构营造法式，堪称南宋石塔的建筑标本。

报恩寺塔历经800余年沧桑，如今只与群山草木为伴，与白云飞鸟为友，纵使经文漫漶，佛像损毁，自另有一番禅意，难以言说，只可近它身旁细细体味，方得一二罢了。

英文翻译 English Translation

Bao'en (Requiting Kindness) Temple Pagoda is located on a small hillside in Baita Community, Hebao Town, Rongchang County; locals call it the White Pagoda.

Driving to the foot of the hill, leaving the highway, and winding up along a stone-step path, one comes to a stone-paved flat ground on the hilltop, where the pagoda is located.

Bao'en Temple Pagoda was built in the 2nd year of Shaoxing (1132), Southern Song; its location was originally Bao'en Temple.

At the end of Ming and beginning of Qing, Bao'en Temple was destroyed by fire, and only this stone pagoda survived.

The pagoda is an eight-story square hollow pavilion style, facing north, with a total height of 16m.

The pagoda base is a plain double-layer square, 5.2m per side and 1m high, already湮没 by dense weeds.

The pagoda body tapers inward from bottom to top layer by layer; each layer either opens windows on four sides or has oval Buddhist niches; a few niches have remnant Buddha statues, but their faces have long been weathered beyond recognition.

At the four corners of the bottom layer there are coiled-dragon column reliefs, with scales, whiskers, and manes still recognizable.

Under the eaves of each layer there are several one-bucket-three-capital bracket sets, and relief dragon-phoenix spandrel brackets (queti), with unique modeling; although there is local weathering, the charm remains.

Between columns and lintels, mortise-and-tenon structures can be faintly seen.

Each layer of the pagoda body is carved with scriptures.

According to records, inside the pagoda there is a square hollow column running straight through to the top layer, with stone steps spiraling around it; people can climb along the stone steps to the seventh layer.

However, today the door on the front of the first layer has been sealed with stone slabs, so one cannot fully enjoy the pleasure of climbing.

Although the eave parts of the entire pagoda body have many defects (the higher up, the more severe the damage; the pagoda finial has been completely destroyed), it uses stone construction to present to later generations the unique Southern Song timber construction methods such as one-bucket-three-capital and dragon-phoenix spandrel brackets, and can be called an architectural specimen of Southern Song stone pagodas.

Bao'en Temple Pagoda has experienced over 800 years of vicissitudes; today it only accompanies the mountains, plants, and trees, and befriends white clouds and flying birds.

Even though the scriptures are blurred and the Buddha statues are damaged, it has its own Chan (Zen) meaning, hard to put into words; one can only get a hint by approaching it and savoring it carefully.

宝城寺

Baocheng Temple
市级 明—清 宗教建筑
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty明—清
地址 Address荣昌县昌元街道宝城寺村
类型 Type宗教建筑
看点 Highlights: 明代藏经楼

中文描述 Description

宝城寺隐藏在荣昌县昌元街上的一个党校内，找到它时里面正在进行维修，我们有幸提前一睹现状。

进去后发现满地的碎石，一片混乱，以至于让人几乎无暇去关注它原本的格局。

宝城寺始建于南宋绍兴年间，传统四合院布局，但朝向却是坐西南朝东北。

现仅存明代藏经楼一座，以及清代前殿、后殿和右厢房，占地面积约2500平方米。

藏经楼保存得很完整，看起来定是经过多次修缮了。

一楼一底，共2层，高9.6米，四周有回廊。

台基为须弥座样式，前部3级台阶。

面阔五间，进深五间，抬梁式梁架。

檐下有如意大斗拱4攒。

重檐歇山式屋顶，翼角起翘明显。

内外柱子柱础均为覆盆式。

沿楼后方有一木制旋转楼梯可登至二层，楼内结构完整。

相比之下，寺内其他部分的状况就凄惨多了。

后殿原为悬山式，六架椽屋，面阔五间，有前廊。

如今前廊尚在，殿前柱子和柱础也还完好，但其余部分已经过较大改造。

右厢房仅留存有抬梁式木构架，屋顶已不见。

前殿为一硬山顶式建筑，内部为穹形天花顶，可见部分梁架结构上用了天然弯木，看上去倒有几分趣味。

整体结构虽有些破损，但尚可辨认。

希望这残破光景能在这次修复中得到改善。

但这样的修复到底能还原多少真实，又会虚构出多少历史，我们不得而知。

英文翻译 English Translation

Baocheng Temple is hidden inside a party school on Changyuan Street, Rongchang County; when we found it, repairs were underway inside, and we were fortunate to get a glimpse of its current state in advance.

After entering, we found碎石 all over the ground, a scene of chaos, so much so that people almost had no time to pay attention to its original layout.

Baocheng Temple was first built during the Southern Song Shaoxing era, with a traditional siheyuan layout, but its orientation is facing northeast from the southwest.

Now only one Ming dynasty Scripture Depository Tower remains, as well as the Qing front hall, rear hall, and right wing room, covering an area of about 2,500 sq m.

The Scripture Depository Tower is very well preserved and must have been repaired many times.

One floor plus one mezzanine, totaling 2 stories, 9.6m high, with surrounding corridors.

The platform base is in the xumizuo (Sumeru pedestal) style, with 3 steps at the front.

It is 5 bays wide and 5 bays deep, with a beam-lifting frame.

Under the eave there are 4 clusters of ruyi (wishful) large bracket sets.

It has a double-eave xieshan-style roof, with obvious upturned wing corners.

The column bases of both inner and outer columns are of the inverted-basin style.

Behind the tower there is a wooden spiral staircase that can climb to the second floor; the structure inside the tower is complete.

In comparison, the condition of other parts of the temple is much more miserable.

The rear hall was originally of overhanging-gable style, with six rafter bays, 5 bays wide, and a front porch.

Today the front porch still exists, and the columns and column bases in front of the hall are also intact, but the rest has been greatly modified.

The right wing room only retains the beam-lifting timber frame, and the roof is gone.

The front hall is a flush-gable-roof building, with a domed ceiling inside; visible parts of the beam frame structure use naturally curved timber, which looks somewhat interesting.

Although the overall structure is somewhat damaged, it can still be辨认.

It is hoped that this dilapidated scene can be improved in this restoration.

But how much truth such a restoration can restore, and how much history it will fabricate, we do not know.

彭氏民居（彭瑞川庄园）

Dwelling of Peng Family (Peng Ruichuan Manor)
市级 清 民居
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address巴南区南泉镇白鹤林村南500米
类型 Type民居
看点 Highlights: 院落 雕刻

中文描述 Description

我们都知道山西的乔家大院，其实，在重庆巴南的南泉街道白鹤村，也有一处传统的民居建筑群，被称作彭家大院，这便是彭氏民居，或称彭瑞川庄园。

彭氏民居始建于清道光二年(1822年)，道光十年(1830年)竣工。

民居前有花溪河，后靠樵坪山，符合传统风水理论的选址特征。

整个大院占地面积5320平方米，建筑面积约3860平方米。

民居采用传统多重合院布局，中轴线上依次排列前厅、过厅、上厅，院内存天井12个，大小房间77间。

整个建筑群采用小青瓦屋顶，地面青石板铺就，四周环绕5～7米高的砖石围墙与封火墙维护。

此处建筑规模较大，形制完整，保存良好，是重要的民居建筑样本。

彭氏祖籍江西，清初迁往四川，宗系内曾出过礼部尚书等高官。

彭瑞川生活在清末，善于经商，资产丰厚，于道光二年(1822年)选址白鹤林，建造彭家大院。

后因世事变迁，家道中落，彭氏一族也不再聚居于此。

彭氏家族没落后，彭氏民居因其规模与气势而成为众多政府机构的驻所，如国民党中央政治大学研究部，中共南方局所创立的西南学院，以及新中国成立后的西南革命大学等。

此后多年，此处一直被用作学校，直至2002年，彭氏民居划归重庆市巴南区文物保护管理所管理，才得到更多关注，近年来也成为多部影视作品的拍摄地。

英文翻译 English Translation

We all know the Qiao Family Compound in Shanxi; in fact, in Baihe Village, Nanquan Subdistrict, Banan District, Chongqing, there is also a traditional residential building complex, called the Peng Family Compound — this is the Peng Family Dwelling, or Peng Ruichuan Manor.

The Peng Family Dwelling was first built in the 2nd year of Daoguang (1822), Qing, and completed in the 10th year of Daoguang (1830).

In front of the dwelling there is the Huaxi River, and behind it leans Qiaoping Mountain, conforming to the site-selection characteristics of traditional fengshui theory.

The entire compound covers an area of 5,320 sq m, with a building area of about 3,860 sq m.

The dwelling adopts a traditional multiple-courtyard layout; on the central axis are sequentially arranged the front hall, passage hall, and upper hall; within the courtyard there are 12 courtyards (tianjing) and 77 rooms large and small.

The entire building complex uses small grey-tile roofs, with floors paved with bluestone slabs, surrounded by 5-7m-high brick-stone enclosure walls and fire-sealing walls for protection.

The buildings here are large in scale, complete in form, and well preserved, being an important sample of residential architecture.

The Peng family ancestral home was Jiangxi; they moved to Sichuan in the early Qing, and within the clan there once were high officials such as the Minister of Rites.

Peng Ruichuan lived in the late Qing, was good at business, with abundant assets; in the 2nd year of Daoguang (1822), he selected the site at Baihelin and built the Peng Family Compound.

Later, due to changes in the world, the family fortunes declined, and the Peng clan no longer lived together here.

After the Peng family declined, the Peng Family Dwelling, due to its scale and momentum, became the residence of many government institutions, such as the Research Department of the Central Political University of the Kuomintang, the Southwest Academy founded by the Southern Bureau of the Communist Party of China, and the Southwest Revolutionary University after the founding of New China, etc.

For many years thereafter, this place was continuously used as a school; until 2002, when the Peng Family Dwelling was transferred to the management of the Cultural Relics Protection and Management Office of Banan District, Chongqing, it received more attention, and in recent years it has also become a filming location for many film and television works.

江公享堂

Former Residence of Jiang
市级 明 民居
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty明
地址 Address江津区几江街道办事处石狮子街
类型 Type民居
看点 Highlights: 院落 楹联 撑弓

中文描述 Description

江公享堂始建于明成化年间，位于江津区中心，3路公共汽车直达。

江公享堂是江津人明代辅相江渊的府第。

建筑合院布局，坐南朝北，面阔21米，通进47米，大门竖匾江公享堂，大门两侧有楹联北极勋臣府，西川相国家，是明成化帝朱见深为褒奖江渊功劳钦题。

清末一场大火将江公享堂的建筑损毁殆尽，如今院内只有青石地面为明代遗物，其余都是近年重建。

现有建筑为砖木石结构，悬山式屋顶，部分构件上刻有仿明代风格的浮雕。

如今的江公享堂开放作为老年活动中心，内部时常举办社区活动，颇受附近居民欢迎。

英文翻译 English Translation

Jiang Gong Xiangtang (Jiang's Memorial Hall) was first built during the Ming Chenghua era, located in the center of Jiangjin District, directly reachable by Bus Route 3.

Jiang Gong Xiangtang was the mansion of Jiang Yuan, a Ming dynasty auxiliary prime minister from Jiangjin.

The building has a courtyard layout, facing north from the south, 21m wide and 47m deep.

The main gate has a vertical plaque reading Jiang Gong Xiangtang; on both sides of the main gate there is a couplet: Mansion of the Meritorious Minister of the North Pole, Home of the Prime Minister of Western Sichuan — personally inscribed by Emperor Chenghua Zhu Jianshen of Ming to reward Jiang Yuan's merits.

A great fire at the end of Qing destroyed the buildings of Jiang Gong Xiangtang completely; today only the bluestone floor inside the courtyard is a Ming relic, and the rest were rebuilt in recent years.

The existing buildings are of brick-timber-stone structure, with overhanging-gable roofs; some components are carved with reliefs imitating Ming style.

Today's Jiang Gong Xiangtang is open as a senior activity center; community activities are often held inside, quite popular with nearby residents.

石门大佛寺摩崖石刻

Cliffside Statues of Dafo Temple in Shimen
国家级 宋 宗教建筑、摩崖石刻
级别 Level国家级
年代 Dynasty宋
地址 Address江津区石门镇白坪村(原凉亭村)东100米处
类型 Type宗教建筑、摩崖石刻
看点 Highlights: 造像 摩崖题刻 楼阁

中文描述 Description

石门大佛寺是一处以佛教水月观音造像为主体的古寺院，由宋代开凿的观世音造像、寺院建筑等构成。

观世音坐像依山崖凿出，通高13.5米，为我国现存最大的以观音为供奉主尊的石造像。

造像容貌端庄，服袖精美，辅以贴金彩绘，风格独特。

寺院坐北向南，由月台、寺门、像阁与左右厢房等组成，主体建筑为覆盖观音造像的木结构像阁。

像阁坐北面南，七重飞檐，逐层缩进，角檐飞挑，极为生动。

像阁规模宏大，气势高昂，正面面对万里长江，气宇轩昂。

像阁大约始建于宋，历代修葺，现存建筑经过近年整修，展现出清初建筑风格特征。

除此而外，寺内存有清同治八年(1869年)重修大佛寺碑一通，以及摩崖题刻若干。

石门大佛寺造像尺度宏大，雕刻精美，像阁建筑保存完整，与山势佛像相互协调，是展现中国传统佛教造像与像阁建筑相互关系的重要范例。

英文翻译 English Translation

Shimen Dafo (Great Buddha) Temple is an ancient temple complex with the Buddhist Water-Moon Guanyin statue as the main subject, composed of the Guanyin statue chiseled in Song dynasty, temple buildings, etc.

The seated Guanyin statue was chiseled against the cliff, with a total height of 13.5m, being the largest existing stone statue in China with Guanyin as the main enshrined deity.

The statue has a dignified appearance and exquisite sleeves, supplemented by gilded paintings, with a unique style.

The temple faces south, composed of the moon platform, temple gate, statue pavilion, and left and right wing rooms, etc.; the main building is the timber-structure statue pavilion covering the Guanyin statue.

The statue pavilion faces south, with seven layers of flying eaves, tapering inward layer by layer, with corner eaves flying outward, extremely vivid.

The statue pavilion is large in scale and high in momentum, facing the Ten-Thousand-Li Yangtze River on the front, with an imposing bearing.

The statue pavilion was approximately first built in Song, repaired through dynasties; the existing building has been renovated in recent years, showing the architectural style characteristics of the early Qing.

In addition, inside the temple there is one stele of Rebuilding Dafo Temple from the 8th year of Tongzhi (1869), Qing, as well as several cliffside inscriptions.

The statues of Shimen Dafo Temple are grand in scale and exquisitely carved; the statue pavilion building is completely preserved, coordinating with the mountain terrain and the Buddha statue, being an important example showing the relationship between traditional Chinese Buddhist statues and statue-pavilion architecture.

利济桥

Liji Bridge
市级 清 桥梁
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty清
地址 Address重庆市江津区朱杨镇境内板桥场
类型 Type桥梁
看点 Highlights: 五孔石拱桥，神仙石

中文描述 Description

利济桥又名万古桥，当地人称其板桥。

清朝乾隆末年(1765年)，乡人筹资修建，清道光六年(1826年)竣工落成。

此桥为五孔石拱桥，横跨溶溪河上。

桥长84米，宽8.8米，高13.2米。

两侧石栏有各种图案花纹，桥面中部镶嵌着传说中的神仙石。

当年乡民集资建桥，到了铺砌最后一块桥面石的时候，却找不到合适的石头。

此时，一个貌似乞丐的人开口对面一位老大娘家的坝子里有合适的石头，大家顺道寻去，果然找到合适的石块。

正要抬走时，老大娘说这是当年所收留的乞丐打造的，他说需要留下二两银子才能搬走石块。

于是乡民们买下了石块，也算是对大娘善行的报答。

大桥终于凭此石块得以完工。

利济桥两桥头，原有两座石牌坊，一侧还有一座文昌庙，可惜这些建筑在文革中均已损毁不存。

英文翻译 English Translation

Liji Bridge, also called Wangu (Eternal) Bridge, is called Banqiao (Plank Bridge) by locals.

In the late Qianlong era of Qing (1765), villagers raised funds to build it, and it was completed in the 6th year of Daoguang (1826), Qing.

This bridge is a five-arch stone bridge, spanning the Rongxi River.

The bridge is 84m long, 8.8m wide, and 13.2m high.

The stone railings on both sides have various patterns and designs; in the middle of the bridge deck is inlaid the legendary Immortal Stone.

When villagers raised funds to build the bridge that year, when it came to paving the last bridge-deck stone, they could not find a suitable stone.

At this moment, a person resembling a beggar spoke up, saying that there was a suitable stone in the courtyard of an old lady's home opposite; everyone went along the way to look, and indeed found a suitable stone block.

Just as they were about to carry it away, the old lady said this was made by a beggar she had taken in that year, and he said that two taels of silver needed to be left before the stone could be moved away.

So the villagers bought the stone block, which can also be regarded as a repayment for the old lady's good deeds.

The bridge was finally completed thanks to this stone block.

At both ends of Liji Bridge, there were originally two stone archways, and on one side there was also a Wenchang (God of Literature) Temple; unfortunately, these buildings were all destroyed and no longer exist during the Cultural Revolution.

龙崖城

Longya Fortress
市级 南宋 堡垒
级别 Level市级
年代 Dynasty南宋
地址 Address南川区马嘴乡三泉镇马嘴村西3.5公里
类型 Type堡垒
看点 Highlights: 城门遗迹 远瞻

中文描述 Description

龙崖城遗址地处金佛山风景区北面马嘴山上，海拔约1784米，地势险峻，易守难攻，自古以来就是兵家必争之地。

南宋时期的龙崖城是宋军抗蒙的重要堡垒，几经征战，御蒙功绩几可与合川钓鱼城齐名。

遗址平面形似马颈，东西宽1.5公里，南北长2.5公里，总面积约3.75平方公里。

城内遗存有城门、石阶、水井、垛墩、射孔。

城门建造在两块突出的巨石之上，为石砌的圆形拱门，门楣上方的条石额上，刻着蟠龙岩3个大字。

城墙虽残存不多，但仍可看出其依势而建，高居山顶，气度非凡。

城内仍保留有10米见方天池一口，应为当年屯兵蓄水之用。

龙崖城虽已破败，但其险绝之处仍然展现建筑与自然相互结合的鬼斧神工之妙，硝烟已没入荒草之中，唯有石头与题刻仍然歌颂着历史。

英文翻译 English Translation

The Longya (Dragon Cliff) Fortress ruin is located on Mazui Mountain, north of the Jinfo Mountain Scenic Area, at an altitude of about 1,784m, with steep terrain, easy to defend and difficult to attack, and has been a contested military stronghold since ancient times.

Longya Fortress in the Southern Song period was an important stronghold for the Song army against the Mongols; after several battles, its merits in resisting the Mongols were almost as famous as Diaoyu Fortress in Hechuan.

The ruin plane resembles a horse neck, 1.5 km wide east-west and 2.5 km long north-south, with a total area of about 3.75 sq km.

Inside the city there remain city gates, stone steps, wells, merlon piers, and arrow slits.

The city gate was built on two protruding huge stones, as a stone-built circular arch gate; on the dressed-stone lintel above the gate opening are engraved the three large characters Panlong (Coiled Dragon) Rock.

Although little of the city wall remains, one can still see that it was built according to the terrain, perched high on the mountaintop, with extraordinary bearing.

Inside the city there still remains a Heavenly Pond about 10m square, which should have been used for storing water for the garrison in those days.

Although Longya Fortress has fallen into ruin, its precipitous places still show the miraculous craftsmanship of combining architecture with nature; the smoke of gunpowder has sunk into the weeds, and only stones and inscriptions still sing praises of history.

数据来源：《四川重庆古建筑地图》青锋等编著 | Source: Historical Architectural Map of Sichuan & Chongqing, edited by Qing Feng et al.
